title: 任天堂常规直面会及塞尔达40周年特别直面会将于下周举行
孙正义弟弟清仓、索尼12亿巨资接盘:《智龙迷城》开发商GungHo抱上新大腿
event_sentences: 提起GungHo，了解手游市场发展的读者可能都不陌生，GungHo 的前身是 1998 年成立的拍卖网站 ONSale，它是软银与 OnSale 的合资公司；2002 年才改名 GungHo Online Entertainment，转身做网络游戏，靠代理《仙境传说 RO》起家。
尤其是2012年初上线的《智龙迷城》，三消、RPG、扭蛋的融合玩法，使之成为全球第一个收入破10亿美元的手游，累计流水突破60亿美元，2013年，仅一款游戏就贡献了GungHo公司91%的收入。
凭借这个爆款，GungHo 在 2014 年前后市值超过一众传统主机大厂，还顺手收购了须田刚一的 Grasshopper Manufacture。
2025 年，持股约 8% 的激进投资机构 Strategic Capital 发起股东运动，点名要求罢免社长森下一喜，理由是GungHo 是”one-hit wonder”，而森下一喜的薪酬比任天堂CEO还高。
2026 年 1 月，森下一喜终于卸任社长兼 CEO，转任首席开发官兼董事长，CFO 酒井一夫接棒。
按照双方公告，这次合作将探索手游、主机、PC游戏的联合研发与运营，还会”利用 SME 集团的 IP 开发新游戏企划”。
2021 年 GungHo 把 Grasshopper 卖给网易，2024 年又把手里的 Acquire 卖给角川。
另一家大厂，任天堂，与DeNA从2016年就建立了合作关系，2024年的爆款《Pokemon TCG Pocket》，就有DeNA参与研发。
韩国 Krafton 2025 年以约 5.16 亿美元收购日本广告与动画巨头 ADK；腾讯旗下 Lightspeed Japan 由前卡普空名制作人伊津野英昭领衔，在东京、大阪招募老兵做原创 3A；沙特 PIF 则已持有任天堂、Nexon、NCSoft、Take-Two、Embracer 的股份，Sega 还与卡塔尔签了游戏人才合作备忘录。

title: 独立创业者疲惫！1人维护SteamDB出售，买家Nexus Mods同样创始人太累退出
event_sentences: GameLook报道/北京时间9月3日,全球最大游戏Mod平台Nexus Mods与第三方Steam数据库SteamDB同日发布声明,宣布Nexus Mods的母公司Chosen，完成对SteamDB的收购。
SteamDB创始人xPaw(Pavel Djundik)在告别信里,留下一句被外媒争相引用的话:”疫情之后、AI崛起,我们曾经爱过的那个互联网已经死了,我的热情也随之而去。
不过，Nexus Mods CEO、Chosen创始人Victor Folmann表示,SteamDB长期是”一人乐队”(one-man band)式运营,并入后将被配齐一支有资金的正式团队,补强基础设施、安全与可扩展性。
”但他同时承诺，不放广告、不设付费墙、不卖用户数据,而是探索”更轻量”的方式:与发行商的合作关系、集成、用户浏览SteamDB后购游戏的联盟链接,以及对开发者/发行商开放的API。
联合创始人Marlamin在Steam Direct上线前后因个人原因退出,此后几乎全部工作落到xPaw一人肩上。
截至2026年4月，Nexus Mods注册用户超过7300万、累计文件下载量超225亿次，覆盖游戏数超过4500款。
其官网slogan颇具侵略性:”We partner. We amplify. We conquer.”(我们合作、我们放大、我们征服)。
由AI整理的两家公司发展史
创始人Victor Folmann曾创办游戏教学平台GamerzClass,2022年被Metafy收购后转任Metafy COO,并做过Bumble Ventures、Dreamcraft Ventures的创投合伙人。
当然，这些目前仍是”探索中”的方向,而非上线即有的功能。

title: 8月抖音小游戏畅销榜Top 100：《灵画师》连冠、三七6款入榜
郭炜炜离职后，西山居《剑侠世界4:无限》10月公测：目标运营20年“终极收官之作”
event_sentences: 前段时间，西山居灵魂人物郭炜炜也宣布离职，给行业和玩家很大的意外。
但这其中，办公软件WPS的相关业务扮演了强力压舱石的角色，贡献了近7成营收。
官方财报指出，这主要是由于旗舰产品《剑网3》运营超16年后的自然流水回落，以及行业竞争加剧所致。
虽然今年上半年公测的《鹅鸭杀》手游成为了业绩惊喜，但对于以国风武侠立足的西山居而言，不仅需要休闲竞技爆款、同样也需要有新的优质新游戏来接力。
9月3日，西山居正式公布了《剑侠世界4：无限》的重磅世界观PV，并宣布游戏将于10月15日开启全平台公测。
从官方之前发布的游戏实机PV及官网介绍来看，本作也在技术突破与玩法继承上做足了文章。
在官方微信公众号发布的《10月15日公测致玩家书：收官之作，坚守这一个江湖！
虽然《剑网3》依然是西山居绝对的基石与基本盘，但对于面临游戏业务营收下滑、急需新血顶上的西山居而言，《剑侠世界4：无限》的到来无疑是一剂强心针。
10月15日全平台公测之后，市场与玩家自然会给出答案。

title: 网易投资胡牌了！CDPR前总监新游Steam全球畅销榜夺冠
event_sentences: 但收缩不等于颗粒无收，网易少数股权投资的发行商Kepler Interactive跑出了《光与影：33号远征队》这匹“2025年度游戏”大黑马，全资收购的草蜢工作室也交出了《罗密欧是个绝命侠》这款真正上线的成品。
随着游戏的上线，游戏首发数据表现良好，网易终于迎来了投资纯血欧美团队的第一次胡牌。
关键NPC可以被直接杀死，不会触发游戏结束，但是会永久关闭对应任务线、改变势力格局。
谈及这次合作，Konrad在投资官宣中表示： “网易提供的资金，是我们全力开足马力所缺的最后一块拼图，有了打造世界级3A游戏的资源，我们现在可以专注于最重要的事情：开发。
当时操刀这笔投资的前网易全球合作与投资总裁Simon Zhu，则这样解释投资逻辑： “能在一支全明星团队刚启程时就与他们合作，这样的机会极其难得，他们打造可持续、有创造力的工作室的长期愿景，与网易孵化有才华创作者的战略相契合。

title: 独游慷慨赴死！Steam一周720款新游，“躲过手游买量，逃不过Steam踩踏”
event_sentences: 但实际情况可能远比外界对于Steam的印象要残酷得多，当前Steam的新游产品数量正在飞速膨胀，最近国外机构ICO Partners的统计，上周Steam上线的新游数量已经达到了720款。
这意味着如果你是一位独游开发者，你在Steam上线自己游戏之时，必须考虑如何与同一天上线的其它100多款游戏竞争，玩家要怎么从这100多款新游戏中找到你？
而如今ICO Partners的数据同样指向了同样的结论，根据统计，上周刚刚上线Steam的720款游戏中，有530款游戏的评论数为0至9条，190款游戏的评论数为10条或以上。
进一步分析显示，95款游戏的评论数超过50条，62款游戏的评论数超过100条，10款游戏的评论数超过1000条。
V社此前早就公布过Steam用户一年平均只玩4款游戏，而玩家用户时长的85%都被上线超过一年的老游戏所占据。
根据营收散点图，2015年之后，Steam平台的游戏数量明显增加，但绝大部分的游戏收入都在100万美元以下。
排名前1%的游戏拿走了预估营收的84.5%，而绝大多数游戏几乎赚不到钱。
另一方面，Steam同样表现出了很强的收入极化现象，头部产品会拿走绝大部分营收，同时玩家还会花费更多时间在老产品上。
回到文章开头的问题，之所以很多游戏开发者将Steam视作“应许之地”，包括近两年也能听到很多从大厂离职的开发者选择在Steam上做独立游戏，主要有两方面因素。
一方面是手游市场经过多年充分竞争，早已是高度成熟的市场，再加上大量的存量手游产品，最终导致手游从研发到首发上线，再到长线运营，都已经形成了一整套成熟的商业化规则。
以中国手游市场为例，手游固然买量竞争激烈，但因为监管侧“版号总量调控”的原因，中国市场每个月新上线手游的数量其实就几十款。
然而2017年之后，由于Steam想进一步推行去中心化的数字游戏生态，并且进一步促进平台的内容增长，最终该机制被取消，开发者只要交钱就能直接上架Steam。
在没有外界审核从供给端进行约束以后，再叠加最近两年AI导致的开发提效，Steam上的游戏产品开始狂增，虽然其中也充斥着许多垃圾产品，但还是不可避免地出现了新品踩踏的情况。
除此之外，随着Steam逐渐完成PC平台游戏发行的垄断，以及PS、Xbox也开始取消实体盘推行数字游戏生态，如今大厂的3A级项目也有可能出现互相踩踏的情况。
比如今年11月上线的《GTA6》，就把一众其它游戏挤到了9月-10月的狭窄档期，GameLook此前统计过，9月份有超过10款大作上线。
今天上线网易投资、万代发行，前CDPR团队开发的《黎明行者之血》，取得开门红、拿下Steam全球畅销榜冠军，但这款游戏因为优化问题遭遇了一些质疑，有玩家就表示厂商是“因为惧怕GTA6临时调整档期，导致基本优化没做好就仓促上线”。
比如今年下半年就有好几个案例，包括Steam同时在线人数破37万的钓鱼+FPS游戏《渔力全开》；上线一个月就收获近1万条评论的寻找伪人+超市模拟经营游戏《Shift At Midnight》（午夜轮班）；以及今年独游最大爆款、2人开发爆卖2000万套的涂鸦躲猫猫游戏《MECCHA CHAMELEON》。
像前文提过的《午夜轮班》，这款游戏由澳洲开发者Bun Muen一人开发，Bun Muen最终选择与英国知名游戏发行商Kwalee合作，将发行工作交给了后者。
去年《幻兽帕鲁》开发商Pocketpair曾经宣布进军独立游戏发行业务，官方表示他们公布消息不到一周，就收到了400多封邮件、2000多条领英请求、以及150多个游戏项目提案。
独游开发者需要对于产品上线以后的竞争激烈程度需要有充足的认知，这意味着每位开发者都需要做好严格的项目管理，包括控制好项目成本和研发周期。

title: 跟叠纸祖龙一桌，她们做了款热度Top5女性向新游
event_sentences: 到了2026年，随着乐元素《他予回声》、祖龙《代号：神不言》相继首曝，百奥《夜幕之下》上线，众多AI乙游走到台前，大厂女性向产品的“缺货”情况有所缓解，独立女性向游戏的热潮似乎稍稍褪去。
程序狐狸是名校在读的直博研究员，主攻AI和人机交互方向，她进入团队较晚，去年《神缺席》发过一轮PV后，“我就被绝美的PV吸引了，然后直接‘boss直聘’去后台私信一书，问她们需不需要程序员，一书老师很善良地给了我尝试的机会。
NPC每天决定要去干什么，和人产生的关系，人生发展的轨迹，这些行为决策树都将通过一种AI算法来驱动。
“但我们用的并不是《斯坦福小镇》那样的大语言模型AI，我们也烧不起token，我们用的是一种......大语言模型还没有流行之前就已经存在的 AI，”狐狸尽量用普通人也能听懂的语言为我解释了游戏里的AI算法逻辑。
这就是我们游戏里用的AI。
需要特别强调的是，游戏的美术素材、文案、动画并没有任何AI参与。
目前，即便是算法里用到的AI，也和如今风靡的生成式AI并非同宗，而是更偏向行为树的方向。

title: 再次登顶畅销总榜，天美射击还在卷
event_sentences: 今天，《三角洲行动》（以下简称“三角洲”）的新赛季“群星”正式上线，毫不意外的，游戏马上又冲上了畅销榜TOP1。
所以，长弓溪谷2.0，在S11赛季正式上线了。
而且分工合作，每个玩家都有充分的参与感。
尽管目前正式服的爆破模式还没有正式上线，但我们还是可以推测出一些模式的信息。
按照测试服已有的专属地图“航天中转站”，“蓝水屋电站”以及“萨米尔庄园”，整体交火距离大多控制都在35米以内，更偏向巷战中的近中距离拉扯。
不过，从测试服此前的平衡调整里，还是能看出一些比较明显的方向：武器整体降温，而战术道具则得到了一轮加强。
值得一提的是，此前S11测试服还出现过一套名为“纵横巅峰赛”的新排位玩法。
不过截至目前，这套玩法还没有被官方明确列入“群星”赛季的上线内容，具体开放时间和规则仍需以正式服为准。
这其实很能说明三角洲或者说射击游戏上线两年后面对的挑战。
一张地图刚上线时，哪里有资源、哪里危险、怎么转点，都需要玩家重新学习。
对此，团队还说过一句在我看来比较准确的总结：关卡发布不是终点，而是面向玩家服务的开始。
从这个角度看，过去两年三角洲变化最大的地方，可能并不是内容越来越多，更在于团队越来越习惯把一个上线后的内容当做持续变化的东西。
三角洲刚上线时，烽火地带和全面战场已经足够建立三角洲的基本盘。

title: 测试号炒到2000块，上海大厂新MMO真让人上头
event_sentences: 《仙境传说3》（简称：RO3）国内首测刚开没多久，一些许久未见的人又再次相见了。
8月27日，RO3在国内开启了首次PC端技术测试，我幸运地拿到资格并参与了本次测试体验。
在参与这次测试前，我对该作的预期大概是一款有双端的手游，毕竟“双端”已经成为现代手游的标配。
无论是超过百人的公会战斗、多人副本，还是在更需要精细操作的时候，游戏的画质、特效都没有丝毫缩水，键鼠操作都是端游级别的水准。
后来，我才了解到RO3在立项之初便是以PC端游体验作为研发基底。
果然，随着测试开启，玩家圈很快就热了起来。
B站首日同时开播的主播超过120位，两天内相关视频就超过了200条。
连测试资格都成了稀缺品，闲鱼上有人把激活码挂到了接近2000元。
20多年过去，一个老MMO IP新作还能在首测时折腾出这么大的动静，情怀当然是最容易想到的解释。
所以RO3这次首测的第一波热度并不难理解。
这恰好也是我觉得RO3国服首测表现比较好的地方，即玩家对游戏的讨论没有一直停留在还原度上。
一位参与了首测的玩家表示：“想靠数值硬过基本不可能，主要还是看配合。
比如，在这次测试中最让我惊喜的部分就是百人同屏的王城战斗。
测试里的“生存者之战”很快被玩家叫成了“RO版吃鸡”。
也正因此，RO3首测里那些看上去很普通的反馈，放在这里就有了点意思。
RO3首测很快就遇到了这种取舍。
就比如有玩家觉得固定时段活动太多，希望取消。
玩家希望游戏更自由，最好什么时候上线都不会错过东西。
玩家在一个世界里投入几百、几千个小时以后，积累下来的东西早就超过了副本、装备、战斗本身。
RO3首测如此热闹，前半段当然可归功于《仙境传说》的IP。
回看RO3测试，有人回来看一眼之后开始研究Build，有人为了副本找队友，也有人第一次玩RO，玩下来之后开始期待后续。
这意味着情怀带来的注意力，至少在RO3首测里没有仅仅停在情怀上。
鉴于游戏仍处在早期测试，商业化尚未确认，玩法、内容也会继续优化。
下一轮测试里，这些职业选择还能不能继续产生研究空间，副本是不是依旧值得组队，今天热闹的公会频道又能热闹多久，都需要继续看。
不过，至少有一件事已经比测试开始前清楚了。

title: 现场体验DLSS 5后，我觉得游戏美术要变天了
event_sentences: 几天前，NVIDIA正式发布DLSS 5，带来了3D引导神经 网络 渲染技术，将生成式AI技术进一步接入游戏实时渲染管线。
今年3月的GTC大会上，NVIDIA首次展示了DLSS 5的基本原理与效果。
也是从这一时期开始，NVIDIA逐渐明确，AI将成为迈入下一阶段的重要工具。
如今，诞生于AI、计算机图形学与实时渲染交汇处的DLSS 5，很可能成为一个新节点——引入生成式AI后，DLSS 5为照片级画面，找到了新的实现方式。
近年大热的生成式AI为这个问题提供了新的思路。
同时，NVIDIA还为DLSS 5设计了 语义AI遮罩 ，进一步限定模型的处理范围。
这个问题，如今已有答案——昨天，首款原生支持DLSS 5的游戏《NBA 2K27》上线，画面效果让不少玩家赞叹。
要知道，今年春季GTC首次展示时，DLSS 5需要两张RTX 5090才能运行。
最后葡萄君 自己也拿了一张RTX 5080进行了 《NBA 2K27》 实际测试，在 游戏 开启 DLSS 5、光线追踪和最高画质后，RTX 5080 依然展现出了十分强悍的性能表现。
DLSS 5背后，生成式AI进一步改变了游戏运行时的图形管线。
所以，已经上线的旧游戏，同样存在 更新 适配的可能性。
发布于：北京市

title: 金铲铲五周年：还在为玩家制造”启动”的理由
event_sentences: 就在派对前几天，「自然之力」刚刚上线，作为最新的一个赛季，它的玩法仍在创新。
五年间它在产品玩法、玩家生态、IP价值三条线上一直持续升级，也不禁让我好奇，它究竟是如何不断突破自我，把每一次升级，都变成玩家再一次”启动”的理由。
围绕“自然之力”这一主题，赛季首次尝试了“峡谷野怪”大羁绊，把召唤师峡谷里的经典野怪搬上了棋盘，凑成了多达 10 个弈子的庞大垂直羁绊。
甚至“在哪块屏幕上玩”的边界，现在也被突破了。
产品升级的第一动力，始终来自对自身玩法边界的持续突破，而不是对已有文化的守成，也正是这份对设计的用心，无论你身处哪个赛季抱着怎样的心态，总能找到属于自己的启动理由。
于是，一条完整的循环慢慢形成：游戏里的“启动”，让玩家走到线下；线下的体验，又变成玩家愿意发布和分享的内容；这些内容重新回到线上，成为更多人认识和参与《金铲铲之战》的入口。
2026年2月”天选福星”模式的更新里，上线了【铲搭请响铃】活动，用语音匹配帮玩家遇见同频铲搭子，主打”春节开铲不孤单”，连奖励都用”铲搭子头像自选礼盒”这样的玩家话术命名。
今年5月，第一次与麦当劳的合作在腾讯总部园区的单店落地，主题叫”以铲换无限”，店内设了打卡装置、请到了兔娘等高人气coser与玩家互动、举办水友赛凭战绩换美食、自制铲子有机会换超大金铲铲或者铲铲钥匙扣配冰淇淋，收获了玩家的大量好评。
《金铲铲之战》选择不断突破自我，将产品升级转化为玩家可以参与创造的真实体验，并把突破的结果，转化为官方与玩家共同点燃的火花。

title: 预约突破千万，腾讯游戏要给「种田建屋」开辟新解法
event_sentences: 科隆游戏展开幕前一天，腾讯北极光工作室《粒粒的小人国》宣布开启二测「定格测试」招募，并登上腾讯游戏在科隆游戏展的展台，面向全球玩家展示，成为这场大展里一个难得柔软的“小”产品。
可以看出，相比半年前的首测，团队对产品究竟该怎么打出有记忆点的产品特色、服务哪类玩家，已经想得更加清楚。
从现场看到的Demo来看，整体美术画面和角色动画表现力的提升，是《粒粒的小人国》相比首测最直观的变化，但游戏内在玩法逻辑的进化或许更加关键。
这个循环没有压力，回流障碍也低，哪怕上线找个地方看看景都行。
大部分建造游戏是四方向、一个方块叠一个方块的模式，但我们的游戏是小人视角，更希望玩家是“摆放”而不是“建造”：物体按正常方式摆下去，还能自由旋转，这是要特意突破的特色。
走过首测，走向全球
Q：去年9月你们开启了预约，至今已经有快一年的时间了，期间还经历了首测，这一年来研发团队的心路历程是怎样的？
A： 实际上之前首测的版本还并不是我们的正式版本，还在开发的早期阶段。
像是在画面上，首测版本的性能优化也没深入做，但为了让测试玩家的设备能够运行，我们必须做一定妥协。
Q：除了画质提升之外，首测期间还有哪些玩家反馈让项目组印象深刻？
Q：在之前的测试中，玩家有没有玩出让你们觉得比较意外的玩法？
他几乎每天固定时间上线、去同一个地方演奏，越来越多玩家特意赶过去听，甚至有人想办法进入他所在的线路，只为不错过这场玩家自发形成的“小型音乐会”。
现在的玩家更知道自己想要什么，愿意为想要的坚持，比如为了在广场弹琴每天固定上线。
Q：选择科隆游戏展这个节点做全球宣发，甚至还规划了PlayStation等主机平台的上线，团队是如何看待生活模拟品类的出海机会的？

title: Xbox adds monthly cloud limits to Game Pass as it "continues to invest in its reliability and performance"
event_sentences: As laid out in a blog post , Game Pass Essential will be limited to five hours, Premium to ten hours, and Ultimate to fifteen hours per month.

After reaching these limits, subscribers may purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Xbox noted that "available hours, purchasing options, and cloud gaming features may vary by market."
Xbox anticipates that these limits will affect 4% of Game Pass subscribers and will provide additional pricing details at a later date.
The platform holder said it made the decision because "the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer."

"Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."

Xbox also announced that from November, players can access Xbox cloud gaming without a Game Pass subscription by purchasing cloud playtime hours and streaming eligible owned games on supported devices.
In July, Xbox began testing ad-supported game streaming , with ads shown before each session while core gameplay remains unchanged.
Xbox said the test is "designed to help give people more affordable ways to play on devices they already own."
These initiatives are part of CEO Asha Sharma's plan to focus on "efficiency and affordability alongside performance."

title: GTA 6 Netflix preview causes PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales to jump in the UK
event_sentences: PS5 Pro consoles are selling out nationwide , and retailers including Argos and Smyths Toys now only have base models available.

Despite a significant jump in the run-up to GTA 6's launch in November, alongside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in October, Newzoo's Ronan Patrick said that it expects to see "an uptick in the install base but nothing particularly massive."
"The PS5 in inflation-adjusted terms is 67% more expensive [than at launch], and Xbox is twice as expensive," said Patrick.

"It's important to remember that the lion's share of time is often spent on older titles, and the closest analogy we have to a hardware shock is during the 2020-2021 GPU shortage, and you didn't see engagement or revenue being taken off course. You basically saw a reallocation of spend into software."
The extended GTA 6 preview was Netflix's most-viewed title last week , reaching 31.1 million views in four days. On YouTube , the preview received 22 million views in one week.

title: Future imperfect: Five predictions for the next decade | Opinion
event_sentences: While not everyone is catastrophising, nobody seems to be outright rejecting the framing of "Crash 2.0" either. The spectre of the 1983 videogame crash looms large, though we can't read too much into its invocation in this particular moment. The industry does have an occasional flair for the dramatic and a habit of raising the spectre of desert pits full of E.T. cartridges at the first sign of market turbulence, after all.

Before talking about the future, in fact, let's talk briefly about the past. 1983 wasn't a downturn or a rebalancing; it was a near-collapse of industry revenues from over $3 billion in 1983 to a mere $100 million by 1985. Analysts justifiably wondered out loud whether video games themselves had been a passing fad that would now fade into obscurity.

We are not facing anything like that. This is cold comfort to anyone who has seen their job or company disappear, or watched their labour of love sink beneath the waves of discoverability on launch, but the industry's headline revenue numbers are fine. Even if Sony was still going to let us have physical copies of anything, we wouldn't be burying them in the desert. Games are a firmly established medium with a huge audience; at this point, wondering if there's any future for video games is no more sensible than asking if people will soon get over this whole listening-to-music fad.

Some of those factors are obvious and often discussed. The wild rise in the price of hardware components that are crucial to every gaming device shows no sign of easing off in the near term , forcing console price hikes and making PC upgrades almost prohibitively expensive. Development costs for games have skyrocketed, with budgets of over $100 million now routine, and $300–400 million budgets being relatively common at the high end of AAA. And then there's the concentration: more and more of the revenue and attention on every platform is being monopolised by a smaller and smaller set of gigantic games, the business models of which are often increasingly focused on extracting more revenue from existing players.
Marvel's Spider-Man 2 allegedly had a budget of around $300 million, according to documents leaked in 2023 | Image credit: Insomniac Games

But there are other factors at play here, too. It's no coincidence that the industry started to convulse with massive layoffs right around the time when interest rates – which had largely held close to zero since the 2008 financial crisis – shot upwards in 2022. Financing dried up across the board as investors reconsidered the risk profile of video game projects, and companies reeled in expensive speculative ventures they'd launched when money was practically free. The boom around generative AI delivered the coup de grace, sucking up any potential tech investment money for miles around, which was instead thrown at the very data centres that are making gaming hardware unaffordable.

Meanwhile, China has become a major force in game development and publishing; it's often still overlooked in the West, but you could argue that Sony's failed attempt to pivot to live service games was less about wanting the next Fortnite and more about wanting the next Genshin Impact. And alongside it all, there's the foundational malaise that's troubled the entire tech industry for the past decade – the failure of every attempt to introduce a new technology with the same transformational potential as smartphones in the late 2000s, or the internet a decade or so before that. Concepts like VR, AR, or the metaverse have largely failed to make a dent on the mass market.
Genshin Impact, developed by the Chinese studio MiHoYo, became a global hit after its release in 2020 | Image credit: MiHoYo/HoYoverse

Even within that tangled mess of probabilities, though, there are a few strands that look reasonably certain. Let's do a little light prognostication, and hope it all turns out more Hari Seldon than Madame Web .

Playable Worlds CEO (and MMORPG legend) Raph Koster cited some figures in the Edge article suggesting that inflation-adjusted budgets for games have risen from around $1 million in the mid-nineties to $10 million by 2005, and eventually to $100 million by 2015. By that growth rate, we'd expect to routinely see billion-dollar budgets at this point, but GTA 6's budget allegedly breaking through that ceiling is instead considered an eye-popping outlier. Budget inflation has slowed somewhat, largely because it's running into some mechanical limits – few companies can finance budgets at this scale, and even among those that can, the risk profile is unappealing. The idea that you could release a game that makes hundreds of millions of dollars and still lose money is enough to start putting a ceiling in place over all but the biggest, surest bets.

We have to acknowledge that there are market forces pushing in the opposite direction too, though. Few, if any, other games will ever justify a budget on the scale of GTA 6, but that game will establish player expectations nevertheless; on some level, every other game (but especially those in an adjacent genre or setting) will be compared to it for years to come. The arms races for graphical fidelity, environmental detail, or open world size don't disappear just because the budget numbers start getting unpalatable, and will continue to drive inflation at the very top end.
"Teams that can deliver polished-looking titles at budgets in the tens rather than hundreds of millions will be greatly in demand"

The slow-down of the hardware upgrade cycle that will be forced by the component pricing crisis will offer some breathing room here – lots of companies are going to put off tooling up for the next generation for several years past their original plans. Figuring out creative ways to do more with less (in terms of both finance and hardware) is already a hugely valuable skill in the industry, and this will only become more prominent; teams that can deliver polished-looking titles at budgets in the tens rather than hundreds of millions will be greatly in demand. Short-cuts will prove disappointing in the end; generative AI tools will likely become a fixture of very specific, ringfenced parts of development (notably on the programming side), but will do little to reduce team sizes or cut budgets, and in the short term might actually have the opposite effect.
AI will make its mark, but perhaps not where you expect

It's almost a certainty at this stage that the AI investment bubble – vastly over-inflated and driven on increasingly wild financial projections and impossible science fiction promises – is going to either pop or (hopefully) deflate in the coming months or years. Once we're through that turmoil, though, the foundational technology of generative AI will continue to exist, and much of it will be usable on consumer-grade hardware (which you'll even be able to buy at an affordable price again once the bubble is over). Once the desperate hope of a trillion-dollar IPO no longer rests on convincing the world that AI can do anything and everything, the more realistic set of things it can actually do will come into focus.
Roblox has already added some agentic AI creation tools | Image credit: Roblox

For the games business, AI's biggest impact won't be in development (where its uses will be quite limited), but in user generated content (UGC). The great barrier to UGC at present is that more powerful tools that can create more varied and interesting content tend to become exponentially harder to use, with a learning curve that's more and more offputting for ordinary users. AI tools that can interpret a user's natural language prompts to coordinate those tools and build levels, minigames, and other content are a natural and reasonably low-cost application for LLMs, and will spur a major boom in UGC-driven titles as adoption becomes more widespread.
"AI tools will spur a major boom in UGC-driven titles"

Existing titles like Roblox will have a platform advantage, but we'll see a glut of new UGC games emerging to try to carve out a slice of this market. The real difficulty will lie in solving discoverability and ecosystem issues; LLM-driven creation will democratise content creation on these platforms, but at the cost of making it increasingly difficult for any user's content to rise above the crowd. The real break-out titles of this kind will be those that take a different approach to UGC, stepping away from the "be your own game developer" concept and instead leaning into allowing players to create content aimed at customisation and personalisation of in-game appearances, experiences, and interactions.

The past few years of mass layoffs in western countries (especially North America) and extensive hiring in China have already shifted the industry's centre of gravity towards Asia to some degree, but the broader effects have been limited by the relatively closed nature of China's own market. The global importance of Chinese games (and Chinese investments) has grown, but the importance of the Chinese market itself – despite its scale – remains muted.

Don't overestimate the market's geographical shift, though. Whatever geopolitical and economic strife we may see in the coming years (let's conservatively predict "a lot"), the sheer market sizes of North America and Europe will remain dominant for the foreseeable future. The cachet of the United States as the world's cultural centre also won't be toppled easily. Companies will want to retain a foothold in the US, even if the cost of developing games there means the actual work is increasingly being done overseas. Consequently, we will end up in a situation where many of the industry's most high-profile creators are US-based, but few full-scale AAA development studios exist there any more.

In his Gamescom Dev keynote , Amir Satvat noted that 50–60% of the industry's revenue is going to just the top 20 games. I'd love to say that will become more fragmented and equitable, but it's hard to think of a scenario where that actually happens.
Gacha-style games, like Honkai Star Rail, are hard to leave behind | Image credit: HoYoverse

Gacha games are a straightforward example of this. How much of the repeat playing of gacha-style games is down to the fact that players have already invested a lot of time and money on their in-game accounts? Moving from a gacha game, where you've expended considerable resources on getting high-level characters and desirable customisations, to one where you're starting from zero creates an incredible level of friction that ordinary games have never had to overcome.

Now consider the boom in UGC I expect to arise from LLMs being integrated into creative tools, and ask yourself how hard it would be for a user to step away from a game which is filled not only with things that they bought, but things that they made (or at least, feel like they made). These kinds of mechanisms will concentrate attention and revenue in a shrinking pool of games that have locked players deep in their ecosystems.
Meccha Chameleon was a huge breakout hit this year, selling well over 15 million units | Image credit: lemorion_1224

That will create some false hopes – discoverability will be as tough as ever, and the median indie success will still look more like a well-executed genre title that pulls in predictable revenues from its niche market, rather than a runaway hit. Any kind of hopes, however, will help to attract investment to the sector, and big commercial successes will spur the logic of grassroots venture capital; in other words, invest relatively small amounts in lots of things on the hope that one of them will be the unicorn hit, earning mountains of money that more than make up for your losses elsewhere.

Those indie hits will also start being the prevailing winds of the industry's creative direction. We already see this to some extent, but major indie breakthroughs will increasingly set the patterns that will be followed by massive AAA titles a few years down the line. Hollywood has followed this playbook for years (expect lots of movies in years to come taking cues from Obsession or Backrooms), and games will follow suit, treating the indie scene as a creative incubator where risk is not only possible, but encouraged.
Five predictions. Drop a note in your calendar to check back in in five years' time and see how I did. If I've really missed the mark, I solemnly promise to watch all of Madame Web again in penance.

title: Nvidia acquires open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9bn
event_sentences: Nvidia has acquired the artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.

As BBC News reports, Nvidia will pay about $11.9 billion to Hugging Face investors and may offer up to $1 billion in stock-based incentives. Amazon, AMD, and Intel are also investors in the open-source AI platform.
Nvidia president and CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a blog post that Hugging Face will stay open-source, and developers will not have to use Nvidia technology.
Huang said the deal will help Nvidia grow and improve Hugging Face's infrastructure for developers and organisations globally.
Nvidia is the biggest contributor to Hugging Face, having released over 500 models and more than 250 open datasets.

"I am honoured that [Clément Delangue] came to me as he considered the next chapter of Hugging Face and believed Nvidia would be a great home for the company, its community and the future of open models," said Huang.

"To the millions of builders on Hugging Face: thank you for pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We can't wait to build the future together with you. Together, we will make AI more open, more capable and more accessible to people and institutions around the world."

title: Inside Tencent's long-term strategy: live service, AI tools, and evergreen titles
event_sentences: Many column inches have been spent questioning the wisdom of focusing on live-service. Sony gambled and lost , as did many other companies chasing the dream of steady recurring revenues, while firms like Capcom that stuck to the traditional path have emerged relatively unscathed .

Highguard was one of the more recent live-service casualties , a game that was reportedly backed by the Tencent subsidiary TiMi Studio Group . But Tencent itself is not shying away from the glittering promise that live service titles bring.
"I think our holy grail is live service, right?" says Yong-yi Zhu, VP and head of operations, strategy and compliance at Tencent Games.

"You look at Tencent's DNA, it's Honor of Kings, League of Legends, Valorant. They're games that build upon themselves, and it provides stability to the studio, it builds communities. And I think more and more games are about not just engaging people for a short period of time, it becomes a lifestyle."

A lot has changed since GamesIndustry.biz last spoke with Zhu just under a year ago . The UK studios Splash Damage and Bulkhead have gone independent, following similar moves from The Chinese Room and Secret Mode earlier in 2025. Zhu won't go into details on the separation, but says "for certain studios we feel like we can't help them amplify their game."
"There are certain situations where we acquire a studio and actually we have trouble integrating them"

Zhu is sanguine about not all of the company's many acquisitions working out. "There are certain situations where we acquire a studio and actually we have trouble integrating them because of market conditions or cultural differences," he says. "Not everything, at the end of the day, is going to be a slam dunk."

So what is the company strategy? Zhu says that evergreen titles are a key part of it – both single and multiplayer, with the former well-represented in the firm's mobile games portfolio – but ultimately "it's really about building sustainable communities long-term, having games that continue to engage with people." And while live service is the holy grail, it's not a singular focus. "It can be an IP that you build up," says Zhu. "This is not our game, but you look at Call of Duty: we consider that an evergreen IP, even though it's really one version after another."
Tencent owns Riot Games, maker of the perennially popular Valorant | Image credit: Riot Games

The ultimate aim is consistency: "You look at a lot of premium games: I think in the past, you've seen a lot of ups and downs with companies that launch a game and have to lay people off. I think more and more we're trying to bring stability, and you typically don't see Tencent doing the same thing."
The other key part of Tencent's strategy is investing in "really high quality talent," says Zhu, again emphasising that "it has to be synergistic between Tencent and the developer."

Zhu runs ops and strategy for Tencent's global games business, and has around 20 studios in his division. That includes Miniclip, Sumo Digital, Funcom, Fat Shark, Sharkmob, 10 Chambers, and Stunlock Studios in Europe, as well as Digital Extremes in North America and Grinding Gear Games in New Zealand.
The New Zealand-based studio Grinding Gear Games is behind Path of Exile | Image credit: Grinding Gear Games

His focus is "less about places we're about to go, and more about how we ensure these studios are successful in the launches that they're about to have." That includes making sure each receives appropriate support from the wider Tencent ecosystem on things like regional publishing, technical support, testing, backend services, or analysis: "Things like that where we provide expertise, because we've done it as Tencent in the domestic market, and now we're trying to translate that into the global market," says Zhu.
Games for Change report aims to ground parental gaming concerns in "evidence rather than fear"
Raising Good Gamers white paper offers roadmap to better support families playing video games

He gives the example of experts from across China and Europe coming to help out on Dune Awakening. "They'll just sit alongside the devs at Funcom and work with them to solve the issues. And then afterwards, if it's an ongoing issue, sometimes they'll stick around. And sometimes we even say, 'Look, if it works out, the person can go to the studio and be a permanent employee'."
Funcom released Dune Awakening on PC in 2025, and it will launch on consoles on September 22 | Image credit: Funcom

He clarifies that things like creative and artistic design are mostly left to individual studios, but Tencent might swoop in to help on issues that are common across studios, like particular issues with Unreal Engine, or help with publishing in certain regions like MENA or Southeast Asia.

Funcom saw a wave of redundancies last October, and the Funcom-owned studio The Outsiders, maker of Metal: Hellsinger, was closed . At the time, Funcom said that the aim was to "focus our internal resources on releasing new content, features, and enhancements" for Dune Awakening. So is Tencent's strategy to focus more on bigger, live-service titles rather than smaller projects?
Tencent, Xbox, Game Angels, Ansible and Flick to speak on Game Republic New Horizons investor stage
Games London also hosting a number of sessions and bringing a cohort of international investors to the show

"It really depends on the studio to be honest," says Zhu. He notes that Funcom had already been running the live-service title Conan Exiles for a long time when Tencent bought the studio. "So that's a part of their DNA. They design games to be live services, and we support them on that journey."
Conan Exiles was first released in 2018; Tencent bought Funcom in 2020 | Image credit: Funcom

Other studios in Tencent's portfolio, meanwhile, have tried live service, but it "didn't work out," and they have "now focused more on premium titles, because that's been their bread and butter. And for us, we really want to help build studios that are best in class in their craft, whatever that might be."
But how small is too small? Joe Brammer, CEO of Wardogs maker Bulkhead, told GamesIndustry.biz earlier this year that Tencent "wouldn't look at any game that was less than £50 million."

Zhu disagrees. "I think we look at games across all scales, to be honest. I think for us, it's more about where the studio is on its journey and what its end destination might be. Could we help them get bigger? Sometimes we feel like, hey, our expertise doesn't quite match, or maybe the cultures don't match, but I don't think there's anything that's stopping us from making smaller games. We do have small games in our portfolio."

He describes Larian Studios and From Software are "north stars" in terms of Tencent's studio investments (the company owns a minority stake in both), and that they have "built up games over time, and not all of those games have been very big, but all of those games have been purposeful and have continued to build on the audience, and have continued to help them build on their craft. I don't think it's necessarily true that we don't look at smaller games."

Last time we spoke , Zhu talked about spinning up some Chinese support teams, with the idea of tying Tencent's Western and Chinese arms together more closely. A year later, he says not as much progress has been made on this front as he would have liked, in part because of challenges working across different time zones. Instead, the focus has switched to trying to instill learnings from different studios across the group.

"For us, it's kind of how many people should we keep on staff and how many people should we then leverage from an outsource vendor? Sometimes it's like, 'Hey, we need high precision folks that are making very intricate things, and we would like them to all be in a certain location working together.' And that's kind of the prerogative of the studio head."

Location has proved a key factor in outsourcing, with some teams happy with distant partners, while others look for help in the same timezone. "And so we're looking across the globe at what the options are for our different studios. Sumo is potentially going to support our studios in Europe, because they're closer. But being in the UK, it's probably not the cheapest place to be. So you have trade-offs on these types of things."
The shift to AI

It was notable that this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live featured a large number of highly polished games from Chinese studios – which leads us to wonder whether we're seeing a power shift in the games industry from West to East.
"China in general really loves AI as a tool"

That better tooling includes "things like AI that can help people iterate more," says Zhu. "And AI for us is not about replacing people. It's about making people more effective and efficient across a number of different things. We have development teams that are a bit smaller, but they're like, hey, now we can make more content, we didn't want to be a big development team. We like our family feel of 30, 40 people, but now we're able to make higher quality things, and iterate more, and come up with cooler looking – whatever it is that they're designing."
"I think that's probably true of the Chinese developers, too, because they're kind of growing up in this age of leveraging tools," he says. "China in general really loves AI as a tool."

In the West, by contrast, developers tend to be more reluctant to use AI, with ethical concerns, copyright worries, and player backlash all front of mind. "I think people should just not be afraid of AI," says Zhu. "It's like the internet, it's coming. And I spent some time personally to figure out what is the best way to leverage AI in my daily life to make myself more efficient."
"I think people should just not be afraid of AI. It's like the internet, it's coming"
He thinks that development teams should be more "open to that way of thinking" and should consider AI as "a genuine tool."

He says that Tencent generally encourages developers to use AI, "because we think there's a lot of potential, but again, as a tool. I think on content generation, that's a very different conversation. I think that's probably further away. For development, it's more like we use this for concept art, we figure out what it's like, then we'll use AI tools for rigging, for motion matching, for code review. There's so many different things in the pipeline that [AI] can do. Even production management tools, they'll have AI bots in their Slack channel asking people for homework and things like that. So it can be used in a number of different ways that's not replacing humans, right?"

He acknowledges that there are still some difficulties to work through, not least when it comes to the copyright status of content produced via generative AI. "I do think that's something that the AI industry will have to figure out," he says. "Let's say the AI is only using our own libraries, right? That makes it very easy, because that's our IP, we've done it in the past, and they've remixed that content into something else. I think that's OK versus using something that's from a different content creator or just the general web. And we look at that very closely. We make sure that our data is confined to our studios."
The formerly Tencent-owned Bulkhead recently released Wardogs in Early Access | Image credit: Bulkhead/Team17

With the backing of its vast parent, Tencent Games is in a position to experiment, placing bets large and small on a wide variety of products and studios. While it's recently retreated from Bulkhead and Splash Damage, and redirected AAA studio Lightspeed , our conversation took place the day after it announced a minority investment in W4 , the commercial development partner of the Godot engine. It seems likely that come next Gamescom, Zhu will have some different projects to talk about. But the throughline is engagement, whether via live service or not.

title: Supercell's acquisition of Metacore expected to close this month
event_sentences: Once the deal is closed, Merge Mansion will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio.
Supercell, the company known for the likes of Clash Royale and Brawl Stars , has signed a deal to acquire Merge Mansion developer Metacore.

According to comments from Metacore in May, its restructure and resulting acquisition by Supercell aims to "better align with the core business, improve efficiency of operations, and respond to an increasingly competitive market environment." This comes at a time where Merge Mansion 's growth has "plateaued over the past few years" since its 2020 launch, as well when new investments have not succeeded in launching new games globally.
Related: Gamecity Hamburg launches second round of prototype funding
Once the deal is closed, Merge Mansion will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio. In the meantime, both companies are already working to plan the transition of the game.

"As we move into this next phase together with Supercell, I'm excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team and our players," Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski says in this week's announcement . "Supercell's expertise in operating and growing global live games over many years gives Merge Mansion the best possible foundation for long-term success."

The acquisition is just one part of what Metacore called "its next phase" back in May. At the time, uncertainty over Merge Mansion's future led to the company initiating change negotiations in Finland. According to information shared at the time, the studio would "consider reducing up to 160 roles" in the country if plans were to be realized.

Moreover, Metacore was also investigating "what kind of changes there could be" to operations in Germany and Sweden. None of these plans are mentioned in this most recent deal announcement. In addition, the terms of the transaction will not be disclosed.

"These are very difficult discussions," Tammenkoski said in the announcement back in May. "We have built an organization with growth ambitions that have not materialized as expected. The competition has become tougher every year since we launched Merge Mansion and created the 'merge 2' category as a pioneer. We need to make changes to remain competitive and to give Merge Mansion the best possible chance to succeed going forward."
Related: CD Projekt Red won't be abandoning physical releases

Supercell, which sits under the Tencent umbrella, has spent the last couple of years buying majority stakes in and acquiring studios . In 2022, Supercell also ended development on two of its projects: Clash Quest and Everdale .
In April, the studio CEO and co-founder received a BAFTA Fellowship award in recognition of his long-standing contribution to the video game industry.

title: Xbox to cap Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers
event_sentences: Microsoft is rolling out new monthly limits on its Cloud Gaming service that will cap the number of hours that Game Pass subscribers can spend streaming games via cloud game technology. The restrictions—announced today via Xbox Wire —will levy stronger restrictions on users paying for cheaper versions of Xbox Game Pass.

"Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."

While Microsoft acknowledges that the new caps may create a "higher cost" for some players, it's also making something of an affordability pitch for existing Xbox One owners who still haven't purchased an Xbox Series X|S. The company is making these playtime hour purchases available to Xbox users who don't have a Game Pass subscription.

"This will provide another option for people who want occasional access to cloud gaming or do not want a recurring Game Pass subscription," the company explained. "Cloud gaming can also give XBOX One owners access to eligible games built for XBOX Series X|S without requiring an immediate hardware upgrade."

If this pitch sounds familiar, it's because reducing the price of Xbox services has been a major talking point for Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in interviews conducted in the wake of laying off 1,600 employees (with another 1,600 still at risk of being let go). She's explained that Microsoft needs to improve the affordability of its devices and services in the face of increasing hardware and memory costs. Said costs began to increase after the Trump administration imposed tariffs on foreign-produced goods and generative AI firms like OpenAI struck exclusive deals for to purchase years of memory chips used in console devices (Microsoft is a major financial partner of OpenAI).

There is one other target market for Xbox's new Cloud Gaming playtime hour purchase system: those who haven't been able to purchase an Xbox because the devices are "unavailable or unaffordable" in their region. If players can't afford an Xbox because currency rates elevate the device's price in their region, perhaps a few hours of playing Gears of War: E-Day will do.

title: Strategically making Star Wars Zero Company, ft. Greg Foertsch
event_sentences: Bit Reactor CEO and Star Wars Zero Company creative director Greg Foertsch discusses the development of the latest adventure from the world of Star Wars.

Editor's note: this interview was recorded before it was confirmed that Bit Reactor furloughed approximately 80 percent of employees in advance of the launch of Star Wars: Zero Company. For more information, you can read our coverage of the topic or review the original reporting on Game File .

Star Wars Zero Company has finally launched, and it's already become a massive hit with fans of Star Wars and turn-based tactical games alike. The games from studio Bit Reactor, which was founded by many former employees of Firaxis who worked on games like XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2 .

One of those employees is CEO, co-founder, and creative director Greg Foertsch, who joins us on this week's episode of the Game Developer Podcast to discuss his passion for well-crafted in-game cameras, his perspective on inviting as many team members as possible into the game development process, and his love for the Star Wars character Huyang.

title: New game digest: Saints Row: The Third, Overwatch Rush, Palworld Online, Bleach, Colony and more
event_sentences: Here every Friday you’ll find the latest global releases, game dates, new soft launches and everything in between.
Saints Row: The Third Remastered (Feral)
Blizzard’s made-for-mobile hero shooter has entered soft launch in the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia. It’s coming to both Android and iOS.
Palworld Online (Garena)

This MMORPG, built under license from Pocketpair, brings Palworld’s creature-collecting survival gameplay into a shared online world. Pre-registration is open now in South Korea on Android and iOS, with a global release planned for later in 2026.
Bleach Mirrors High (Bandai Namco)

Bleach Mirrors High is an officially licensed team battler-RPG made in collaboration with series creator Tite Kubo. It’s currently listed for pre-order on iOS and Android, with a launch expected later this year.
Colony (Parallel Studios)
Colony is a 4X survival game built around AI-driven agentic characters and real-time 3D item generation. It’s live on iOS and Android now following a “silent launch,” with a marketing push to come.
As we reported previously, Google has tipped the game as one to watch as the AI-driven games category develops.

title: 触乐怪话：播客初体验
在电影和电视剧里讲游戏故事，这家公司是专业的
event_sentences: 《刺猬索尼克》在制作期间遭遇了一些挫折，比如当首支预告片发布后，索尼克的形象引起众多玩家抨击，制作团队不得不迅速重新设计……不过2020年初，尽管疫情导致《刺猬索尼克》的院线放映提前结束，这部电影仍然斩获3.2亿美元的全球票房，票房收入远远超过了制作和营销成本（约9000万美元）。
从那以后，Story Kitchen招募了伊莲娜·桑多瓦尔（Elena Sandoval）、蒂莫西·I·史蒂文森（Timothy I. Stevenson）和达拉斯·狄金森（Dalls Dickinson）等业内资深人士担任高管，还先后在2022年2月和2024年5月，与亚马逊和梦工厂动画公司签署了优先合作协议。
这个数字听起来似乎很夸张，在电子游戏的汪洋里却犹如沧海一粟……那么，Story Kitchen为什么不直接带着一份写满游戏名称的清单去拜访电影制片厂、电视台和流媒体平台，以这种遍地撒网的方式谈合作呢？
“当我们向潜在合作方推荐IP时，根本不想谈论‘这款游戏卖了多少份？
在与潜在合作方的沟通中，我们更倾向于解释为什么游戏里的故事和角色精彩绝伦，或者它具备哪些人们从未见过的亮点。
他们非常清楚，我们并非为了捞钱与他们谈合作，而是真心希望打造出高质量的游戏改编作品。
按照约翰逊的说法，在Netflix动画剧集《古墓丽影》制作期间，Story Kitchen与游戏工作室水晶动力（Crystal Dynamics）建立了良好的合作关系。
“作为合作伙伴，我们希望在未来再次携手，并为此制定了非常清晰的计划。
双人合作冒险游戏《双影奇境》将被改编成一部真人电影
我们和Hazelight以及其他合作伙伴的沟通都非常顺畅。
目前，这家公司正在筹备3款Roblox游戏《种植花园》《Steal a Brainrot》和《Jailbreak》的电影改编项目，并与环球影业合作，为《正当防卫》《忍》和《Ruiner》制作真人电影。
“我们正在为一款尚未公布的游戏筹备剧集，并即将向潜在合作方介绍相关方案。
约翰森补充，早在《光与影：33号远征队》发售前，Story Kitchen就与这款回合制角色扮演游戏的法国研发工作室Sandafall达成了合作。
“事实上，我们从2023年就开始与Sandfall合作了。
经过一番努力，我们与《漂泊者》的开发团队建立联系，并在与另一家制片公司的首次谈判中就达成合作意向，对方同意将这款游戏改编成一部真人电影。

原文标题：《'That's our next mission — proving that games are art': meet Story Kitchen, the bold, trail-blazing studio behind the popular Sonic movies that wants to turn your favorite game into the next movie or TV hit》

title: 《致命躯壳2》：魂Like红海的另类解？
event_sentences: 在游戏行业打拼多年，厌倦了扮演 3A 流水线上的螺丝钉，决定出门单干 —— 这是许多我们耳熟能详的 “ 行业老兵离职创业做独立游戏 ” 故事的开头 —— 《致命躯壳》系列背后的开发商 Cold Symmetry 也不例外；不过，和那些 “ 所有职位人手齐备再行动 ” 的 “ 布莱梅乐队 ” 故事不同， Cold Symmetry 的创始团队，可以说从一开始就把 “ 偏科 ” 写在了脸上：

业内知名 3D 数字怪物创作者，在过去超过 20 年的时间中，曾参与项目包括《辐射 3 》《地铁：最后的曙光》《教团： 1886 》以及《光环：士官长合集》知名 3A 大作系列，主要负责角色与怪兽模型制作；成立 Cold Symmetry 工作室之前，曾经在 Sucker Punch 认知资深角色设计师， TGA 2020  最佳艺术指导奖得主《对马岛之魂》，即出自这位的手笔。

title: Crimson Desert Channels The Sims With Its Chartering The Unknown Expansion
event_sentences: Revealed during today’s State of Play presentation , Pearl Abyss has confirmed that Crimson Desert ’s first major expansion will be launching in October. It not only adds a new region and plenty of new narrative surprises, but also gameplay features that pull from the most unlikely of places. If the reveal trailer is any indication, Crimson Desert could soon be a life sim that gives The Sims a run for its money.

Other unexpected additions coming to the paid expansion include Assassin’s Creed -esque naval combat, giant underwater dragons, and a new narrative threat that seemingly revolves around an unexplored location far beyond the Crimson Desert. Players can likely expect a new region dominated by a huge body of water, and a city in which abused workers are beginning to rebel against their leaders. Nothing about it makes sense, but players have come to expect that from Crimson Desert by now.

But one of the most exciting things coming to the game as part of Charting the Unknown is the ability to construct your own buildings and fill them with whatever you like. The trailer is focused primarily on erecting what appears to be a massive castle outside the city, showcasing its evolution from a foundation in the ground to a formidable stone fortress. There is even plenty of scaffolding, which gives off the impression you will be able to climb buildings while they’re being constructed or perhaps help out with the assembly yourself.

The trailer then transitions to the interior of a completely different building, where the player is using an interface to place walls just like you would in The Sims or Paralives . This isn’t just an open-world action-adventure game anymore; it’s a borderline life sim where you can construct a series of rooms, place furniture, and, thanks to the forthcoming update, start up a romance with one of the game's numerous NPCs.

Towards the end of the trailer, we see protagonist Kliff Macduff getting on his knees and offering a lovely bouquet of flowers to an NPC, suggesting that more robust romance options could soon be coming to Crimson Desert. If you’re adding all the other ingredients of life sims, obviously it makes sense to let our hero fall in love and settle down.

It’s likely the expansion is hiding plenty of secrets we’ll have to wait until launch to discover. It also gives you the option to hire employees, each with different statistics and roles, so you might want someone with particular skills to run the castle kitchen or a smart-talking fella to act as your castle’s traveling merchant. The presence of attack and defense stats gives off the impression that there will also come a time to defend your castle from outside forces. It wouldn’t be surprising if the presence of a pirate ship also asks that players assemble their own crew, which could come from your castle, or vice versa.

The Chartering the Unknown expansion follows in the footsteps of countless free updates that have utterly transformed the ambitious open-world game since it arrived earlier this year, with the most recent patch adding several narrative-focused cutscenes to its once lightweight main story.

Crimson Desert has proven itself to be quite polarizing since its release, with critics arguing it does too much mechanically and far too little narratively. However, this throw everything at the wall attitude also makes it impossible to look away when an expansion like this comes around. Nobody expected it to suddenly transform into a life sim where you can make a castle and fall in love, yet here we are.

title: D&D’s World Of Warcraft Crossover May Not Be A One-Way Street
event_sentences: Dungeons & Dragons fans will soon be exploring the dangerous lands of Azeroth, as World of Warcraft is coming to the tabletop game . Wizards of the Coast (WotC) and Blizzard have gone all-out with this crossover, as not only does it feature multiple World of Warcraft classes and six additional subclasses, but also various specializations, spells, items, and enemies. That sounds like a dream pairing between two titans of the fantasy genre, but could we see Dungeons & Dragons make an appearance in World of Warcraft's digital realms?

WotC isn't saying anything official right now, but in an interview at Gen Con with GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell, Head of Dungeons & Dragons Dan Ayoub and VP of World of Warcraft for Blizzard Holly Longdale were certainly teasing something . "I cannot say at this time," Longdale said. "Not at this time. This is a grand experiment. I am really excited to see where it goes."

If a reciprocal crossover is in the pipeline, then it'll most likely be revealed at BlizzCon later this month . Blizzard's big event for all of its games typically kicks off with a grand-opening ceremony--this year's one will be on September 12--and dedicated panels will be held over the weekend for its games. That same day, World of Warcraft will be in the spotlight , as Blizzard will host a 45-minute "What's Next" panel for the game on the main stage, which does suggest some big news. On September 13, that panel will continue on the main stage as the development team previews upcoming adventures, features, and updates.

World of Warcraft might not be the only Blizzard franchise coming to Dungeons & Dragons, as Ayoub teased that StarCraft would also be a dream addition to the tabletop game. "I know a guy," Longdale said in response. While WotC continues to introduce new IP to Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons, Ayoub also stressed that the core games won't be sidelined in favor of Universes Beyond crossovers.

title: A Long-Dormant Blizzard Franchise Could Be Coming To Dungeons And Dragons
event_sentences: "I will say this, since I am sitting here with [World of Warcraft VP] Holly Longdale, who is super persuasive and has cool stuff: I think StarCraft would be badass," Ayoub said. "As I said earlier today, I quite literally almost flunked out of university because of StarCraft. That one gives me the feels."

Blizzard was not giving any more details on a potential StarCraft crossover and at this point, it’s not clear if it’s even officially in the works. However, their coy nature discussing it has us very intrigued.

title: Game Pass Is Getting Worse, And More Expensive
event_sentences: Microsoft has made a big announcement about one of the big perks of Xbox Game Pass, cloud streaming, and the news is not great.

Microsoft said it understands this is a "meaningful change," especially for those who use the cloud regularly for gaming. However, the company said it estimates that these changes will impact about 4% of Game Pass subscribers, though the company did not share any specifics on how it arrived at that projection.
A first look at the "cloud playtime remaining" UI on Xbox.
For people who want or need more monthly streaming hours, Microsoft will allow people to buy more--but pricing was not announced.

Additionally, Microsoft said that in November, for the first time, people will not need to have an Xbox Game Pass membership to stream games with the cloud. People outside of Game Pass will be able to buy cloud playtime through the Xbox Store, though, again, pricing was not shared. Microsoft said this option is meant to appeal to people who don't want to subscribe to a recurring membership like Game Pass and only want "occasional access."

"We’re introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer. Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost," Microsoft said. The company added that it will "listen closely" to player feedback and make adjustments if necessary.

Xbox's cloud gaming service runs on Azure servers , and the Azure business is booming. For the first time ever, Microsoft just revealed how much money it makes on Azure quarterly, and the latest numbers showed $29.4 billion in sales. As relayed by Reuters , that's behind Amazon's latest quarterly revenue for AWS of $42.2 billion but ahead of Google's $24.8 billion cloud business results.

title: The New Gundam Game Has A Collector’s Edition Just For Gunpla Sickos Like Me
event_sentences: Gundam Rogue Orbit is a break from tradition for Bandai Namco, as new entries in the franchise typically debut as an anime series first, then as a line of collectible model kits. But this Gundam is arriving first as a video game--one that was shown in more detail today during the September PlayStation State of Play broadcast . If you're a Gundam fan, fret not, because at least one part of the traditional Gundam experience is being kept intact if you buy the $160 Rogue Orbit collector's edition.

Like other special editions from Bandai Namco, Gundam Rogue Orbit combines a physical copy of the game with a few physical in-game goodies. It's the inclusion of a High-Grade model kit based on the new Gundam Helix mobile suit that could make this collector's edition sought after, as it will be exclusive to the game. Gundam model kits aren't usually hard to come by as Bandai Namco regularly keeps store shelves restocked with them, but the HG Helix model looks like a rare exception to that rule.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AiPllyLIvSo

If you are planning to grab one, it's worth noting that HG Gundam model kits are 1/144-scale figures and are designed to appeal to casual builders with their moderate detail, minimal foil stickers, and durable design. You won't need too many tools to build one either, and the Helix design features a lot of panels and other mechanical details, so that could be a nice kit to build. The new trailer for the game also teased other shells that you can apply to the Helix to shake up its look, including an RX-78-2 skin and a red Zaku-inspired look that would make Char Aznable proud.

Aside from the model, you'll also get a poster, reversible cover art, a pack of five promo cards, a steel case for the game disc, and DLC that includes 14 different color patterns for the Helix in the game. You won't have to wait too much longer to play it, as Gundam Rogue Orbit launches on March 5, 2027, for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

title: Something Is Brewing With StarCraft
event_sentences: The glitches were flagged on Bluesky by John Carson, and they specifically appear on the section of Blizzard's website advertising 2017's StarCraft Remastered, rather than StarCraft II. The glitches see certain images and text become briefly distorted, though to my eye, there is nothing specific to glean from them.

But this sudden marketing stunt feels noteworthy given that the StarCraft franchise has largely been dormant for years. 2026 has brought rumors that something is afoot: The publisher behind Arc Raiders was said to be working on a StarCraft shooter that would be revealed at BlizzCon . More recently, a report from The Chosun Daily claimed that Nexon was seeking the rights to develop a new RTS, possibly StarCraft III.

That anything is happening with StarCraft could come as welcome news to fans of the franchise. StarCraft II was released in three main components between 2010 and 2015, and other than the subsequent remaster of the original, no new games in the series have been released or even announced. As Blizzard's focus shifted to maintaining WoW and Diablo, as well as developing Overwatch, it wasn't terribly surprising to see its more niche real-time-strategy series fall by the wayside, but it was no less disappointing: The StarCraft games are among the best strategy games ever, and fans were already tortured through years of hoping the canceled StarCraft: Ghost spin-off would ever see the light of day.

StarCraft II did get a sizable update earlier this year, which might have been part of an effort to begin to revitalize interest in the franchise as Blizzard prepares to bring it back. Should that come solely in the form of the rumored shooter, that would come as a blow to those wanting to see Blizzard return to the strategy genre that it has otherwise abandoned (first with Warcraft, and then with StarCraft). Were that complemented by a new Nexon-developed RTS, it might soften the blow, though the lack of Blizzard's direct influence might undercut the excitement such an announcement would otherwise produce, but beggars can't be choosers, after all.

title: The Last of Us Season 3 Did Not Include Naughty Dog’s Involvement For Creative Choices
event_sentences: Writer-director Neil Druckmann dropped out of HBO's The Last of Us TV show to focus on Naughty Dog's gaming output, including Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. In a new interview, he said Season 3--which, again, he had no direct involvement in, will "wrap up" the series. He also revealed that, unlike Seasons 1 and 2, Naughty Dog "did not have a creative role in the direction" of Season 3.

Druckmann said this to The Washington Post , confirming, "I wasn't involved in shaping this season's creative direction," nor was Naughty Dog involved. "So I can't personally speak to how production is progressing," he said.

The Last of Us ending after Season 3 would be no surprise, as HBO management said that would likely happen . Druckmann was very closely involved in Seasons 1 and 2; he co-wrote some of the episodes and directed two.
Druckmann went on to say that Naughty Dog remains "the steward of this IP" and even though the HBO show might be coming to an end, he teased, "We're not done with The Last of Us."
This isn't the first time that Druckmann has teased future The Last of Us projects. Earlier this year, he said there are "a few stops that remain on the road ahead" for the series.
Troy Baker, meanwhile, who played Joel in the game series, said this year that, "I definitely know we've not seen the last of Joel."

title: GTA 6 Is Completely Changing How You Steal Cars
event_sentences: Carjacking in Grand Theft Auto games has been, as the title denotes, a staple of the series. Up until now, it's largely been the same. While there have been more details and animations added over the years, the premise has remained that you'll walk up to a car, press Y or Triangle, throw the driver out, get in and drive away. If the car was parked, you'd execute the same button press to smash the window and steal it. With GTA 6 , carjacking is getting a complete overhaul. Here, we've got all of the information we know so far on how to steal cars in GTA 6.

There are two ways to steal a car: taking one that's stationary, or taking one that someone's driving around in. However, there are more details that make GTA 6 feel more like true simulation gameplay now.

If you do want to get away cleanly, you need an item to disable the tracking device. It seems like that item, along with the slim jim, is not something you start out with, meaning you'll need to progress through the story or complete side objectives to obtain them.
Stealing cars isn't as straightforward as it used to be.

How do you know what kind of security a given car on the street has? The app Waink allows you to scan vehicles, and it'll tell you the security systems on board as well as how much it'll cost to register it as your own vehicle.

One other interesting detail about registered vehicles that was in one of TGG's videos is that if you ditch one of your own cars while you are wanted, the police will set up a perimeter around your car so that if you return to it, in theory, they will be waiting for you. If you wait too long, they will impound it. This leads to some interesting gameplay implications. Perhaps you'll have to sneak into the impound lot to retrieve it, or if you have the money, you could show up and pay the fee before driving off.

There's certainly something deeper going on with the Grand Theft Auto mechanics we've known for years. Supposedly, when you start the game you won't have access to a lot of these tools. You won't be able to instantly steal cars; you'll have to progress to that point. It seems like better vehicles will slowly be introduced throughout the game.

If you want better vehicles, you'll have to work for them, whether that's through stealing or more legitimate means. This also leads to interesting repercussions when it comes to robberies and other activities. You'll want a fast getaway car--previously, you could just acquire the nearest suitable one, but in GTA 6 you'll have to plan ahead. If a nearby car is parked, you might not have the equipment to stealthily steal it. Even if you do, maybe you don't have the gear to remove the tracker, which will bring more heat on you.

title: GTA 6 Online Could Struggle To Pull Players Away From GTA Online, Says Valve Veteran
event_sentences: What's the biggest question about Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Easily Rockstar's plans for GTA Online, and how it'll factor into the post-launch plans of GTA 6. Considering just how consistently popular GTA Online has been for the developer, it is strange that Rockstar has yet to publicly comment on the anticipated multiplayer mode, as it has so far only focused on talking about the "single-player experience" of GTA 6. And that could be a major problem for the franchise.

As Valve veteran Chet Faliszek pointed out, Rockstar might be caught between a rock and a hard place. GTA Online continues to be a big money-maker for Rockstar and its parent group, Take-Two Interactive, but moving people to a GTA 6 online mode is a challenging prospect. As Faliszek explained, a lot of GTA Online players are heavily invested in the game, and thanks to GTA 5 regularly going on sale--or being given away for free through various programs--access to it has been cheap and easy.

"What are they going to do? That's a mess. We can all look through recent history--without pointing fingers--and see some people who did it by total replacement. We can see people who tried to win people over, and when that didn't happen, shut down the other thing," Faliszek said.

Whatever choice Rockstar makes, it won't please everyone . There are a few approaches Rockstar could take--like making GTA 6 Online a separate experience that exists alongside GTA 5 Online--but there's no one-size-fits-all solution for this brewing problem. In other GTA 6 news, fishing and hunting has been radically changed for the game, there is such a thing as too much crime in the game, and the game is making big changes to how you steal cars . GTA 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: Steam Has Generated $15 Billion In Revenue So Far In 2026, And New Games Are A Big Part Of It
event_sentences: As the platform that gets the lion's share of PC game sales, Steam naturally makes a lot of money every year from commissions, publishing fees, and more through its storefront. But how much cash has it made so far in 2026? Unsurprisingly, enough dough to buy Valve co-founder Gabe Newell a few more superyachts . According to the head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, Rhys Elliot, Steam has made $15 billion in 2026, and with a massive period of high-profile game releases around the corner, that number is likely to surge even higher before the year is over.

Steam's top releases by gross revenue include AAA games and breakout indie hits, with Forza Horizon 6 leading the charge. The new racing game earned Steam $210.5 million in revenue, while Crimson Desert sales were responsible for $203.3 million, Resident Evil Requiem made just over $200.9 million, and Slay the Spire 2 brought in over $148 million. Rounding out the list is Subnautica 2 at $139.2 million and Meccha Chameleon at $89.8 million.

That's a lot of cheddar, but it only counts for 6.6% of the $15 billion that Steam has made so far. Elliot noted that the top 100 new games by gross revenue make up 15.9% of Steam's total 2026 revenue so far--around $2.4 billion. Crimson Desert is also doing a lot of heavy lifting, as it accounts for about 18% of all new-IP revenue in the top 100. "Of the new-game top 100, 63% were actually new IP, but 52.5% of the revenue ($1.25B) came from established IP," Elliot wrote. "But it’s worth noting Crimson Desert, with its $203M, accounts for about 18% of all new-IP revenue in the top 100. When we take Crimson out of the analysis, the 62 new-IP games make up only about 39%. So yeah, a lot of established IP is doing the legwork, as you'd expect."

Looking ahead, Steam's coffers can expect an influx of cash from highly anticipated releases like Phantom Blade Zero, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Gears of War: E-Day, just to name a few. Valve gets a cut from whatever is sold on Steam, including the lucrative microtransactions and DLC that accompany most games these days. Elliot also spoke to GameSpot recently about what goes into a game price tag as part of our Cheap Week deep-dives .

title: Two Nintendo Directs Announced For Next Week, Including A Zelda Presentation
event_sentences: Rumors of a Nintendo Direct began picking up earlier this week after Ubisoft announced that a new look at Just Dance: Decades of Hits was on the way. It's worth noting that the publisher announced it for September 10, but given how often Just Dance games appear in Nintendo broadcasts, it was assumed this would be the date of a Nintendo Direct. With Nintendo hosting a September Nintendo Direct almost every year for the past decade--with 2024 being an exception--it looked like it was only a matter of time before the broadcast was officially announced.

As for what you can expect, Nintendo is keeping its lips zipped for now. Last year's September Direct was focused on several first-party games, smaller third-party titles, and the surprise reveal of a new Virtual Boy headset designed for Switch consoles, so we're guessing that it'll be more of the same for 2026. Following the release of the Switch 2 in 2025 and a steady stream of first-party games, 2026 has been slower by comparison, so here's hoping we get to see what new experiences Nintendo is working on. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is out later this month, so we'll probably get a new trailer for the turn-based tactics game.

When it comes to The Legend of Zelda, it feels like Nintendo has barely acknowledged that this year marks the 40th anniversary of the beloved hero in green, but this could be a prime time to show what's on the horizon. The remake of Ocarina of Time was announced several months ago, and there's also the upcoming live-action movie --so a teaser trailer wouldn't be unwelcome. If we're lucky, we might even get confirmation that The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD is finally coming to Switch consoles.

title: Xbox’s New TCL Partnership Couldn’t Come At A Worse Time
event_sentences: Xbox has announced a new partnership with TCL, which will see the Xbox app added to "select" models from the brand. This means that owners of those TCL TVs won't need to spend $500 on an Xbox Series S or $800 on an Xbox Series X, as they can instead take advantage of the cloud-based gaming features offered as part of a monthly Xbox Game Pass subscription-- but only for a few hours per month , before they need to start coughing up some extra cash to buy more hours to play.

If your TCL TV is supported, all you'll need is a Game Pass subscription and an Xbox controller to start playing. Xbox Game Pass also offers a library of games to play, so you'll be good to go once you're signed up and logged in. As a reminder, you'll only get a few hours of cloud streaming depending on which tier of Game Pass you sign up for. The cheapest option, Game Pass Essential, will give you five hours of cloud streaming; Game Pass Premium doubles that number to 10 hours, and Game Pass Ultimate caps out at 15 hours. Pricing for top-up cloud streaming packages has not yet been announced.

This announcement also comes during a busy time for Xbox, as its next big first-party game is Gears of War: E-Day. It arrives after a busy year for the gaming brand, which saw  75 day-one releases  through its subscription program. More Game Pass titles are also on the way in Septembe r, with Speedrunners 2 and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War headlining the first wave of new arrivals.

TCL TVs are typically positioned as budget-to-mid-range sets, which could potentially give Xbox exposure to millions of consumers who wouldn't normally buy one of their expensive consoles. The Azure servers that Xbox uses for streaming games belong to its parent company, Microsoft, and these have started to turn a tidy profit for the company. Microsoft recently reported $29.4 billion in Azure server sales for the last quarter, but Amazon Web Services still eclipses those numbers with $42.2 billion in quarterly revenue.

title: Game Director Finally Addresses His Rumored Foot Fetish–Wait, Not Kojima, The Other One
event_sentences: Though Miyazaki says he's not sure where the idea that he has a "thing for feet" comes from, it's something fans of his games have noticed for years . Whether we're talking The Maiden in Black from Demons' Souls or Priscilla (or Gwunevere, or Sister Friede, or Maneater Mildred) from Dark Souls, it's hard to ignore how many barefoot women are roaming Miyazaki's fictional worlds. Elden Ring's Malenia is rocking bare feet, too, although hers are metal prosthetics. The game's beaches even differentiate between barefoot players and those who are wearing footwear.

But regardless of what fans might think , Miyazaki insists this is not a Tarantino situation. And to be fair, plenty of other games are even more foot-focused than Miyazaki's work--and far less subtle about it.

title: AI浪潮下，游戏出海最赚钱赛道，变了
event_sentences: 2026年，AI已经进入游戏研发、发行和运营的各个环节。
AI能够提高产能，却不会自动告诉厂商应该做什么产品、进入哪个市场，以及哪些用户值得长期经营。
7月29日，在“一人一AI·罗斯基AI开发游戏2026私享会”上，Sensor Tower中小企业新业务总监胡伟清从市场洞察、增长案例与落地方法三个方面，分享了AI 时代的游戏出海趋势。
他反复强调的一点是：AI是放大器，而数据决定它应该往哪里发力。
2026年上半年，受部分头部产品进入流水调整期影响，市场收入环比下降约6%，至331亿美元（约合2234亿人民币）；下载量也环比减少约4%，录得222亿次。
2026年上半年，解谜（Puzzle/益智）手游内购收入环比增长7%，达到79亿美元（约合533亿人民币），超过策略游戏，成为海外收入规模最大的手游品类。
Sensor Tower统计显示，2025年7月至2026年6月，全球19个核心市场的手游广告收入超过110亿美元，预估全球整体规模约为167亿美元（约合1127亿人民币），广告展示量达到2.2万亿次。
过去一年，其广告变现收入超过3.1亿美元。
美国拥有全球最大的广告收入规模，日韩市场的千次展示收入超过100美元；东南亚和印度拥有庞大流量，但单次广告展示价值相对较低。
Sensor Tower数据显示，2026年第二季度，Tripledot Studios旗下产品在美国市场的网页商店收入占比已经达到16%。
收入榜前20中，有超过10款是年内上线的新作，说明PC市场仍然存在较强的新品消费需求。
·AI的两种用法：提高效率，或者创造新体验
分享中，胡伟清用《异环》和《Mimesis》说明了AI在游戏中的两种不同角色。
《异环》代表的是AI对全球发行效率的提升。
产品上线首日登顶日本、韩国和美国等市场的iOS下载榜，并在Steam、PlayStation等平台获得较高关注。
上线3个月后，其移动端累计内购收入达到约5300万美元（约合3.57亿人民币），其中海外市场贡献78%。
在市场推广中，团队借助AI批量生成不同地区的定制素材。
AI还被用于多语种剧情适配，以及不同设备上的画面和性能优化。
这里的AI更像一套效率工具。
AI让同一款产品可以更快覆盖不同语言、审美和媒体环境。
《Mimesis》则把AI放进了核心玩法。
游戏中的AI可以模仿玩家动作、语音和表达习惯，让其他参与者难以判断身边究竟是真实队友还是AI。
据现场分享，《Mimesis》销量已经超过200万份，并依靠玩家自发创作形成持续传播。
两款产品的区别是：一种用AI把原有流程做得更快，另一种则利用AI创造传统技术难以实现的体验。
前者正在快速普及，后者更接近所谓的“AI原生游戏”。
·数据确定方向，AI放大结果
胡伟清将AI驱动游戏出海总结为四个环节：研发端提高美术、关卡和叙事产能；投放端生成区域化素材并动态调整预算；运营端面向不同用户推送个性化活动；发行端统一移动、PC和主机数据，实现跨平台增长。
如果不了解目标国家、细分品类和竞争格局，AI只会帮助团队更快做出一个方向错误的产品；如果没有竞品素材和渠道效果作为参照，批量生成内容也可能只是批量制造无效素材；如果缺乏用户分层，所谓个性化运营也只能停留在表面。
海外游戏市场已经进入存量竞争阶段，AI让生产速度不断提升，但用户时间并没有同步增加。
用数据洞察把握趋势，用AI技术突破增长边界，再用全链路能力重塑中国游戏的全球竞争力。

title: 下载量暴跌90%后，这款老游戏把用户价值翻了10倍
event_sentences: 一款上线9年、下载量较巅峰期下滑超过90%的老游戏，还有机会重新增长吗？
三方数据显示，《Toon Blast》美国市场的ARPDAU曾长期维持在0.17—0.38美元，调整后突破3美元。
移动游戏设计往往习惯做加法，而爆破品类的突破来自做减法。
Peak做好了这个当时排名靠后的品类，最终累计获得超过50亿美元玩家支出，其中《Toon Blast》贡献约60%，《Toy Blast》贡献约37%。
具体到功能上，《Toon Blast》收入反转的起点，是2023年10月上线的Super Light Ball，可以直译为“超级光球”。
同期下载量较峰值下滑超过90%，收入却接近历史高位，留下来的玩家贡献了接近过去10倍的价值。
多数团队可能还在反复论证，Peak选择先上线，再根据数据修正。
例如Rocket Monday要求玩家制作一定数量的火箭，First Try Tuesday则奖励首次尝试便通关的玩家。
Moon Active测试中的《Royal Splash:Tower Blast》，就采用了相近的设计。
团队没有把他们视为产品衰退的证明，而是当成一项仍可挖掘的资产，并围绕这批用户持续测试了两年。

title: How to escape Xanthe's trap in The Blood of Dawnwalker
event_sentences: Working out how to escape Xanthe's trap in The Blood of Dawnwalker took me a lot longer than I'd like to admit. This event only occurs during your assault on Griefberg Castle if you chose not to spare Xanthe , or straight up killed her before starting the final sequence. Obviously, this guide will contain some spoilers , but I'll also explain how to escape the trap she leaves for you from beyond the grave.

You should enter whichever room has this banner and drop down the hole inside Rebel Wolves You'll have to pull the bookcase back to reveal the hole in the first room Rebel Wolves The key to getting through Xanthe's labyrinth lies in the banners you can see hanging up next to each door. You should go through the doors that have the banner pictured above next to them —triangular, pointing downward, with a kind of tentacled eye depicted on them. There's actually a note earlier in the castle you can read, which explains the only way to get into the dungeon is by following the banners.

If you've just entered the trap, you'll have to fight the enemies in the main room, go through the door ahead and to your left, and pull back the bookcase to reveal a hole you should drop down. After that, enter the main room again, fight the enemies, look for the door with that banner next to it, and drop down again. One last time: enter the main room, kill the enemies, find the banner, go through the door next to it and drop down the hole.

title: Guild Wars 3 is a lot smaller scale than Guild Wars 2 because of the new approach to combat and movement: 'You would probably see about 20 players in a large combat scenario'
event_sentences: Since ArenaNet's approach to sequels is non-traditional, I'm a bit more open to the smaller scale. Guild Wars 2 won't be going anywhere, just as the original Guild Wars is still around and being updated. If I want massive PvE fights, I can just fire up GW2 again.

That said, the party size is going to create some issues in my regular game group. Most of my time in Guild Wars 2 has been spent with four friends, but at the moment ArenaNet is planning to limit Guild Wars 3 parties to four players. One of our crew is going to be left out in the cold.
