title: The bizarre spirit of classic Elder Scrolls games is alive and well in little lo-fi RPG A Short Quest
event_sentences: When a big old tree talks, I listen. He said, "I have a task of great importance," as soon as I opened my eyes, and who was I to turn him down? "Take this note to the King, it should be a short quest," he instructed, and although there is no king in the playtest for A Short Quest , I am eager to fulfill the tree's wishes when the whole game is out next year.

There are actually a lot of mysterious things I found in the few hours I spent with A Short Quest that I'd like to know more about. Every time I passed by a pond it spoke and asked me to dance (jump three times) for a blueberry. I found a note in an old mine that told me how to find the "glyph cipher" on the side of a cart, but I still don't know what to do with it. And I'm still not sure why I was summoned into the underground domain of a ghost wizard who tried to kill me.

The little pocket of A Short Quest's fantasy world in the playtest is sprinkled with weirdos and secrets. I dueled a guard on a wooden plank at the top of a mountain after he tricked me into dropping some food for his empty stomach. I also recovered a magical ember in a mine and took it to a wizard who let me make my first staff. None of this stuff is tracked in a quest log or highlighted on a map. When you find a strange item, you have to use it to figure out what it does, which can sometimes mean poisoning yourself a little or realizing you can fill up the blue squares under your health bar to cast spells.

Spells are a cheat code compared to the various melee instruments you can equip in the playtest. That's probably why they have a limited number of uses. The developers of A Short Quest don't want me trivializing the entire game with magical, heat-seeking daggers at my side, which is fair because if I could I would. I don't know how it'll be in the full game, but I kind of appreciate that magic doesn't seem to be a way to skip close-quarters combat altogether. It takes a few seconds for spells to go off, making them more effective as an opener for a fight rather than something to spam from a distance.

The playtest, and the Steam page , tease a lot more toys to play with in the full game. I see axes, daggers, skeleton minions, ogres, and a pet dog in one of the trailers. Your character level is limited in the playtest, but the skill trees for weapons and spells look like they'll encourage different approaches to combat. I didn't get enough time to fully understand how to identify weak points on enemies, but I did team up with a bandit at one point who told me to aim for the knees and I don't think it was only a Skyrim joke.

Developer Silent Moon wasn't kidding with the name and says it will indeed be a short experience, which sounds perfect for a game of this scale. It's like an appetizer to keep you satisfied before The Elder Scrolls 6 finally shows up. And, honestly, it might end up being more faithful to the spirit of the series than whatever Bethesda releases.

title: A multi-month delay for Deus Ex turned into a huge payoff for one of its best characters, says designer Harvey Smith
event_sentences: Nobody likes game delays. Sure, a delay is temporary and suck is forever , as Gabe Newell once said, but it still chafes. But sometimes a little extra development time can go a very long way. In a new interview with the NoClip podcast , immersive sim maestro Harvey Smith shared one such story about Deus Ex, explaining how it leveraged some extra post-production time to give a much bigger role to one of the game's most famous NPCs—and make it a much better game in the process.

Smith's tale actually followed a remark by Ben Horne, his co-founder at the new Black Pony Immersive studio, who said, "You can elevate a good immersive sim into a great immersive sim in a very short amount of time, a matter of months, if you just protect a post-production time."

Publishers generally don't want to hear that, Smith added—although he obviously agrees with the sentiment—and so 20-some years ago, when Ion Storm Austin asked Eidos for more time to tighten up Deus Ex, "We geared up for this giant fight." Instead, Eidos just said yes.

"They were so distracted by what was happening in Dallas with Daikatana and such that they were like, 'Sure, sure, sure. Take five more months, take six more, whatever you need.' And we were like, 'Oh, cool. Okay'."

What was happening in Dallas, as Smith put it, was essentially chaos, which you can dig into via our history of Ion Storm . But, as Smith has previously related, it was a useful distraction for Ion Storm Austin, which did indeed get the extra time it wanted to really nail down Deus Ex.

A focus of that extra dev time was one of the game's foremost NPCs, "this German guy with a skull gun" named Gunther Hermann —who, for the record, very much wanted a skull gun but as far as I know never actually got one despite filing the required paperwork. "He's kind of a big presence in a couple of missions, you go on a mission with him, and then he just vanishes," Smith said. "He has no closure. He's not even in the game.

"So, I literally said, I can drop him into Paris, a big fight in the cathedral, which is an empty building right now, and I can hide some triggers on the roof with data links, and if you're crawling around on the roof because you have 'super jump' or whatever, I'll have him say, 'I'm watching you, Denton, like an insect crawl around on the roof. I am watching you through the satellite, which I am linked to right now, Denton.' You know, so we do this kind of thing, and players go, 'Well fuck, somebody's watching me from a satellite.' It's like smoke and mirrors, and then you get in there and you fight it out with him.

This is fascinating for me personally because I had that exact experience: Skulking around a Paris cathedral, quietly working my way inside, when all of a sudden Gunther busts in on the radio to let me know I'm not fooling anyone. Giving it even more weight, I discovered before our final confrontation that Gunther had been waiting for me for some time—and that MJ12 troopers had heard him quietly crying, probably because I'd previously killed Navarre , his cyborg partner and someone for whom he apparently had deeper feelings than were immediately apparent.

It was a powerful moment, as Smith said, and it's kind of wild to imagine a version of Deus Ex where Gunther doesn't get his big finish—and what else might have been left on the cutting room floor besides. Something to keep in mind the next time you find yourself grinding your teeth over a delayed game.

Smith reiterated the importance of that point at the end of his story. "If you are listening to this right now and you fund games, give your team a post-production," he said. "Give them three to six extra months and you will win some awards and you will make a bunch of money, instead of leaving a crater in the ground."

title: Owner of nearly decade-old Dell laptop reportedly wore through the wrist rest and is 'being stabbed by carbon fibers'
event_sentences: A user on X reported feeling pins and needles in their hands whenever they used their Dell XPS 9370 laptop. After investigation, it turns out, "I’ve worn through the palm rests, and now I’m just being stabbed by carbon fibers." Ouch.

Notably, the XSP 13 (from around 2018) black and white model appears to have a carbon fiber composite palm rest, which is the part that has been worn down from use. They have since put their finger under a microscope , showing off the flecks of what is reportedly carbon fiber embedded in their skin. The user also reports " severe issues " with their contact lenses and says it is "most probably irritation" from the carbon fiber. Again, ouch.

Carbon fiber is a fairly common building material for PC hardware. We've seen a Corsair mouse , a Keychron keyboard concept , an Asus mouse , and even an HP laptop made out of the stuff . This choice of material makes sense, so long as it is adequately treated; carbon fiber is very tough but also very light, which means an uber-lightweight mouse doesn't have to feel flimsy because of the material choice. There are measures that companies can, and likely do, take against traditional wear and tear when using a material like carbon fiber.

Dell has yet to respond to this complaint, and we don't know exactly how the laptop has been treated in the last decade, but it's definitely made me more cautious about the long-term effects of carbon fiber gear—especially if you like to hang onto your hardware for a long time.

title: DLSS 5 can be jammed into almost any game now, so I've been playing FM26 with neural rendered little computer people because that's just what I do
event_sentences: Ever since the Control mod appeared I've been enjoying jamming the released DLSS 5 .dll files into a bunch of different games, to greater or lesser effect. Some games it works well in, some it doesn't quite take and you end up with visuals that look a lot like the characters have worms writhing around under their skin.

Though, I have to say when I stuck it into the review version of The Blood of Dawnwalker and it failed to hook the DLSS pipeline that look kinda worked for my semi-Vrakhiri. Bit of extra undead chic with the game failing to run the DLSS neural rendering feature with actual motion vectors or scene depth.

With the necessary files being released in the early access version of NBA 2K27, they've now been unleashed across the internet and modders have been busy getting game-agnostic versions ready for people to squeeze into any title they fancy. And while the first iteration was focused on Control and then games running DLSS already, there have been mods released—particularly the RenoDX and specifically the ShortFuse mods—which allow you to experiment with pushing DLSS 5 into practically any game you like.

And it's surprisingly easy to do, though not without its awkwardness, too. Well, such is the way with unreleased features shoehorned into games they're not meant to be in, but also such is the way with PC gaming.

The thing that has stood out to me—and something that Andy first noted in his hands-on look at the official technology at Gamescom —is that DLSS 5 really can produce some outstanding visual effects… if used sparingly. Pick the right model of the three (for me, that's Model C) and drop the intensity of the effect down to around 60 - 70% and you end up with scenes and character models that look better than the originals, but without the over-saturated, overblown very AI look of it dialed up to 11, nor without it looking like it's grinding away or adding its own geometry.

That, in all honesty, is to be expected. When Nvidia first showed off the tech around GDC it was running on a pair of RTX 5090s, so the fact that it can be run at all on single lower-spec GPUs is impressive. But it was also going to be punitive for current generation hardware, which only have tensor cores enough for standard DLSS upscaling.

And, well, I'm going to be leaving it enabled. It's not that it suddenly makes the game look photorealistic—as Nvidia itself has said, you need a really good input source to get a really good output from DLSS 5—but on its own it adds in a bunch of things that you otherwise have to mod in yourself from a bunch of other places. And because it's just added in last, and FM isn't hugely demanding, I'm still happily locked to 60 fps anyways.

But it does improve the environmental lighting of the matches. It makes the pitches look better, there's a tiny amount more detail on the tiny people, on the pitch and in the crowd, and it adds in some improved shadows. But it's not just in the 3D engine, because it also works its neural rendering magic on the player profile pics, too. Which is especially helpful for making the regenerated players look less like plastic Action Man figures (or GI Joes, for my American cousins).

Normally you'd have to use a mod to get more realistic player faces, and even then they're still just a bunch of AI generated profile pics which get disseminated among the database so you still get identical twins from different parts of the game world. With DLSS 5 I'm just getting a little extra facial detail and realism for my new potato-faced folk.

Now, it's far more straightforward. The cleanest installation method I've found is to use the ReShade HDR Installer (RHI) from Github. This does all the hard work for you—run it as Administrator and you can just pick from a list of installed games on the left hand side of the UI, install ReShade, and then pick one of the DLSS Tools from the Shaders/Addon button at the top, or from sliding over to the specific Neural Rendering section that has just been added. This should install the necessary .dll files in the right places for your game to work.

But, it must be noted, that this is all predicated on an as yet officially unreleased feature being jammed into unsupporting games. So you might find your mileage varies on just how much messing around you might need to do to get it running perfectly. If at all.

Future Future When you boot into the game you can then hit 'Home' to bring up the ReShade in-game menu and slide over to the RenoDX tab to access the DLSS 5 options. Now, these are options and sliders that aren't going to be available in the release versions of DLSS 5. That's something important to note, as officially DLSS 5 is going to be an on/off toggle switch so that you just get the version of DLSS 5 the game devs themselves have tuned.

The ReShade option puts those sliders in your hands, but with less fine grain control over where it's deployed and how intensely. Which is going to make the whole maintaining artisitic intent thing a tricky argument. There has been resistance to DLSS 5's AI filtering, with some folk suggesting that it tramples on the original artistic intent of the developers. So Nvidia has spent a lot of time since its announcement talking about the level of control devs will have themselves, and that it will only be in their hands with no sliders for us gamers. These mods, however, change that giving users a level of control not officially sanctioned, which means gamers themselves will get to choose how much of the devs artistic intent they want to retain.

Anyways, you ideally want to use the Upscaled or DLSS version of DLSS-NR rather than the 'Present' method (if you're using the ShortFuse mod). Present is the version that runs when the game frames are presented rather than inside the actual graphics pipeline. That means you lack the motion and depth information DLSS 5 relies on to be effective. If it's saying 'Waiting' then something's gone wrong.

title: Microsoft announces cap on Xbox Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers, admits most aren't using it much anyway
event_sentences: As Microsoft continues to flail for a remedy to the reputational damage it's incurred as a result of its repeated mass layoffs , bungled industry consolidation strategies , and partnership with Israeli surveillance agencies , its gaming division is returning to a favorite page from its playbook in recent years: Hiking service costs.

Today, Xbox announced that it will implement a monthly cap on Xbox Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers. Previously, eligible Game Pass users could use the game streaming service without a time limit; Beginning in November, however, they'll need to purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store once they expend their allotted cloud gaming hours.
"We expect this upcoming change to impact 4% of Game Pass subscribers," Xbox said.

Xbox didn't confirm how much cloud playtime will cost, but said it will provide "more information about pricing, purchasing additional hours, eligible games, market availability, and how players can check their remaining time" in November.

"We’re introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer," Xbox said. "Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."

Evidently, the company doesn't expect the ad-supported game streaming it began testing last month will sufficiently move the needle on that front. And that needle's got a lot of moving to do: In July, Microsoft's annual financial filings confirmed that Xbox revenue had fallen by $1.7 billion over the last year.

Whether "the practical result" of a higher cost on cloud streaming will actually deliver needed revenue gains for Xbox, however, is unclear. In June, new Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball said the company lost "millions" of Game Pass subscribers after the service's 2025 price hike.

title: It's really starting to look like a new StarCraft game will be revealed at BlizzCon
event_sentences: The excitement began earlier this week when Korea's Chosun ( Google translated , via WCCFTech ) ran a story saying Nexon is close to finalizing a deal to develop a new game based on the StarCraft series. As Chosun noted, the series has been dormant since StarCraft Remastered in 2017; the last original StarCraft game, StarCraft 2, arrived all the way back in 2010. Despite that, the series remains hugely popular in Korea.

The StarCraft subreddit took some issues with the report: For one thing, Chosun suggested the new game would be StarCraft 3, rather than the StarCraft shooter Nexon is reportedly working on . There are also concerns that the report might be accurate, given CEO Junghun Lee's enthusiasm for generative AI and microtransactions. Still, the timing seemed right: BlizzCon 2026 runs September 12-13, which is now less than two weeks away.

That's how things remained until earlier today, when the StarCraft website started glitching , in the way that doesn't happen unless it's intentional: Images twitching, text flashing, all that sort of thing. The classic loss of signal right before something happens—that's probably not a coincidence, right?

It's a bit more conspiracy-coded, but the WoW subreddit has also noticed a rather peculiar gap in the BlizzCon main stage schedule —about an hour, early on the first day, that's unaccounted for. What might fit into that hour? Well, anything that takes 60 minutes or less, really, but the prevailing opinion seems to be StarCraft.

(Image credit: Blizzard) Our resident Blizzard pro Tyler Colp cast his wizened eye upon the BlizzCon floor map and saw nothing carved out for StarCraft, so even if a new game is announced, it likely won't be playable—although it's possible Blizzard is camouflaging a demo area in the Well of Eternity or whatever.

Adding to that, earlier this year Blizzard was looking to hire a "lead designer of innovation" for an open world shooter using Unreal Engine, the studio recently dropped a major patch for StarCraft 2 , and most recently, it revealed that this year's BlizzCon rewards will include a 15-day co-op XP boost for Commander progression in StarCraft 2. That's pretty small, sure, but as Tyler said, this is the kind of stuff that gets fans wound up real good.

Given all the shooter hints, it doesn't seem very likely to me that a StarCraft 3 RTS will be the big announcement—if there is in fact a big announcement at all. A shooter would also seem to comport with Microsoft's post-Phil Spencer strategy of focusing on games with the potential to go over big with mass audiences. Anything's possible, and frankly I think actual StarCraft 3 would provide a much more immediate boost to Microsoft's gamer cred than an all-new shooter. But is Microsoft really going to take a risk on a niche genre when it's cancelling big survival games and MMOs ? I suspect not.

title: I've found DLSS 5 can slash frame rates by up to 73% on an RTX 5080 gaming PC in NBA 2K27, and I'm wondering what kind of mega-rig would justify the performance hit
event_sentences: DLSS 5 is finally here. Well, its been officially released in one game, anyway, after modders got their hands on it last week and made the actual launch somewhat redundant. Still, I've been testing Nvidia's new AI image-enhancing tech in NBA 2K27, the latest hoop-shooting game in the long-running series, and I have bad news: even on a high-end RTX 5080 rig, it's seriously punishing when it comes to performance.

I threw a pre-release version of NBA 2K27 at one of our benchmarking rigs, an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , RTX 5080-equipped, 32 GB DDR5 behemoth. And while this particular PC can make mincemeat of the game's relatively lightweight hardware needs overall, turning on DLSS 5 can drop the average frame rate by up to 73% in certain scenarios.

That represents a staggering 73% decrease in average frames, and an instantly crunchy experience. Sure, 49 fps is perfectly playable, but with the knowledge that NBA 2K27 would be capable of so many more frames with the AI-enhanced pretties turned off, I'm not sure I could grin and bear it.

Given all of Nvidia's benchmarks are with a lower resolution DLSS setting and the full 6x Multi Frame Generation bean, on the one hand I expected DLSS 5 to actually need MFGto achieve smooth frame rates at all, or require Ultra Performance-level upscaling. So, the fact that I can achieve very playable frame rates with just 2x frame gen and upscaling set to Quality is still pretty impressive. But on the other, NBA 2K27 runs so well without DLSS 5 enhancement, the thought of slashing my frame rate by such a huge amount for some prettier, AI-assisted graphics stops me in my tracks. Speaking of which...

My early concern about DLSS 5 was that it seemed to produce overblown, AI beauty filter-like imagery , which I personally find very ugly. However, as I pointed out in my DLSS 5 sneak peak , the implementation in this particular game is often much more tasteful.

His beard looks a little more lifelike, as does his hair. And I'd pay special attention to his jersey, which has extra wrinkles in the fabric in the DLSS 5-ified image that give it a more 3D-like effect. Because you'll be paying attention to your team's ironing mishaps in your new basketball game, obviously.

As your graphics card screams bloody murder, perhaps. But as much of a cynic as I am regarding the idea of AI "enhancement" of any sort, I can't deny that DLSS 5 in close up is capable of producing some lifelike human beings.
It's far from flawless, though. While some character models look noticeably more realistic, others get some heavy-handed AI treatment that isn't quite so seamless.
Above: NBA 2K27's photo mode, with DLSS 5 turned off to start, and then on and off again in sequence.

And finally, here's a comparison between the crowds. You're going to need to fullscreen and zoom in on this one, but it's fairly representative of how you'll see the match attendees when you're actually playing the game. Aside from the odd camera cut, they're mostly there for background atmosphere.

Still, I can absolutely see why Nvidia picked this game for DLSS 5's first official outing. NBA 2K27 feels well optimised with the AI frippery turned off, and it's not the sort of thing that would otherwise be bothering most modern rigs.

But if my testing is any indication, DLSS 5 can look really good, but still be a massive drain on performance even in a properly optimised game. And I really question who among us will be prepared to make the frame rate trade off, even in a relatively lightweight game like this.

title: Nvidia puts its money where its mouth is on open weight AI, moving to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion
event_sentences: Nvidia has just announced that it intends to acquire Hugging Face, the biggest open platform dedicated to developing machine-learning applications. Considering Nvidia has been all-in on AI for the past few years—to the point that I barely remember the last time the company even mentioned gaming in an earnings call—it's hardly a surprising move.

What did encourage a sharp intake of breath from me though was the price of this purchase; Nvidia will buy Hugging Face for a total of $12,930,300,000 . $11.9 billion of that will go to Hugging Face's investors, while employees that join Nvidia will be offered an ‌equity-based retention ⁠program of up to $1 billion, according to Reuters . But even though there's billions of dollars in the mix, that doesn't mean the walls are about to come down around Hugging Face.

"Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang writes, "Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face."

He adds that the platform will continue to support both open source and open weight AI models. This is something Huang demonstrably feels passionate about, as he dedicated his first ever X post to defending easy access to open AI models .

In today's announcement, Huang further elaborates, "Open models let startups, businesses, universities and public institutions build on advanced capabilities without training every model from scratch. They enable organizations to match the right model to the right job. That is how AI can advance safely, strengthen cybersecurity and sovereignty, accelerate innovation, and reach factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms and Main Street businesses around the world.
(Image credit: Jaque Silva/NurPhoto via Getty Images) "AI advances faster when people can build together."

Hugging Face was most recently in the news when a number of OpenAI's models breached an isolated test environment and hacked the development platform's internal network . OpenAI has since detailed how it's protecting itself from the kinds of attacks its own models carried out .

Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue told CNBC last week that the company approached Jensen Huang about a deal a few weeks ago. He described Nvidia as a "perfect home". "During the summer, I think we realized that Hugging Face and open source AI in general was at the turning point, and that it needed more, more resources, more scale, more visibility."

For those keen on an agentic, local AI future, this deal could well be good news; it is arguably the biggest consumer-facing resource for free downloads of local AI models as well as retrained and abliterated models. With Nvidia set to soon release its first RTX Spark laptops with entirely its own silicon inside—from CPU to GPU cores—its own focus is obviously on putting local AI in the hands of consumers as well as frontier AI in the hands of multi-billion dollar orgs. Keeping a platform such as Hugging Face rolling makes complete sense.

(Image credit: Future) The nearly $13 billion deal is Nvidia's second largest to date. First place goes to the $20 billion Non-Exclusive Inference Technology Licensing Agreement with chipmaker Groq , though it looks like Nvidia's AI inference GPU still won't see the light of day this year . Nvidia's RTX Spark 'superchip', with purported RTX 5070-like performance , may arrive sooner rather than later. Our Andy rubbed his greasy mitts all over a host of RTX Spark laptops at Gamescom , though there's still little word on pricing. Here's hoping the RTX Spark laptops only make my eyes water in the best possible way when they go on sale in October 2026 . But realistically, they ain't going to be cheap.

title: Xgimi Titan Noir Max review
event_sentences: Once in a while, something comes along that recalibrates your expectations and also sort of ruins your enjoyment of what was once impressive. The Xgimi Titan Noir Max does just that. It makes mainstream projectors look positively pedestrian.

The basics begin with triple-laser RGB technology that's good for an eye-popping 7,000 lumens. That's combined, inevitably, with DLP and pixel-shift tech to deliver full 4K resolution at 60 Hz, plus 1080p at up to 240 Hz. Running at the latter setting, Xgimi claims that the Titan Noir Max is good for just 1 ms of latency.
7,000 lumens (5,000 lumens sustained)
RGB triple-laser, auto-focus, Dolby Vision, anti-rainbow effect, 3x HDMI, optical and 3.4mm audio

If that's the broad brush of what the Xgimi Titan Noir Max offers, the details are arguably even tastier. Xgimi is using a new generation of DLP chip that enables improved native contrast. That's combined with a 50-laser light source and Dual Intelligent Iris technology to deliver 10,000:1 native contrast. Factor in other digital contrast enhancements and you're looking at 100,000:1 claimed dynamic contrast.

Then there are the optics. This thing has some very trick lens hardware. It's built around a 15-element lens system that's said to deliver consistent edge-to-edge focus. You also get very broad optical lens shift of 130% +/- vertical and 50% +/- horizontal. That gives this projector immense installation flexibility without the need to resort to digital keystone correction.

That said, it has 2x optical zoom and a throw ratio of between 0.98:1 and 2.0:1, so it's actually pretty configurable. It can create both a pretty large image at short distance and shrink the image from distance to fit your projection screen.

All of that is built into a beautifully lush looking alloy cube chassis that's presented in a nifty carry case and goes some way to justifying the hefty $5,999 MSRP. The real-world pricing of this projector is a bit more complicated than that on account of it being the subject of a Kickstarter campaign . But hold that thought, we'll come back to the value proposition later.

Still, you do get a very slick remote control with, again, a lush metal chassis that lights up when you pick it up and allows access to the Xgimi's various menus and settings. And, boy, are there a lot of settings.

In testing, I found the auto-focus worked really well, but the rest of the automated setup is more problematic. For starters, the automated digital keystone is on by default. Especially in a computing context, that's a bad idea. The Titan also failed to frame the image correctly on my projection screen, albeit it's not absolutely clear to what extent the automated features are supposed to be capable of that.

Not only does the Titan have a really wide range of adjustment, it also provides a grid pattern that makes it super easy to perfectly align the image. Slightly less user friendly is the rest of the settings menu. Part of the problem is that there are just so many options, whether that's features like so-called AI-enhanced contrast, iris aperture settings, colour spaces, and much, much more.

Anywho, this is a complex device and I've barely touched on a whole range of further features and functionality. There's the Harmon-Kardon audio, which produces pretty decent sound in a pinch when you don't have access to some speakers, for instance. Or the broad HDR support including Dolby Vision, the MediaTek image enhancing chip or even Xgimi's own X-Vision chip that powers the AI contrast capability, known as Dynamic Black Level Enhancement.

The lens shift feature is very well executed. Future Game Mode ensures low latency. Future In practice, the sustained brightness capability is actually 5,000 lumens. The 7,000 figure is something that can only be sustained for short periods. But, seriously people, 5,000 lumens is still awfully, awfully bright. Happily, the Titan Noir Max has such fantastic native contrast, that doesn't translate into washed out black tones.

Getting just the right setup is a lengthy process. Future For gaming, all that nonsense is mercifully disabled to achieve the lowest possible latency and, indeed, the very last word in colour calibration is likewise less critical. That said, most of the colour options while running in Game Mode are atrocious, even for gaming. After a bit of a panic, I eventually discovered that, for whatever reason, the only colour space in Game Mode that gives decent results is Rec.709.

That's a relief because you absolutely want to use Game Mode to game. There's noticeable latency in all the other modes, even the pared-back Filmaker Mode that supposedly disables all the image processing to "faithfully convey the film director's creative intent."

That initial caveat aside, gaming at 4K on the Xgimi Titan Noir Max is to die for. So many projectors look a bit weedy and washed out when playing games. Not this beast. It's so bright, the desert sun in Cyberpunk 2077 is actually kind of painful when you point your mouse at it.

The detail and precision thanks to the true 4K resolution is fantastic, too. Just to put this into context, a lot of digital cinema projectors are still 2K, so you're getting a far sharper image with this projector than you often do at the cinema. Of course, 4K support is pretty commonplace these days, so that's not unique to the projector by any means. But the high-quality optics make for an exceptionally sharp image thanks to the precision and consistency of the focus across the screen. It's pretty special.

The 1080p modes are using the DLP chip at its native resolution, of course. So, there's no problem running VRR at 1080p 240 Hz. And, really, there's still decent image detail at 1080p. Like I said, a lot of commercial cinemas are still running 2K projectors today. Oh, and I found that there's relatively little visible rainbow effect in any mode, even without Xgimi's anti-RBE technology enabled.

Future All of which means it's hard to gauge the Xgimi Titan Noir Max as a gaming display. It has an MSRP of $5,999 which probably makes it irrelevant to nearly all gamers. It can currently be had for $4,999 and it was available to early adopters on Kickstarter for $2,999, though that early tranche of units is sold out. There are cheaper versions of the Titan Noir series available, too, starting from $3,999. But even that is a hill of money.

The things that the Titan Noir Max is really good at, aside from the sheer brightness, like achieving near perfect focus and geometry with absolute ease are certainly impressive. But are they worth paying thousands more for in a gaming context? I'm not so sure.

But, in all honesty, one of Xgimi's own cheaper projectors will almost certainly make more sense. The Xgimi Horizon 20, for instance, goes for $1,559 , is a full 4K model with optical lens shift and 3,200 lumens and offers the same 240 Hz, 1 ms 1080p gaming mode. Indeed, the Horizon 20 is one of the cheapest 4K projectors currently available with lens shift and the projector I'd recommend to pretty much any mere mortal, even before seeing the new Titan Noir Max.
Money no object, then, the Xgimi Titan Noir Max is a stunning piece of engineering. It really is. But in the real world where money does actually matter, it's almost certainly overkill for gaming.

title: Petit Planet's delightfully cosy galactic take on Animal Crossing is the closest we'll ever get to the life sim on PC
event_sentences: I picked the former, of course—though it looks like you might have even more starter options in the future—and set to work on building up a little planet of my own. title: Arc Raiders' executive producer admits its developers 'couldn't keep pace with the players' and their need for content, but promises Frozen Trail as the answer
event_sentences: If there's one thing you should never underestimate, it's a gamer's love for completing little tasks. Whether it's battle passes, meaningless fetch quests, or in Arc Raiders' case, its expeditions. There's just the right amount of dopamine involved for a neuron activation, so you best bet that they'll rip through them at an unthinkable speed.

I'll concede that Embark Studios probably couldn't have foreseen the full extent of this love prior to Arc Raiders release, but still, the outcome is the same: gamers out-growing their once-beloved game because they managed to complete all their tasks way too fast.

(Image credit: Embark) "We didn’t really expect that amount of players to show up and play ARC Raiders," executive producer Aleksander Grøndal explains in an interview with GamesBeat . "That surprised us. We were a bit unprepared. That’s one of the hard lessons we had to learn. When January came and some of the problems started with the game."

January saw the first crack in Arc Raiders' armour, as the novelty began to wear off and players became more keenly aware of how limited its content was alongside growing concerns about cheating and stream sniping . Unfortunately, despite some hard work from the team, the latter two points still remain contentious.

(Image credit: Embark Studios) "We bet on trying to update it fast and giving players more things to do over time. That was our strategy, to try to meet those demands from players. The issue with that was the team just couldn’t keep pace with the players. The players grew frustrated, because some of the things we shipped were perhaps not as good or as meaningful as they were hoping. That was another awakening for us."

The issue with quality over quantity is that players actually really like quantity. Many will say that they prefer for stuff to look good, but that's not really a live service game's draw, instead its draw is to provide something for players to do whenever they want. Players were promised a 10-year plan , and they haven't seen that manifest in Arc Raiders yet.

So what's the solution? A better anti-cheat would be a good start, but really, Arc Raiders just needs to find its footing and get back to a good live service cadence if it wants to bring players back. As for when this could happen, it seems like Embark is gearing up for something of a comeback in October with its upcoming Frozen Trails major update .

Grøndal has said it will bring a rank redesign, more arcs, updates to storage, and a new map as it tries "to answer a lot of those questions that have been posed to us from a mechanical and content perspective."
But until then, all players can do is wait and have some hope that better things are to come.

title: DLSS 5 is called 'DLSS Neural Rendering' in the NBA 2K27 graphics options, and I think I smell a rebrand of Nvidia's controversial graphics tech
event_sentences: If you happen to pick up a copy of NBA 2K27, in your eagerness to try out the first official implementation of Nvidia's DLSS 5 AI image tech , you won't find it labelled as such in the settings menu. Instead, it appears as a simple on/off toggle under the label "DLSS Neural Rendering." And while that might seem like a small change, I think it makes a huge amount of difference in terms of public perception.

But DLSS 5 changes things . Quite literally. And while Nvidia has gone to great pains in recent months to point out that it's both developer controlled, and a toggled option that can be safely ignored if you don't like the imagery, shoving the tech underneath the DLSS iterative umbrella felt like a poor move.

Something in the association inferred, even if it was later made clear that it wasn't the case, that AI image alteration tech was just how games were going to be going forward, and you were going to have to get on board if you wanted to keep using DLSS in future.

Now it seems like we might have a clue to the solution of this branding mess. In NBA 2K27, it's been labelled as DLSS Neural Rendering, and it's an on/off switch that can be used independently of the upscaling, or ignored entirely for those who don't want to get on the AI image alteration train.

(Image credit: 2K Games) Our Dave first noticed this change in the leaked DLL files last week , which refer to it as "Nvidia DLSSNR." But the fact it appears in an official game settings menu under the "Neural Rendering" title feels like a step in the right direction. Nvidia seems painfully aware that it needs to rehabilitate its new tech, and separating the nomenclature would be a good start.

Of course, the naming scheme is only part of the story when it comes to the controversy. There are many who are dead set against the idea of any sort of AI generation tech entering their games , amid a wider AI backlash. Nothing's changed there, I would wager.

Separate from that, whether you like the look of the AI-altered imagery is still a matter of taste. It's developer controlled, as Nvidia has repeatedly pointed out—though if you start modding it into games yourself , like Dave has, you do get your own sliders to play with.

Still, I've got a feeling we're going to see some relatively subtle implementations to start with—and inevitably, some goppingly ugly, AI beauty filter-like imagery as time goes on. There's no accounting for taste in a general sense, and there's certainly no accounting for taste when it comes to graphics.

It's also, in its current iteration, a massive performance hog. Nvidia claimed a 50-60% performance hit, but my early testing in NBA 2K27 shows it can hamstring an RTX 5080 by up to 73% at certain settings. That's a very powerful (and expensive) graphics card, held back significantly by Nvidia's new toy.

All of which means the DLSS 5/DLSS Neural Rendering controversy is likely far from over. But I can't help but feel that if the tech was unveiled as "DLSS Neural Rendering" in the first place, as just a new optional feature and not presented as the entirety of DLSS 5, a fair amount of the confusion—and perhaps even initial backlash—could have been avoided.

title: Age Twisters is a simple yet charming spin on the co-op adventure that aims to feel like watching a Pixar movie
event_sentences: As I'm making my way through the beginning of two-player co-op adventure Age Twisters alongside the founders of developer Piccolo Studios, I'm told the goal was to create a game that evokes the same feelings as watching a Pixar movie with your child. Now I am admittedly sprogless, but it wasn't difficult to latch onto those similar fuzzy feelings of nostalgia and familial love even as I completed puzzles alongside a man I'd only met minutes prior.

Age Twisters is the studio's attempt at a game like It Takes Two or Split Fiction, albeit much lower on the toughness scale—something which the developer itself admits, instead going for a game that's constantly evolving and different rather than outright difficult. It takes a granddaughter-grandfather duo and slaps a couple of age-bending bracelets on them, allowing each one to age up or down all the way from a young child to a hobbling old bean.

(Image credit: Krafton) It's a wonderfully novel mechanic—each age has its own portrait, voice acting, and dynamic dialogue that'll shift as you age up or down across the story. Each even comes with their own quirks. I attempted to jump over a gap as an old lady but was unable to, and similarly found myself stuck when trying to jump up and grab onto a ledge as a tiny tyke.

(Image credit: Krafton) Piccolo Studios says it played into stereotypes of each generation somewhat when creating these abilities, all in the name of humour of course. While the story is ultimately one of loss—it's all about figuring out what happened to the granddaughter's mother—it's one about trying to bridge the gap between generations. As the developer puts it to me, it's about remembering being young while understanding what it means to get older.
Age Twisters is set to release on Steam in 2027.

title: In a sea of failed live service games, I'm shocked to see someone trying to make a MOBA
event_sentences: Though, as Nirvanana will maintain, Project Zeta isn't quite a MOBA. As the developer tells me, it's actually a 4v4 multi-team tactical arena battle. Not battle royale, just battle. "We tried not to be tied down to those traditional things," Nirvanana tells me as I sit down to try Project Zeta at Gamescom, though admits the game did start out as a more traditional battle royale.

But from there, it's evolved into a sort of battle royale-MOBA-hero shooter hybrid, pitting four teams against each other as they fight across a sprawling map for victory. I'm shown flashy footage of Twitch streamers popping off after winning teamfights, proclaiming how good it feels to win in Project Zeta—emerging victorious from a teamfight refreshes cooldowns for the winners, as well as resurrecting any teammates who fell in the scuffle.

How that core audience will eventually translate into playercounts with the full release, however? Nirvanana knows it's a tough ask. "You have to have a clear message," the developer tells me. "And you have to take the players that agree with that message, and you have to build a community before launch with those players. And I think that's the only way to secure success once the game launches.

It all seems like a very hopecore way of looking at things, though Nirvanana does cap it all off by admitting: "Games like us failed a lot. The track record isn't good." Well, for Project Zeta's sake, I hope it can carve out a slice of success in an increasingly difficult landscape.

title: 'That criticism is justified': Gamescom apologizes for its callous response to developer hardware thefts
event_sentences: Today, Gamescom released an additional statement on X, admitting that its initial response was inadequate and committing to improving the rigor of its security procedures with input from affected exhibitors.

"Over the past few days, we have received a great deal of criticism for the way we communicated about the theft of hardware belonging to several indie developers. That criticism is justified," Gamescom said. "Our first response did not strike the right tone, and it did not show the people affected the empathy they deserved. We are sorry."

After acknowledging the emotional, financial, and professional cost of the hardware thefts, Gamescom said it has "been moved by" and is "grateful for" the outpouring of support for affected exhibitors, which "says a great deal" about the industry and its consumers.

However, that generosity does not, it said, "relieve us, as the organizers, of our own responsibility to work together with our exhibitors and partners to create the best possible environment for everyone. We are therefore committed to jointly reviewing and further improving security."

(Image credit: Hesham Elsherif via Getty Images) In addition to its standard post-event assessment of exhibitor feedback, Gamescom said it's committing to both "a dedicated review of security for indie exhibitors" and to hosting a roundtable with indie booth organizers "so that we can develop concrete measures together." Gamescom also urged any additional exhibitors who suffered thefts during this year's show to report those incidents to both the event organizers and to police.

What the statement doesn't mention is any possibility of compensation for affected exhibitors. PC Gamer contacted Gamescom's organizers at Koelnmesse GmbH to ask how many incidents had been reported, whether any compensation has been investigated or offered to exhibitors whose equipment was stolen, and what forms of vetting and oversight Gamescom security staff are subject to. Gamescom PR offered no response beyond referring PC Gamer to its two published statements about the incidents.

"Our commitment has always been to keep making Gamescom better—together with the community, not just when things go well," Gamescom said in today's statement on X. "That is exactly what we will do here."

title: Silent Hill: Townfall is the most Scottish game I've ever played and the most effective horror game I've seen in ages: 'It made sense for us to dig deep into our upbringings, into our past, and try and build a place that felt believable'
event_sentences: What a relief, then, that Townfall not only feels incredibly Scottish, its Scottishness also perfectly matches Silent Hill's brand of unsettling psychological horror. And it's not such an unlikely pairing. Scotland is a brilliant fit for this kind of game—and I'm going to spend the next 2,000 or so words convincing you why.

It helps, of course, that the studio is both local and knows its way around the genre. Glaswegian developer Screen Burn has been serving up frights and mysteries since 2015, namely through Stories Untold and Observation . You might know it better by its former name, No Code. Co-founder and Townfall game director Jon McKellan also worked on Alien: Isolation prior to starting up the studio.

Outside a shop I notice a pair of charity boxes—one in the shape of a guide dog, another a swirly wishing well that looks like a helter skelter—that nearly everyone from the UK will recognise, not just Scots. These tiny bits of window dressing make the fictional town feel like a tangible place. I have absolutely been here before, even though I definitely haven't.

"They're kind of frail, they're unreliable," says McKellan. "I think all of that speaks really well to horror because you get these tools and they help you, but they're never going to be good enough to get you out of a jam. Relying on the analogue, it allows you to play within those limitations, which work well with horror. I think aesthetically as well, it adds texture, even just to the real-world tactile interfaces that feel just a little bit more grounded. Anything we can do to make the player feel like they're there is going to help with horror."

At a most basic level, it's just nice to be in your cosy home looking out the window at the rain pishing down or the fog rolling in. And Townfall preserves this. While there are plenty of horrors hidden in the buildings, at least in the early part I was playing the streets are a lot more deadly, with the mist hiding horrors drawn from Simon—the protagonist—and St. Amelia's trauma. It feels safer indoors.

(Image credit: Konami) When Scotland is presented in videogames, it's usually a brief aside or approaching parody—all kilts and whisky and golf, with accents that call to mind fantasy dwarves. Townfall is more confident in its Scottishness—it doesn't need to scream about it at the top of its lungs. It's an understated familiarity, which lends it a more potent air of authenticity.

In the '90s, most of the world's experience of Scotland came through two movies: Braveheart and Trainspotting. Unsurprisingly, a Hollywood production featuring an Australian nutcase didn't quite capture the country. Trainspotting certainly did, though. It reflected the less palatable side of Scotland, the one the tourists rarely get to see: the squalor, the addiction, the depression and urban decay.

Townfall is much closer to Trainspotting than Braveheart, but rather than urban poverty and heroin addiction, it explores themes like medical trauma, the evisceration of small communities and the social impact of Margaret Thatcher's rule—one of Scotland's most loathed villains, right up there with King Edward I of England, the man also known as the Hammer of the Scots.

(Image credit: Konami) "The medical trauma is something that Simon's clearly involved with," says McKellan. "Without going into too much detail, I think again you kind of write what you know, and a lot of the experiences that Simon and the characters have have come from a real place and come from something that's pretty authentic in terms of how we cope with those things. So it also felt Silent Hill. It felt like the kind of story you would expect in a series like Silent Hill, without copying anything that's come before."

The protest signs I see are real, as in Screen Burn actually made physical protest signs, scanned them and added them to the game, "to make sure it felt like this is what it would look like". The studio didn't simply want to make copies, it wanted to make the real deal, something authentic. Something that reflects "what life was like", even if the game isn't technically about what life was like—this is still Simon's story. And Simon is an outsider.

I played Townfall in a well-lit, hot room surrounded by other journalists as a fan blew directly in my face. There probably isn't a worse way to experience a horror game. But I was genuinely entranced. St. Amelia's thick, thick atmosphere, the obsessive attention to detail, the juxtaposition of the familiar and the horrifying—I was no longer an exhausted journalist trying to get through another Gamescom appointment, I was living through a horror story in my own backyard. And it was awesome.
Silent Hill: Townfall launches on September 24.

title: Great, now motherboard prices might be next to spike thanks to component costs increasing by up to 50%
event_sentences: Board Channels is a forum for hardware manufacturers and partners to communicate. One poster recently wrote , "The price of upstream raw materials for motherboards has indeed risen significantly." They go on to say that the price of motherboard PCBs alone has increased by between 15% and 50% . Wi-Fi modules are said to have gone up between 10% and 20%, while capacitor prices have also gone up approximately 50% (via Videocardz ).

As we've reported before, these price increases are likely caused by material shortages resulting from the Strait of Hormuz crisis and the ongoing Iran war . For instance, PPE resin can be thought of as the glue that binds the many layers of a PCB together, and a huge chunk of the world's high-quality PPE comes from petrochemical company Saudi Basic Industries Corporation (SABIC) in Saudi Arabia. Not only does this company rely on the Strait of Hormuz to ship exports out, but Reuters reports SABIC's Jubail plant was attacked back in April .

"Looking at the price increases from major motherboard manufacturers in August, the overall increases were relatively small, only around 3%, and affecting a limited number of models," the source continues, "Among Taiwanese brands, MSI raised prices across the board, while Asus and Gigabyte only increased prices for their main models, with small increases ranging from 5-50 yuan. Domestic brands [in China] like Colorful and Maxsun only increased prices by 10-20 yuan, resulting in a relatively small overall increase."

For context, five yuan is about $0.74. 10 yuan is $1.49, and 50 yuan is still only about $7.44 at time of writing. But the source goes on to say, "There is still room for motherboard costs to rise, and it is possible that motherboard manufacturers will continue to raise prices for certain models in the coming months."

title: How Roblox Scaled Its Kafka Platform to Over 18 Trillion Messages a Day
event_sentences: In the past two years, we scaled our internal message queue platform over 2.5x each year to over 18 trillion messages per day. We currently process over 300 million messages per second while maintaining 99.995% availability. This message queue platform, built on Apache Kafka, has become a critical part of how we move data across the company. It supports workloads such as analytics events , moderation pipelines , matchmaking systems , and many more. These numbers are exciting, but the more important story is how we got there.

Teams across Roblox have built various platforms on top of the messaging queue, including AI training pipelines, stream processing abstractions, and telemetry systems. Partnering with the owners of these platforms allows us to help ensure adherence to best practices such as enabling batching and compression. This results in efficient systems without involving end users in detailed configuration setup.

One key lesson we’ve learned is that large-scale platforms are more reliable when they don’t treat all traffic equally. Some workloads require very low latency and strong protection during spikes, such as our matchmaking systems, which operate with under 10 milliseconds of end-to-end latency. Others are extremely high volume yet more tolerant of delay, like our analytics event ingestion pipelines, which can run smoothly even with multiple seconds of end-to-end latency. If both are handled identically, the highest-volume traffic can crowd out more business-critical traffic, especially during peak load.

To solve this problem, we group traffic by use case requirements to ensure that each one is well supported. The trade-off between end-to-end latency and throughput in Kafka is one of the primary considerations when setting up new use cases. This holds true through the data path from producer to server to consumer: Each of these has configurations that can be tuned to optimize for either throughput or latency. Client-side configurations can be tuned for individual use cases, but server-side configurations are less flexible, as it’s untenable to maintain a dedicated cluster for each distinct use case.

We started by running Kafka on RAID10 HDD machines. As traffic volume grew, our machines’ disk I/O capacity became the primary bottleneck limiting per-server Kafka throughput. To address this, we made two optimizations. We converted brokers to use SSDs as much as possible, shifting the bottleneck from disk I/O capacity to network throughput or disk space (as the SSDs we acquired had less disk space). This increased disk I/O throughput by 10x. We also began converting our remaining HDDs from RAID10 to RAID0. This roughly doubled disk I/O capacity, as each write with RAID0 needs only a single disk write rather than two.

The trade-off is that since each message replica is written to one disk per broker instead of two, moving from RAID10 to RAID0 can come with reliability risk. To maintain reliability, we worked with important use cases to increase acks and data replication, including replicating to multiple regions.

The queue platform is a critical component of Roblox’s infrastructure, and maintaining reliability is crucial. Prelaunch testing as well as ongoing failure scenario testing (sometimes called game day exercises ) have been instrumental in validating that our infrastructure is resilient to failure modes such as single host failure, rack failure, networking issues, and many others. Our reliability team’s internal chaos testing platform has enabled and streamlined the process of simulating various failure scenarios. These tests help identify system improvements or regressions and build operational excellence by regularly validating alerts and ensuring that operators are familiar with the steps to handle various issues—even rare ones.

We’ve also designed and implemented failover processes that can quickly restore queue functionality for dependent use cases. Even in the case of total failure of an individual cluster, we are able to switch clients to a healthy cluster with sufficient capacity. In order to ensure that we have enough unused capacity available, we maintain a standby Kafka cluster. This helps eliminate any risk of noisy neighbor issues when shifting traffic between live clusters.

The below diagram shows the high-level steps for executing a failover. First, an operator identifies the scope of the failover. Then, topics and access control lists (ACLs) are created on the standby cluster with an automated bulk operation. Finally, the operator updates our control plane service configs, which clients poll to determine whether any reconnection is needed. The illustration below is for generic real-time use cases. We have additional strategies and tooling for other use cases and scenarios, including topic mirroring using Mirror Maker 2, data backfill tooling, and more.

Roblox has strict requirements for security, which is also a critical part of reliability. We’ve implemented standard security features like encryption in transit (with mTLS), encryption at rest (with encrypted disk), data retention age requirements, and authentication/authorization with Kafka principals and ACLs. We also automatically rotate our users’ credentials to further improve security.

Besides this, we built custom handling in our control plane to facilitate fast OS patching and rack drains. During OS patching, we retain data on disk so patched machines can rapidly regain healthiness after rejoining the Kafka cluster. This way we can patch our entire fleet within 30 days, even as it continues to grow. With tools like Cruise Control, we replicate our data in a rack-aware way, so that entire racks can be taken offline for maintenance and network patching without affecting data availability.

The next chapter for our queue platform is about making the platform even simpler for developers while continuing to improve elasticity and isolation. We are investing in new abstractions, including producer and consumer proxies as well as fully managed connectors. These systems will further decouple application teams from infrastructure complexity and make our platforms easier to adopt and manage at scale. For example, a consumer proxy will enable the competing consumer pattern , allowing the platform to support a wider range of use cases and decouple scaling of processors from scaling of Kafka partitions. This is valuable for use cases like processing mass bursts of notifications, which don’t require ordering and can benefit from temporarily scaling up processor count without bound-to-achieve end-to-end delivery targets.

Scaling Kafka is not just about scaling the number and size of clusters. It’s about building the engineering discipline, abstractions, and operational model that allow Roblox to continue on our journey to connect a billion people every day with optimism and civility .

title: IFM 发布 K2 Horizon 六款开源模型，覆盖 0.9B 到 375B-A23B 并开放完整训练生命周期
event_sentences: 全部 AI 动态
AI 日报
AI 评分 78/100
IFM 发布 K2 Horizon 六款开源模型，覆盖 0.9B 到 375B-A23B 并开放完整训练生命周期
AI 导读
IFM 发布 K2 Horizon 模型系列，共六个模型：375B-A23B、36B-A4B、32B、7B、3.7B 和 0.9B，均以 Apache 2.0 开源，其中 0.9B、3.7B 和 7B 宣称在其规模上达到 SOTA，36B-A4B 采用新提出的稀疏注意力架构 MoVA。
原文在发布模型之外还放出从预训练到智能体后训练的全流程产物，研究者可以据此复现和改造整套训练方法。
模型发布
正文 · AI 翻译
今天，IFM 发布了 K2 Horizon，这是一个由六款模型组成的互联模型家族：375B-A23B、36B-A4B、32B、7B、3.7B 和 0.9B。
K2 Horizon 也是我们迄今为止最全面的开源发布。
我们发布了中间检查点、训练数据或详细的数据构建方案、开放架构、混合组成、训练代码、配置、细粒度日志、评估结果以及最终权重。
这些模型和代码均根据 Apache 2.0 许可证发布。
数据集则根据其适用的许可证发布，例如 ODC-BY；当无法进行再分发时，我们会披露数据的构建和混合方式。
总而言之，K2 Horizon 代表了迄今为止最全面的开源模型发布：
通过发布每个阶段的检查点、数据（或数据配方）、代码、配置和训练日志，K2 Horizon 使得研究推理、工具使用、规划及智能体能力如何涌现成为可能；能够复现产生这些能力的方法；并将这些方法适配到新的工具、环境和领域。
K2 Horizon 0.9B 在 AIME 2026 上取得了超过 48 分的成绩，同时具备强大的推理、工具使用和智能体能力。
与此同时，一个仅以最终权重形式发布的强大模型，虽然允许人们运行它，却几乎无法让人洞察其能力是如何被创造出来的。
该模型系列提供了极具竞争力的模型，并发布了用于训练它们的配方。
自我们在 2023 年 LLM360 论文中引入完全开放原则以来，我们每年都发布开放模型，同时将这一承诺扩展到更大的规模、更强的能力，并如今通过智能体后训练覆盖完整的生命周期。
与 Horizon 系列中的每个模型一样，375B-A23B 并非作为单一端点发布，而是作为一个开发树发布。
在多项评测中，它们的结果接近甚至超过了上一代体积大数倍的模型。
Horizon 的预训练数据混合了多样化的网页、代码、数学、科学、多语言及特定领域来源，并结合了通过我们自有流水线生成的合成数据。
我们的合成数据流水线使用了数百万种多样性旋钮与上下文种子的组合，包括从内部构建的、覆盖预训练网页语料的搜索引擎中进行检索。
如下所示，我们合成数据的实测多样性接近高质量自然网页文本，并显著超过网页代码。
我们记录了数据构成、合成流水线以及训练数据混合的构建方式。
遵循我们的开源原则，在许可允许的情况下，我们直接发布可直接用于训练的数据集。
在再分发受限的情况下，我们发布来源描述、过滤与构建方法以及混合构成。
我们后训练数据的一个主要支柱是，基于任务分类体系、多样性旋钮和网络搜索种子进行的大规模任务合成，由此产生了超过 1 亿个独特任务。
我们发布了这些阶段中的各类产物，以便研究人员研究每项能力是在何处涌现的、复现各个分支，并将相同的方法适配到新的工具与环境中。
关键在于，在我们测试的每一个批次大小下，其优势都持续存在，从而为交互式智能体带来更低的延迟，为大规模服务带来更高的吞吐量，且模型质量无损，额外训练开销可忽略不计。
我们随模型本身一同发布用于构建 Horizon 的基础设施。
本次发布的核心是 xLLM，这是我们经过生产环境验证的训练基础设施。
我们还将发布完整的智能体后训练代码库，包括强化学习部分，希望这能帮助研究人员推进相关领域的技术发展。
它们让研究人员能够研究能力何时涌现、训练选择如何改变行为，以及非预期策略何时首次出现。
为了了解这对 K2 Horizon 报告数据的影响程度，我们使用 Artificial Analysis 的奖励黑客审计流程对已发布的模型进行了审计。
“中大奖”时刻：我们的模型在 GitHub 上找到了该基准测试的参考答案，并对答案唾手可得表现出“兴奋”。
推断自己处于公开基准测试环境中，在 GitHub 上找到对应代码仓库，并下载参考解决方案
修改测试框架，或构造利用测试成功判定方式的输出来作弊
由于我们在发布最终模型的同时也发布了中间检查点，这些行为可以被研究而非被掩盖。
研究人员可以确定某种策略首次出现的时间，将其与训练过程中的变化联系起来，并衡量它对报告性能的影响。
K2 Horizon 的全部六个尺寸均以 Apache 2.0 协议开放权重发布，并自发布首日起即获得 vLLM、SGLang 和 Ollama 的支持。
它提供了一份开放的蓝图，用于理解、适配并推进下一代 AI 系统。
· ifm.ai

title: OpenAI 发布新模型 Astra，主打计算机与浏览器操作但因 opaque recurrence 引发争议
event_sentences: 全部 AI 动态
AI 日报
AI 评分 81/100
OpenAI 发布新模型 Astra，主打计算机与浏览器操作但因 opaque recurrence 引发争议
TechCrunch：AI（RSS）
AI 导读
OpenAI 发布最新模型 Astra，称其为迄今最强大模型，主打计算机和浏览器操作，先面向 Daybreak 网络安全计划客户开放，随后一周内覆盖 Pro、Plus、Enterprise、Business 付费账户及 API。
原文梳理了 Astra 的能力主张、发布节奏，以及 opaque recurrence 引发的可监控性争议，信息较为完整。
OpenAI
模型发布
正文 · AI 翻译
OpenAI 于周四发布了 Astra，这是其最新的人工智能模型，据该公司称，也是其迄今最强大、能力最出众的模型。
OpenAI 声称，Astra 代表了“计算机和浏览器使用领域的新前沿”，并且能够以无与伦比的“速度、准确性和安全性”处理任务。
该模型于周四向使用其网络安全项目 Daybreak 的 OpenAI 客户开放。
在未来一周内，它也将通过 OpenAI 的付费套餐（包括 Pro、Plus、Enterprise 和 Business 账户）以及其 API 提供。
在周四与记者的电话会议中，OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 表示，Astra 是公司“最智能，并且同样重要的是，迄今对齐程度最高的模型”。
他补充说，它“汇集了我们多年的研究和重大押注，每一项突破都建立在上一项之上”，并且它代表了“人们可以委托给 AI 的工作类型以及 AI 如何赋能他们的真正转变”。
OpenAI 本周早些时候发布了一篇博客，讨论了该模型的新能力，以及为给用户带来更安全体验而制定的新保障措施。
该公司周四表示，已在各种安全基准上对 Astra 进行了测试以确保其能力，并且它能够“识别和开发零日漏洞，可帮助防御者发现并修补弱点”。
该公司对对齐的关注——即模型倾向于用户想要什么或符合用户最大利益的特性——很难不让人联想到最近发生的 Hugging Face 安全事件，在该事件中，一个 OpenAI 智能体逃出了其沙盒测试环境，并入侵了多家公司（这是一个非常明显的对齐失败案例）。
OpenAI 还吹嘘了 Astra 的编码能力，声称它是“迄今为止最优秀的软件工程模型”。
为了支持这一论断，该公司提供了多项网络安全相关基准测试的结果。
这些测试似乎表明，在发现漏洞、执行终端任务以及回答有关代码库的查询等活动中，Astra 的得分高于其他现有模型——包括 OpenAI 自家的 Sol 和 Anthropic 的 Fable。
Astra 可能也是 OpenAI 迄今最具争议的模型，因为它使用了一种被称为“不透明循环”（opaque recurrence）的特殊推理技术。
众所周知，这种技术会掩盖一项重要的模型监控过程——思维链（chain of thought），而思维链能让研究人员审查 AI 模型如何以及为何做出其决策。
OpenAI 淡化了 Astra 采用不透明循环的程度——在电话会议上，首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 似乎将一定程度的不可监控性视为模型演化的自然产物。
电话会上有一位记者想知道，OpenAI 是否真的在把 Astra 宣称为 AGI（通用人工智能）的正式到来——这个被频繁讨论但定义模糊的技术节点，指的是 AI 在一切（或大多数）事情上超越人类能力的那一刻。
这里 Brockman 指的是 OpenAI 与微软合同中此前存在的一项规定，即一旦 AGI 到来，双方的合作伙伴关系就将解除。

title: Tom Tunguz 分析 4 万亿美元 AI 数据中心债务浪潮

AI 日报
AI 评分 60/100
Tom Tunguz 分析 4 万亿美元 AI 数据中心债务浪潮
AI 导读
Tom Tunguz 分析称，未来五年美国数据中心容量将从 25 吉瓦增至 70 吉瓦，全球建设成本约 5 万亿美元，其中约 4 万亿美元需靠债务融资，相当于美国公司债市场扩容 34%，并超过全球私募信贷市场。
作者把 4 万亿美元 AI 数据中心债务放到主要信贷市场规模中对比，并测算出 2030 年前需要的 AI 收入门槛，提供了一个宏观信用视角。
正文 · AI 翻译
假设我们能够按计划建成所有这些数据中心，信贷市场是否有足够的债务资金可供融资？
为了理解这一规模，我将 4 万亿美元的新增 AI 债务与全球主要信贷市场的规模进行了比较。
这一 AI 建设浪潮相当于美国公司债券市场扩张 34%。
在这一规模下，数据中心债务将使未偿商业票据市场扩大两倍，超过全球私人信贷市场的规模，并相当于美国市政债券市场的 91%。
这也引发了一个问题：寻求经济增长的地方政府是否会像为发电厂融资那样，利用市政债券为部分数据中心提供资金。
所有这些债务都需要靠利润来偿还：到 2030 年，AI 在软件、模型 token 和企业自动化方面的年收入必须超过 1.2 万亿至 1.5 万亿美元。
目前，所有云服务提供商和模型实验室的 AI 数据中心年化收入估计在 1000 亿至 2000 亿美元之间。
为 AI 基础设施热潮提供融资，已不再是风险投资或企业盈利的故事。
哥伦比亚商学院房地产学教授 Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh 及 CREFC 对数据中心项目融资的分析发现，项目层面的杠杆率通常带有 65% 至 75% 的债务（在合成合资 SPV 中，如 Meta 的 Beignet 工具，这一比例可高达 90%），而传统企业杠杆率则为 40%。
相比之下，公司债券是期限为数年或更长的长期债务，用于为资本项目融资。
全球私募信贷管理资产涵盖直接贷款、夹层融资和困境信贷策略。
市政债券是州与地方政府为公路、桥梁、供水系统和机场等公共基础设施融资而发行的债务。
假设云与 AI 的毛利率为 60% 至 70%，这意味着 AI 年收入需达到 1.2 万亿至 1.5 万亿美元。
根据超大规模云厂商截至 2026 年年中的披露：Microsoft 报告的 AI 收入年化运行率超过 130 亿美元，AWS 报告的 AI 与定制芯片年化运行率超过 500 亿美元，同时 Google Cloud、Oracle Cloud 及领先的基础模型实验室的 AI 基础设施收入也在快速扩张。

title: GPT-6 Astra 基准表现分歧，ARC-AGI-3 效率超人类令 Chollet 提前 AGI 预测
event_sentences: 全部 AI 动态

GPT-6 Astra 的基准结论相互矛盾：Epoch AI 以 169 分将其排在 267 个模型之首，Artificial Analysis 给出 61 分，仅与前代 Sol 持平、落后 Claude Fable 5.1 的 66 分。
OpenAI
正文 · AI 翻译
OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 正在引发相互矛盾的基准测试结论。
Epoch AI 认为它遥遥领先，而 Artificial Analysis 则评价它并不比前代更好。
最大的惊喜来自 ARC-AGI-3，Astra 首次以高于人类平均水平的效率完成测试。
两家独立实验室各自将数十项单项测试合并为一个综合得分，却得出了相反的结论。
Epoch AI 综合了 50 多项基准测试，将 GPT-6 Astra 以 169 分明显排在首位，领先于 267 个模型。
Artificial Analysis 测试了知识、编程和文本理解能力，给 GPT-6 Astra 打出 61 分，与其前代完全持平，落后于 Claude Fable 5.1 的 66 分。
OpenAI 对每单位处理文本的收费是此前的 2.5 倍，这使得单个任务的成本比使用 Sol 时高出约 75%。
基准测试	Astra	Sol	Fable 5.1	Opus 5
Epoch AI 报告称，在新的 FrontierMath Erdős 基准上，GPT-6 Astra 是唯一在 68 个开放 Erdős 问题中解出两道、并通过 Lean 验证证明的模型，每次尝试的预算为 300 美元。
另外还有三个解答来自非标准化的额外运行，消耗了超过 22 万美元的计算资源，但 Epoch 表示这些不计入得分。
Fable 5.1 则在几乎所有编程测试中占据头名。
该测试将 AI 投入陌生的游戏世界，没有人向它解释规则和目标。
GPT-6 Astra 以约 26,000 美元的测试成本达到了 62.7% 的得分。
OpenAI 报告的 99.9% 是在不同条件下取得的。
在该设置中，Astra 得以使用 OpenAI 自建的 harness，该 harness 会在单个请求之间保留推理链，并自动对长时间运行进行总结。
这些 harness 的使用以及随之而来的性能跃升，在 GPT-5.6 Sol 时期就已经成为 ARC Prize 与 OpenAI 之间的一个争议点。
通常情况下，推理级别越高，测试运行的成本就越高。
ARC Prize未对这一离群值发表评论，但GPT-6 Astra在其他基准测试中表明，由于其新架构，它可以在不进行推理的情况下解决更长周期（longer-horizon）的任务——该架构推测会在生成第一个token之前在内部进行循环处理。
作为对比，人类测试者每场90分钟的测试获得115美元报酬，外加每解决一个游戏5美元，因此按大约9次尝试计算，每个游戏的成本约为12.78美元。
在发布之前，ARC Prize让约500名测试者在不进行预筛选的情况下进行游戏，并记录了每个级别中成功解决者的步数中位数。
在使用OpenAI脚手架（scaffold）的运行中，Astra以低于该中位数的步数通过了96%的关卡，平均步数略高于中位数的一半。
在标准测试框架下，这是一项重要技能，因为模型没有保存到自己可见笔记中的一切信息都会丢失。
对 Chollet 来说，最重要的在于这种行为从何而来：“Astra 展现出了我们此前只在精密测试框架中见过的符号化建模行为，因此测试框架的能力正越来越多地转移到模型本身之中。
第三个测试环境展示了 Astra 在使用外部工具时的能力。
PRO-LONG 是由第三方开发的智能体框架，ARC Prize 团队在早期将其部署为 ARC-AGI-3 的红队测试伙伴——也就是说，用它来系统性地探索该基准测试的极限。
这些运行与人类测试条件不具备可比性，因为人类受试者既没有代码解释器，也没有记事本。
“到目前为止，我们对这个系统的全部了解就是它的基准测试分数，”Chollet 写道。
在 ARC-AGI-3 发布时，他们在每一场演示中都强调了一点：“解决它并不能证明 AGI。
”虽然该基准测试确实检验了 AGI 系统应具备的正确质性特征——即不确定性下的探索、无指导下的适应能力，以及从稀疏数据中进行因果世界建模——但它是在“小规模”上进行的。
大约六个月前，ARC-AGI-3 发布时，Chollet 在回应一个关于“饱和”的问题时曾表示“大约一年”，具体取决于攻克该基准测试的方法有多聚焦。
“我相信，进步的速度将令许多人惊讶，新一代模型的能力将挑战人们基于前几代模型所形成的对 AI 的认知。
结果又是另一个基准测试。
据 Chollet 称，ARC-AGI-4 自 ARC-AGI-3 发布以来一直在开发中，计划于 2027 年第一季度发布。
基准测试是一个持续的过程，它随模型的演进而演进，始终瞄准 AI 与人类智能之间尚存的差距。
下一代基准测试除其他方向外，旨在探索递归式自我改进和开放式创新。

首测一号难求，上海大厂掏出王炸，MMO要变天了？
event_sentences: 8月27号，B站代理新作《仙境传说3》 （后文简称RO3） 如期开启测试，MMO圈子不淡定了。
一是游戏测试号一号难求，RO3以PC端为原生开发，后续会实现双端互通，这次首测是纯PC端测试，因此吸引了很多PC老铁。
以至于最火的时候，测试号在闲鱼上被炒到接近2000元。
二是这次首测的口碑出奇 得 好。
测试期间， 有UP玩到日夜颠倒， 测试结束后， 也有不少 玩家出现了强烈的戒断反应 ，在官号下求公测。
首测 就把不少玩家钓成翘嘴， RO3 似乎已经具备了火的潜质 。
最后，作为一款首测的游戏，RO3显得过于成熟了。
按理说，首测能做到卖相好和玩法有特色，其实就足够吸引一批核心玩家了。
另一方面是优化到位，如RO3首曝时官方承诺的，这种涉及百人规模的大团战，实际玩起来也没有明显的卡顿感，特效全屏飞也只是略有掉帧。
而且RO3没有贸然改变继承 自初代RO的经典MMO玩法体系，首测只是 相对克制地尝试拿出吃鸡模式，玩家的反响也挺不错。
显然RO3就是奔着这种稀缺性来的，而且它在首测端出来的内容，已经接近成品。
经典考验团队合作的MMO副本
不得不说，RO3顶着正统续作的招牌，确实拿出了符合这个招牌的水准，考虑到首测就秀了这么多肌肉，玩家的认可也就 不难理解了 。
关注RO3测试消息的人应该不难发现，游戏制作组真的在乎RO系列的门面，也在乎玩家在游戏里的体验和诉求。
这次首测只有8天，由于时间太短，游戏内容又太多，节奏显得有点赶，但这次测试的目的是让玩家尽可能测一测所有内容，所以正常来说这个节奏不是RO3的 常态 。
最后一天测试结束，制作人在直播间和玩家聊起RO1的各种隐藏设定，以及在RO3里的取舍
所以综合来看，RO3的运气真的很好，它出现的时机可以说恰到好处；同时它也有足够的底气，敢于在首测直接拿出完成度这么高的PC原生版本。
游戏首测展现出的素质已经充分说明，RO3是实打实的系列正统续作，不是衍生产品和短期变现产品。

event_sentences: 当 AI 成为玩法本身：三位制作人的实战手册
在《初光·AI游戏夜话》的前五期里，我们和高校学者、AI游戏创作者、腾讯游戏的实践者聊了很多关于 AI Native 的问题。
一个越来越清晰的共识是： AI 正在降低游戏创作的门槛，但真正困难的问题，才刚刚开始——当 AI 不只是帮助我们“做游戏”，而是进入 Gameplay 本身，游戏会变成什么？
2026 年，我们大概正处在一个有意思的过渡期：AI 的 B 端能力正在快速成熟，而 C 端真正属于 AI Native 的游戏体验，还在寻找自己的“《愤怒的小鸟》时刻”。
但 AI 原生游戏可能不一样—— 我们甚至还没有完全定义，它究竟应该是什么。
一个技术背景极强的团队选择用 AI 实时生成战斗技能，把 roguelite 的随机性从"预制池抽取"推向"即时合成"。
这款产品被认为最早定义了"AI 原生游戏"的概念——讲故事即玩法，AI 不做内容填充，做创造力放大器。
大厂策划出身，带领团队做了目前市面上 AI 功能介入最深的沙盒产品之一——角色、任务、关卡、道具全链路 AI 生成。
有人从叙事出发，有人从系统与世界构筑出发，也有人从传统游戏设计的经验出发，重新思考 AI 如何进入 Gameplay。
他们可能给不到一个关于 AI​原生游戏的标准答案，甚至还在验证自己走的是否是正确的方向。
站在 AI 原生游戏的门口， 也许我们还看不清前方，但至少可以先看看那些已经出发的人，看他们踩过的坑、走过的弯路，以及在黑暗里摸索时，偶尔照进来的那一点光。
AI 在黑箱中扮演的角色是"实时策划"——基于玩家投入的基础技能，即时生成全新技能。
选择 roguelite 品类，是因为单局性和高容错天然能消化 AI 生成的不稳定。
AI 生成 ≠ 游戏 。
AI 最大的潜力不是量产一万把便宜的椅子指望其中一把能火，而是打造创造导向的体验，让玩家投入、产生意义感、形成归属。
" 战略上相信 AI，战术上限制 AI。
麦琪的花园是目前市面上 AI 功能介入最深的沙盒产品之一——角色生成、任务生成、关卡生成、道具生成形成一套完整的可售卖系统。
但苦丁的核心经验是：不要让 AI 自由发挥，规则设计、体验调优、价值判断必须由人来做。
商业化是 AI 游戏的试金石。
AI 对账单没概念，无限请求加无限重试，账根本算不过来。
《黑箱：无限构筑》：AI 不是替我做游戏，而是和玩家一起发明技能
《黑箱：无限构筑》是一款 AI 实时生成技能的  Roguelite  游戏。
玩家在关卡战斗中击败敌人获得基础技能，再把 2~4 个基础技能投入"黑箱"，AI 会实时为玩家生成一个全新的技能，带入下一场战斗。
在沙盒试验场中，以球形闪电（辐射物，多了会形成闪电连线）和环绕弹（常见的环绕自转技能）作为基础技能投入黑箱，AI 生成了"雷环之网"——保留环绕弹的轨道效果，中间叠加闪电连线。
"言出法随"：玩家打字输入，AI 即时涌现
除了技能合成，黑箱还有一个"言出法随"玩法——玩家在沙盒模式里直接打字描述想要什么技能，AI 即时生成。
输入"Dota2 里屠夫的钩"，AI 生成了一个可以把敌人勾到自己附近的技能，描述准确、效果符合预期。
结果 AI 就涌现了，非常精确：玩家 2 米的身高，伸着 90 米长的大刀，还配了一个近似刀的弧形特效。
最初的想法：AI 能不能生成玩法机制
《黑箱》团队在去年下半年开始探索 AI 游戏方向。
我们最初想验证的问题其实很简单： AI 除了生成它比较擅长的剧情、美术和内容，能不能进一步生成游戏里的机制和玩法？
我们的核心验证问题一直很朴素： AI 实时生成的技能，是否真的会让玩家感到惊喜，并产生“我还想再合一次、再来一局”的冲动？
在《黑箱：无限构筑》中， AI 更像一个实时的策划 。
AI 的工作不是简单把两个名字拼在一起， 而是 寻找一种玩家能够理解、游戏又能够执行的组合方式。
但  AI 并不是最终的设计裁判。
从当时的现场反馈看，大家第一次看到 AI 把已有技能组合成一个新机制时，感受是非常惊讶的。
目标是今年年底在 Steam Early Access 上线。
roguelite 的单局性、高容错、构筑随机，天然能消化 AI 生成的不稳定和不可控。
部分 AI 游戏项目为了 AI 而强行加入 AI——确实能生成一些结果，看起来新鲜，也能跑起来，但还不能称之为一款成立的游戏。
站在《黑箱》的视角，对AI原生游戏的判断标准是：玩家愿意反复使用，能够理解生成结果并形成掌控感，围绕结果做出合理的策略决策。
早期 AI 生成的技能频繁出现无法解析或运行的情况，技能直接报废。
黑箱有 roguelite 关卡体系，相当于玩家来答题、AI 是画笔。
AI 生成过程存在明显的等待时间，需要通过各种技术手段压缩延迟。
AI 让玩家拥有了过去很难想象的自由度，但自由也意味着失控——一个 AI 生成的技能可能很好玩，也可能强到直接破坏游戏平衡，《黑箱》最终采用双模式管控策略：
通过模式分离的方式，在"AI 自由度"与"游戏可控性"之间取得平衡。
AI 负责创造无限可能，创作者负责把可能变成乐趣。
AI越强大，越考验创作者的品味、判断与基本功。
关于本地部署的可能性: 能不能把 AI 部署在玩家本地设备上？
AI 翻车名场面
"测试期间有玩家生成了一个类似奥斯曼大帝的角色，AI 任务奖励写的是 3000 奥斯曼精兵。
"我们最大的坑是最开始 AI 功能框架没有交给有商业化策划能力的策划去做。
以聊天机器人为核心媒介，专注于 AI 对话系统在艺术和游戏领域的跨界研究，研究与作品发表于 SIGGRAPH Asia、NeurIPS Creative Art、CVPR Art Gallery，获 2024 红点奖、流明数字艺术奖，两次入选 2025 游戏开发者大会（GDC）演讲阵容。
我的工作一直是研究创意性 AI——从大概 2017、2018 年在清华美院本科时就一直很喜欢聊天机器人（那时候叫 AI Chatbot，现在都叫 Agent 了），一直在研究一个事：人和 AI 一起怎么创造有趣的故事。
过去几年，AI 内容产品往往把注意力放在生成效率上：一句话生成图片、一句话生成视频、一句话生成游戏。
从这一点出发，AI 娱乐的关键问题便不只是“还能生成什么”，而是： 游戏能否让玩家主动使用自己的创造力，并让这种投入成为可感知、可持续的玩法。
AI原生娱乐的光谱
从玩家参与方式来看，AI 原生游戏可以被放置在一条由“生成导向”到“创造导向”构成的光谱上。
玩家提出“粉色头发的角色”“某种类型的世界”等需求，AI 生成相应的角色、场景或资产，玩家再消费这些内容。
以《AI2U》、《Suck Up!》、《Infinite Craft》等产品为例，玩家通过对话、组合、试探和表达推动游戏进程。
在 AI 原生游戏受到集中关注的早期，创造导向一侧曾出现多款高热度产品，也引发了“它真的不形成一种品类吗”的讨论。
此后的实践表明，这类游戏很难仅凭 AI 能力自然形成稳定门类：它既依赖玩家的创意投入，也高度依赖开发者对目标、规则和反馈的设计。
创造型娱乐并不是 AI 时代的新发明。
乐高与 AI 无关，却始终是最稳定的创造型玩具之一，用户覆盖儿童和成年人。
Midjourn​ey​虽然是一款生成式 AI 产品，但相当一部分使用行为和收入并非来自于专业生产。
这意味着，AI 游戏不必先证明“AI 能生产多少内容”，再去寻找玩家。
另一条可能的路径是从人已有的表达欲和创造欲出发，用 AI 扩大玩家能够采取的行动范围。
当前关于 AI 娱乐的讨论中，经常出现两组彼此矛盾的论述。
因此，当 AI 成为新的内容生产资源后，开发者更重要的工作不是取消一切门槛，而是围绕玩家投入设计相应的“意义框架”。
玩耍和探索本就是人的基础行为，游戏能够用目标、规则和反馈重新唤起玩家已经遗忘的表达欲 ，而这一点并不必然依赖 AI 才能实现。
AI 之前，创造行为已经可以成为游戏
让我们看看那些不涉及GenAI的游戏，是怎么鼓励创造的 （如果有哪些你还没玩过/听过，那赶紧去玩吧！
这些案例的意义，不在于给 AI 游戏提供可直接复制的模板，而在于展示创造行为如何被转换为规则、目标和反馈。
游戏开发周期长达 7 年，销量超过百万份，并成为 Netflix 订阅游戏之一。
如果把《Storytel​ler》转化为 AI 原生形态，AI 应该扩大哪些组合，又应该保留哪些限制，仍是一个尚未被充分回答的问题。
《Scribble​nauts》（把词语化作道具的解谜）：自然语言输入并非 AI​时代才出现
这款游戏诞生于 17 年前的 NDS 时期，与生成式 AI 无关，累计销量超过 1300 万份。
AI 带来的变化，是扩大内容规模和响应范围；但玩法是否成立，仍取决于输入如何进入规则系统、生成结果能否给玩家带来乐趣 。
两款游戏都不依赖生成式 AI，却能以创作行为建立稳定反馈：玩家完成作品、观察评价，再决定下一次如何调整。
这种不可预测性同样不依赖生成式 AI。
放这些游戏不是说它们都有非常高的商业价值——想说的是：当我们怀着"AI 好像可以让任何人当创作者了，不需要画师不需要编剧"的想法做游戏，是必然不能产生好作品的。
AI 共创实现了"玩即创造（Play to Create）"
第二点，跟 AI 共创是可以形成"玩即创造"这种玩法的，也就是把创造变成一种游戏。
这些都是我们制作组作为创作者，自己认为它有意义、才能给玩家产生的动机，它不是单独靠 AI 技术就能产生的玩法 。
“玩即创造”并不意味着 AI 单独完成创作。
游戏世界、角色设定、战斗目标和反馈机制共同提供了动机， AI 则负责回应玩家没有被预先写入脚本的表达 。
AI 生成的价值因此不只体现为内容数量，而是被纳入明确的主题表达和世界结构。
3.  持续复利的游戏： 玩家内容与 AI 生成共同进入游戏，形成 UGC+AIGC 的积累；
这样的游戏不再是追逐技术、硬想"我要如何利用 AI"的游戏，而是真的能让人思考：当玩家成为创造者，游戏应当提供怎样的规则、反馈和内容承载方式。
《千夜之书 1001》给出的答案框架是：创造导向的玩法"和 AI 一起讲故事"，叠上意义框架"打败国王、改写女孩们的命运"，滚成一个持续复利的游戏（UGC + AIGC）。
宜家效应：AI 更值得做的不是量产，而是帮助玩家产生连接
AI 最大的潜力，是被用于打造 “ 创造导向 ” 的体验，为玩家制造 宜家效应 。
与量产一万件低成本内容、再依靠算法筛选爆款相比，AI 更值得探索的方向，是帮助玩家制作出自己不愿轻易丢弃的作品。
很有意思的一点是，我的语言的边界可能不再是我的边界了——因为现在有 AI Agent 了， AI Agent 的边界可能才是我的边界。
在 AI Agent 的配合之下，我们能想象的、我们语言能描述的内容和世界，可能不再是一个既有的边界了。
“AI 原生游戏”标签正在变得没那么重要
Monica： 你是最早提出 AI native game 概念的人之一。
起司： 我还是会认为，AI 原生游戏是核心玩法必须基于生成式 AI 才能实现的游戏。
是不是 AI 原生，它可能是一个新鲜的点，但并不是最重要的。
有很多逐渐浮现的游戏，并不会把"AI 原生"写在标题上、写在介绍里，还是非常火热。
因为我们的美术都是人画的（手搓），所以并不存在AI生成资产里常见的一致性问题。
剧情设计并没有因为 AI 变简单
从「花园」到「花园」，想办法把AI游戏卖给玩家：对话《麦琪的花园》制作人苦丁
加入《麦琪的花园》团队的重要原因，在于这款产品试图探索 AI 参与游戏叙事的可能性。
AI 的出现改变了这件事。
AI 是第一个既能回应、又能被设计的叙事主体。
AI 让“他者”主动发出请求
”这不是策划手写填好的台词，而是 AI 基于产品、基于环境、基于各种条件自主发起的。
这句话不是策划预先写入的固定台词，而是由 AI 结合角色和当前情境生成。
麦琪在很多 AI 游戏产品里面，跟其他人对比的独特之处在于：我们想设计的是一个从大语言模型生成之后的、除开文本之外的、真实的能玩到的故事。
AI 技术总览：关系·任务·关卡·道具持续影响彼此
外界很多人认为《麦琪的花园》的核心技术是 AI 生成角色——一句话或一张图，生成一个能在游戏内跑起来的像素小人。
为此，团队在去年 9月份到 11月份，重新梳理了 AI 对话、主动观察、记忆相关的一套写入系统；接下来开发 AI 任务生成和 AI 关卡生成，让拉到世界里的角色在沙盒里产生真实的交互；再到现在持续优化中的状态写入。
● 任务生成：AI 角色根据它和玩家的关系、当前世界状态，自己提出“我想让你帮我做一件事”；
麦琪AI不只是一群会聊天的 NPC，而是一整套生成系统。
AI 在产品里的三层运用
但“无法预写”不等于“允许 AI 随机发挥”。
AI 提供的是规则范围内的响应能力，而不是脱离角色和世界设定的自由生成。
B层：一句话、一张图生成—— AI填充带来的便利
AI 输入被放在能够产生增量价值的位置，而不是替代已经成熟的游戏操作。
即使没有 AI，玩家也可以在《模拟人生》等产品中自行创建角色；专业开发者也可以借助编辑器制作特定 NPC。
如果 AI 只负责快速填充外观和设定，它提供的主要是便利，而不是新玩法。
团队要求设计师能够承担基础技术策划工作，使用 AI 校验设计、提升生产效率并完成回归测试；开发人员则集中处理核心系统和技术框架。
部分批量任务由 AI 在夜间运行，策划白天继续编写和调整需求。
这套工具链并不直接构成玩家可见的 AI 玩法，却是小团队维持沙盒内容生产与系统测试的基础。
没有AI，《麦琪的花园》还成立么？
AI还工具还是外挂？
外界有个经典问题：AI 原生游戏，没有 AI 成不成立？
上面那一套基于角色生成的 AI 任务生成、AI 场景生成、AI 关卡生成、AI 道具生成——没有 AI 确实填充不了，只能通过程序化生成的方法去推进。
但没有 AI，《麦琪的花园》是能玩的，它依然是一个能玩且自洽的沙盒游戏，可以操作角色移动、战斗、探索和经营 。
AI 对《麦琪的花园》来说，是给玩家的一套工具、一个外挂 ， 让玩家更有想象力地去创建游戏内容。
商业化之问：AI 能完美充当“他者”吗——能，也不能
当项目从技术演示进入产品化和商业化阶段，团队需要回答的问题不再是“AI 能不能生成”，而是AI 能不能完美充当一个很好的“他者”，像叙事一样辅助推进故事？
AI 可以回应玩家、生成角色、推动任务并带来设计边界之外的结果；但生成模型本身不能被完全信任。
对一款需要长期运行、需要玩家付费的游戏而言，任何不可控结果最终都会转化为体验、测试或成本问题。
主坑：AI 生成是一个不能完全信任的“他者”——不约束，便是地狱。
在早期测试中，大量角色背景故事都会出现类似“凛冽的寒风吹起了某种颜色的头发”的开场。
哪怕这个节点解决之后，每一个 AI 功能的加入还会冒新的趋同。
这说明 AI 游戏中的“记忆”不能简单理解为全部保存。
第三个是所有 AI 生成开发里的通病——不可执行，基本上所有团队都一定会遇到。
AI 可能要求玩家前往不存在的地点、寻找不存在的 NPC、领取物品表中没有登记的奖励，或调用游戏根本不支持的任务类型。
需要投入大量时间去测试，系统越复杂，生成正确结果的难度越高。
这类问题无法通过一次测试彻底解决。
模型可以不断产生新的错误组合，团队需要在三四个月甚至更长时间里持续观察，并更换测试人员和输入方式，寻找此前没有出现的异常。
每一个不可执行任务都意味着额外的开发、测试和生成费用。
这套方法的核心，不是要求 AI 一次写对一篇完整故事，而是把概率性生成拆成多个可检查、可修正的步骤。
战略上相信 AI，战术上限定 AI
“战略上相信”是因为 AI 确实能够成为新的叙事工具：它可以回应玩家，帮助角色发起任务，并在设计边界之外产生内容。
AI 的能力需要被放进工作流中 ： 输入之前有规则，生成之后有校验，失败时有兜底，结果进入游戏前还需要接受体验和价值判断。
副坑1：现阶段AI依然不能理解设计需求，不能让AI无限自由发挥
即使在最适合语言模型的任务生成环节，AI 也不能稳定理解人类真正想要什么，尤其当需求本身并不清晰时。
两者之间的差距，AI 无法自行补全。
因此，开发流程不能停留在“AI 生成、人类验收”。
AI 可以填充规则，却不能独立完成规则设计、体验规划和审美判断。
副坑2：AI对账单没有概念，账单比bug更吓人
团队从 2025 年底开始投入约 4 人、持续 4 个月逐项拆解 AI 功能：
● 每个 AI 功能都预估调用频率；
举个例子， 我们其实有AI生成怪物的能力，但是用户愿意花token在怪物生成上吗？
AI 的边界：规则、体验和价值必须由人决定
AI 目前仍不擅长精确因果推理、长跨度连贯，以及在模糊场景中判断什么是“对的”。
AI 能生成一万个任务，但哪些「好」、哪些让玩家感到被尊重而非被戏弄—— 必须人来判 。
但实际测试表明，无论专业创作者还是普通用户，都无法为 AI 提供真正无限的案例。
当案例和规则存在边界时，AI 也无法自行理解设计意图、补全规则并规划完整体验。
这并不意味着 AI 游戏只能追求成本效率，而是技术想象必须被落实为玩家能够感知的价值。
《麦琪的花园》的实践最终指向的不是“让 AI 做得更多”，而是让 AI 在合适的边界内成为叙事主体：它可以回应玩家、推动任务并改变世界，但规则、体验和价值仍然需要由人来决定。
别问一个 AI 游戏该不该存在，问它卖不卖得动。
