title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
event_sentences: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series.

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

This was a year after The Last of Us came out in 2013. It was a hot property, as the game was a critical and a commercial success for Naughty Dog and Sony. With Sony also owning and operating its own film studio, all the synergies were there for Sony to make a Last of Us film.

Neil Druckmann, who directed The Last of Us game, confirmed in 2014 that the movie would adapt the story of The Last of Us , as opposed to branching off in some other way. At the time, Druckmann said the movie would "take into account the unique properties of film," but he stressed it was early days and the team hadn't yet mapped out how it would condense the game's story into a two-hour film. In 2015, Druckmann confirmed he had written a second draft of the movie's script, which he said contained "pretty big changes" from the source material.

It was also at this time that Druckmann said a table read had already taken place with "a bunch of actors," though he did not name any outright. Game of Thrones star Maisie Williams was said to be a frontrunner to play Ellie , and many people said that casting was perfect. Williams herself confirmed she met with Druckmann and Raimi about it, but remarked at the time that there was no script or director at that point. Williams, who was 17 at the time, also joked at the time that she hoped Sony would make the movie quickly because, "If they make it in 30 years, they can't have a 40-year-old Ellie." Kaitlyn Dever was also considered for the role of Ellie in the film , and, spoiler alert: Dever would go on to play Ellie's adversary, Abby, in the HBO TV show.

In 2016, Druckmann said the movie hadn't progressed for "over a year" at that point . "It kind of entered development hell like these things tend to do," he said. The movie also never had a director signed on, nor was there a cast or a release date.

This wouldn't be the last time a Naughty Dog film project was subject to development hell, as the Uncharted movie is a very infamous example of this , but that did eventually come together for release in 2022 after a decade of development.

Druckmann said in an interview with Sacred Symbols that movie executives told him to "make it bigger, make it more like World War Z," and he pushed back against this. "Go make World War Z. Why make The Last of Us? The Last of Us is not that," he said. Conversely, Druckmann said HBO boss Casey Bloys told him, "'Do as much action as you need to, and no more. Do as much violence as you need to, and no more. Here, we sell drama.'"

Druckmann said he got the opposite notes when The Last of Us was envisioned as a feature film. It's not a stretch to imagine this is part of the reason why Naughty Dog opted for a TV show instead of a film, in addition to there being a more supportive and understanding team at HBO to produce and back the show.

Druckmann also said HBO approached the source material with "such reverence and artistry," ensuring Naughty Dog would be involved in the process too. This is not always the case, of course, as the Baldur's Gate TV series at HBO does not involve Larian Studios . Druckmann also mentioned that HBO was supportive of the many changes to the source material that Druckmann and writer/showrunner Craig Mazin made.

Appearing on Logically Speaking in 2024, Druckmann said the movie version of The Last of Us "would have been awful." He said, "It would have been one of those bad adaptations had we finished that one."

In a recent interview with GamesBeat , Druckmann said he changed his mind about how to approach such projects. Whereas in 2014 he said The Last of Us movie would be an adaptation of the game, in 2016, he said Naughty Dog had "evolved our feelings" about adaptations.

"As time goes on, we are not excited by a direct adaptation of a story for a game into a movie,” Druckmann said. “We have told that story well, cinematically. The idea for The Last of Us film was to be a direct adaptation. I don’t want that movie to be made."

Druckmann indeed got his wish, and that movie was never made. The TV series with HBO, meanwhile, premiered in January 2023, and its first season--starring Bella Ramsey as Ellie and Pedro Pascal as Joel--was a huge success in terms of critical reception and viewership numbers. A second season aired in 2025, and was similarly successful, though not quite to the same degree. A third-- and potentially final --season is in the works now, but Druckmann dropped out to focus on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet and other projects at Naughty Dog ( maybe The Last of Us 3? ).

title: D&D is getting a Netflix series about Strahd, involving the director of The Prisoner of Azkaban, and I honestly think this could work great
event_sentences: In the one Strahd campaign I played in, my first encounter with the man involved him bleeding our cleric and making my thief drink his blood—so, you know. Normal.

Anyway, per Deadline , we'll be getting a fully-fledged live action Netflix series about him dubbed Ravenloft—after the wider set of domains that darklords like Mr. Zarovich himself enjoy dominion over. It's being helmed by writer and executive producer John August and executive producer Alfonso Cuarón.

The report reads: "Described as a prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance, Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread tackle adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue.

"At its heart, the series follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains."

title: A popular streamer turned down a 6-figure deal to play Arc Raiders because 'the game frustrated me so much'
event_sentences: Everyone has a price. Maybe it's $100, maybe it's $1,000, maybe it's for someone to see your innate value as a human being, or maybe it's $1,000,000. Popular streamer TimTheTatman recently revealed what it would take to get him to go back to Arc Raiders , and spoilers, it's not the third option.

There was apparently an ad deal floating around for the Arc Raiders and Subway collab, which TimTheTatman was approached for, but did not entertain. "I did say no to six-figures with Arc Raiders, I did," he revealed in a stream earlier this week. "I said 'No thank you'. And it was the Subway Arc Raiders ad. I said I just can't do it, I'm sorry."

(Image credit: Embark) This was met with the exact response you'd expect with people being baffled that he'd ever think of turning down such a lucrative offer. "That's kind of the funny part of being in a streamer position," TimTheTatman continued. "People say 'you're a fucking sellout' but then in the same breath I said I passed on six-figures from Arc Raiders and people are like 'you're fucking stupid'."

He revealed that he does actually have a price to play Arc Raiders again: they'd just have had to add another zero onto the offer. "If that Arc Raiders deal was seven-figures—hey boys welcome back to Arc Raiders and Subway, right, you see what I'm saying? 100% we're going back. But it's just for me, the game frustrated me so much—I got frustrated so much with that game, I just don't want to play it ever again. Even to a point where six-figures isn't going to get me back on it."

I can't say I'm surprised. Arc Raiders is in a bit of a rough spot right now, especially for streamers, what with all the cheating and stream sniping. Embark Studios' executive producer Aleksander Grøndal recently admitted the shortcomings of Arc Raiders and promised that its upcoming major update Frozen Trails will reset the game and provide enough incentive to get players to come back, though—even if they don't get a six-figure deal to do it.

title: I have filled GTA 5 with realistic Los Angeles snow
event_sentences: Okay, two things. First: Los Santos Customs will be taking a hiatus next week, as I spend nine days in a row sleeping and attempting to develop the antibodies to counter whatever exotic German illness it is I acquired at Gamescom 2026 .

(Image credit: Rockstar) I have installed WinterV Beta , with the aim of making Grand Theft Auto 5's weather a little more interesting than it usually is. The pitch is simple: what if there was snow? Well, reader, having played a little GTA 5 with WinterV Beta, I can assure you that there very much is snow. Plus, all the world's lighting takes on a kind of a sickly, ochre hue, which is also just like LA.

From the sky: flurries of flakes. On the roads: cars covered in a sheen of powder, tyre-chains inexplicably equipped (the snow does not, in my version of GTA 5 where a significant chunk of the exterior map has absconded to the phantom zone, settle). In the air: a crisp winter chill. Santa Claus is coming to town; fire a truck at him .

title: The Blood of Dawnwalker endings and how to get each one
event_sentences: It took me quite a while to work out all The Blood of Dawnwalker endings . Similar to The Witcher 3, there are a fair few different options, each with a number of variables that can change based on your choices. There are also some secret endings to discover.
Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers for just about everything, you've been warned. Here's each ending, how they work, plus a short explainer about the epilogue and its different outcomes.

All endings, except for one of the secret ones, involve an epilogue sequence which runs through decisions you made throughout the game—and there are some big differences, but I'll explain all of those in the epilogue section at the end if you're curious. Side note, make sure to have 800 Denarius on hand for any ending involving the epilogue , as the church will ask for a donation and you can give your sister Yanna a dowry.

This ending sees Coen assault Griefberg Castle by himself at either day or night, depending on which of the approaches you take. If you do fight Ambrus, Bakir, or Xanthe in the assault, you won't be able to drink their Vrakhir blood and gain their abilities if it's daytime, or invite them in, and will instead just kill them.

You can either fight Brencis here, or make a deal with him if you agree to bow and give up either Crake and the Manumits, or Lacra, though if it's the former, you'll have to go their hideout and mark it, as in the A Deal With the Devil ending (I'll explain that one in its dedicated section below).

This is genuinely one of my favorite endings—Vale Sangora becomes independent and there's some degree of lawlessness, but the Manumits protect the valley from the worst enterprising ruffians. You can read a proclamation on a tree in Laslea explaining that Svartrau city council plans to petition Bohemia, Hungary, or Poland to join their realms in the spring.

Since there are no more Vrakhiri, the plague returns, the Uriashi return to their villages, but Christianity also returns, the cathedral is restored, and Father Florin becomes a saint. I'm sure you're thinking " That's a good ending??" but just wait until I explain the others.
In this ending, Crake explains that Catalin Dragosti (the son of Vale Sangora's former tyrant) is waiting outside the valley with an army, and you attack Eastridge Outpost to let him in.

After this, you'll continue to the banquet hall, with or without Crake, and will fight Brencis in a room with your family tied to chairs. Unlike the A Lone Wolf's Hunt ending, you can't make a deal with Brencis at this point, since you can't stop Catalin and his army. You'll fight and defeat Brencis, invite him in, or leave him in hell, and the epilogue in Laslea will play.

You'll assault Eastridge outpost so Catalin Dragosti's army can enter the valley Rebel Wolves If you choose to not save Catalin in the throne room, Marat will die instead Rebel Wolves This is one of the worst endings in my opinion. Catalin Dragosti undertakes a campaign of retribution against anyone he sees as having helped the Vrakhiri, burning entire districts of Svartrau and filling the castle dungeons. As you see in a note on a tree in Laslea, he also imposes a large tax and encourages people to inform on each other. The epilogue also mentions his mercenary army loots and pillages towns whenever it feels like it.

Alongside Lacra, you enter the Griefberg Castle dungeons via the ancient ruins below and destroy Brencis's ritual, before ascending through the castle to face Brencis himself. The key variables here are that in smashing the ritual, Lacra unleashes hell on the castle. Corpses start coming back to life, huge chunks of the castle are ripped up into the air, and the prisoners lose their minds.
If you betray Lacra and choose your family , she'll fight Brencis, but he'll win and drink her blood. The outcome here is the same as the A Deal With The Devil ending (explained below).

Lacra disrupting the ritual messes up the castle Rebel Wolves Your family almost get killed by the red roots Rebel Wolves You can make a deal with Brencis and betray Lacra, or fight him together Rebel Wolves This ending isn't a particularly good one—as with A Lone Wolf's Hunt, Vale Sangora becomes independent for a time, the Manumits defend it, and both Christianity and the plague return. The negative here is basically everyone in the castle dies and it remains a cursed hellscape.

You can also choose to kill Brencis here, though spilling any blood summons the dead, and you'll have to fight him with a million ghosts trying to get in the way. This is also inadvisable because you leave your father, Pieter, to the mercy of all the angry spirits you summon, which will lead to his death. Before you can agree to Brencis's deal, your father picks the absolute worst moment to trip over and hurt himself, summoning a legion of ghosts you have to fight through with Brencis to escape and save him.
The main difference is that the epilogue is, understandably, short as hell because you didn't do anything in the game.
The Blood of Dawnwalker's epilogue explained
Certain characters showing up in the town.
Below I'll run through the epilogue section post-Laslea, which shows you a series of tableaus you can examine. These explain the outcomes of various quests and choices you made:
The Uriashi will either retreat to the mountain or stay.
The plague will return or remain absent based on whether Brencis remains in power.
Is killed and sent to Anachora by Brencis and his court if he remains in power.
Is canonized and made a saint. This might only happen if you complete his A Hero's End quest.
Is publicly burned alive if Brencis remains in power.
It remains cursed and filled with undead.
This tableau only shows up if you spared Xanthe during her The Cycle of Love quest (which you get by angering her). It basically explains how Xanthe keeps murdering women to keep Chariklea alive.

title: Me: You can now run DLSS 5 on AMD GPUs. My RX 9070 XT: Please stop, it hurts us
event_sentences: Another day, another DLSS 5 story that actually kinda doesn't involve Nvidia itself doing anything, because it seems now AMD GPU owners can get in on the act. A new homebrew app has been released on Github that will allow you to run the DLSS Neural Rendering feature on a Radeon GPU. I've tried it and it works, but damn does it hurt the poor Radeon silicon.

Initially Windows flagged it as containing a virus, but I did some checking around with VirusTotal and seemingly the Defender flag is a machine learning false positive. Probably. But even then I still struggled to have it running happily.

I am not entirely sure what I did wrong, but when I enabled the feature in-game all I got was a black output where the 3D world ought to be, even though the HUD and game kept on running. After some file deletion, redownloading, verifying of integrity (mine and Cyberpunk's), and a rollback of my AMD Adrenalin drivers, I finally got it working. Kinda. I mean it's still kinda crashy, and I can only now launch Cyberpunk 2077 directly from the .exe file rather than from Steam, but it works.

Now it's worth noting that the fact it is running at all on AMD GPUs is impressive on its own, but it's not going to make any Radeon graphics card owners any happier about it when they're getting unplayable frame rates out of their new ill-gotten pretties. An 85% performance drop is not sustainable. Nice for screenshots though, eh?

title: The White House launches online 'arcade' with its own takes on Tetris and other popular games, and it's as rotten as you'd expect
event_sentences: We'll set aside the question of "why?" for now and get straight to the games, beginning with Flappy Bill, a game in which you fly a bald eagle down the National Mall. It's not clear whether the bird's name is actually Bill because it's also carrying a bill, which my young years of being exposed to Schoolhouse Rock from across the border taught me is part of the US lawmaking process, or at least used to be before they decided that having the president do everything by fiat is more efficient or something. In any event, it's an entirely unremarkable Flappy Bird clone, innocuous but about as much fun as tying a shoelace.

(Image credit: White House) Moving on: The third game in the White House Arcade is called Rio Run, a recreation of a "border patrol along the Rio Grande" based on the ancient classic Snake. As a balding white guy in a suit, you pick up brown-skinned people one at a time, each of whom joins a train behind you wearing shackles and an orange jumpsuit. Once the game ends, when you run into a wall or your train of prisoners, they're all deported and you're encouraged to try again. Lovely.

I don't really know what to make of the fourth game. Supply Line, as it's called, charges you to "sort the school line to make America healthy again" by letting 'good' food ride a conveyor belt to the school lunch box, while chucking 'bad' food—anything with coloring, additives, sealed packages, or seed oils—into the "reject" box.
Also, reading labels is apparently bad, according to a sign with a red strike through it. Ain't that America? For you and me, baby.

In my country we encourage reading the labels. (Image credit: White House) The fifth and final game on the White Hours Arcade tour is Trump Savings Tycoon, a game about filling your kids' Trump Accounts , which are basically retirement savings accounts for children, backed by money from various super-wealthy individuals like Jensen Huang and Michael Dell who may or may not have anything to gain from big-money sycophancy.

The obvious question is, as noted earlier, is why? Who are these games for? I think the answer in one sense is that they're for no one in particular, but are instead just another wave in the flood of sewage pumped out every day by the US president and his administration. Over the last couple years, the US government has posted numerous gaming-related memes , video clips , and AI generated images to promote its leader and his agenda.
But more broadly, this effort is targeted at the young male gamer demographic, at least in part to leverage the political influence it first demonstrated during the Gamergate harassment campaign.

"A big chunk of the modern political right in America emerged from Gamergate. The hate movement was brought into the political fold by Steve Bannon and Breitbart after it showed how it is possible to wash extreme talking points into the mainstream political environment. Its members became online 'shock troopers' for Trump, as well as becoming foundational figures in the alt-right and nuttier fringes like QAnon. And as they've grown up, the almost entirely young men who made waves back in 2014 are now in positions of power on the right. This allows them to shape the online narrative, encouraging them to reach a fresh generation of men through an increasingly fragmented social media ecosystem that allows transgressive macho 'manosphere' content to trend."

While the owners of properties used in past posts have thus far opted to stay silent, The Tetris Company did obliquely suggest that it might take a more aggressive approach. Following an Instagram post in which the company said "we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it added, "PS: The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of Build the Wall. PPS: We take copyright infringement very seriously."

As completely crappy as all of this is on every possible level, it seems likely there's more to come. A currently unoccupied sixth game window on the White House Arcade page says "a new adventure awaits," and encourages interested followers to "stay tuned." I've reached out to the White House for comment on the new virtual arcade and will update if I receive a reply.

title: After a massive 2021 office expansion, Bungie is now trying to sublease its 211,000 square foot headquarters
event_sentences: In 2021, as studio CEO Pete Parsons cited the company's recent "tremendous growth and opportunity," Bungie announced its plans for a massive expansion to its Bellevue, Washington headquarters . The campus embiggening, which internal sources have reportedly described as costing "hundreds of millions" of dollars, more than doubled the size of Bungie's offices from 84,000 square feet to just under 211,000.

Now, after five and a half years of spending sprees, publisher acquisitions, stumbling product launches, project cancellations, and repeated mass layoffs, Bungie appears to be seeking subletters for the goliath game development headquarters it's no longer capable of filling.

According to a 10-page leasing brochure reviewed by The Game Post , Bungie is seeking interested renters to sublease its expansive headquarters, listing its 210,984 square feet as a "turn-key" production facility. In addition to expected office fixtures, the listing also features a dedicated lobby, gym and exercise facilities (including a rock climbing wall), a motion-capture studio, a cafe, catering space, and a private exterior patio.
While the brochure didn't directly identify the studio, a statement provided to press verified that Bungie was actively pursuing a sublease.

"Bungie is exploring options to sublease its campus in Bellevue, Washington. The studio transitioned to a digital-first model several years ago, and this move reflects the team's evolving workplace needs and the effectiveness of its remote collaboration," Bungie said. "Bungie will continue to maintain a physical office presence in Bellevue."

Bungie formally adopted remote work eligibility for most of its roles in 2022, following the studio's shift to work-from-home development during the COVID-19 lockdown years—effectively defeating the purpose of its office expansion due to circumstances that would have been impossible to predict during its early planning stages.

Bungie wasn't the only games company to make ill-fated investments during the height of the pandemic: Analysts have repeatedly cited overly-ambitious expansions and acquisitions—propelled by the COVID era's low interests rates and explosion of at-home entertainment revenue—as one of the driving forces behind the games industry's brutal cost-cutting in the years that followed.

Bungie's overextension, however, was particularly drastic. After Sony purchased the studio for $3.6 billion in 2022 , Bungie leadership embarked on a rampant hiring spree, adding hundreds of developers to the payroll to fill out development teams for a swath of simultaneous incubation projects—projects that would prove unsustainable as the impact of Covid waned and revenues started to tumble across the industry.

A mass layoff followed in October 2023 , affecting roughly 100 employees. The next round cut 220 developers in July 2024 as fallout from Bungie leadership having reportedly "overstated their studio’s financial prospects to Sony," leading to a dire enough fiscal outlook that even the success of Destiny 2's Final Shape expansion couldn't salvage it. As Sony intensified its oversight amidst the mounting turmoil, Bungie's leadership began to abandon ship, culminating with Pete Parsons departing the studio in 2025—presumably in one of his vintage collector cars .

Bungie staff ultimately suffered another sweeping layoff in June 2026, with most of the Destiny team losing their jobs in the aftermath of Destiny 2's end of live service. At peak employment, Bungie's staff numbered over 1,600; in July 2024, Parsons said the studio numbered around 850 . The WARN notice issued for this June's layoff indicated at least 292 jobs were affected.
In other words, if all of Bungie's remaining employees gathered in its office, there would be fewer than 600 people to fill its 211,000 square feet.

title: 'Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity': Miami-Dade County Sheriff comes out hard against a proposed GTA 6 collab with Rockstar
event_sentences: Officials with Miami-Dade County have held talks with Rockstar about using facilities and landmarks in the county to promote the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 , according to a recent report by The Miamian , saying it could represent "a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience." Just one problem: the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office is dead-set against it.

The Miamian report (via RPS ) says the county submitted a pitch deck to Rockstar on June 29, after which staff had "some conversations with Rockstar about potential opportunities around the launch of GTA 6," said Carlos Suarez, a spokesperson for Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava.

"Nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any idea would have to go through the appropriate review and approval process," Suarez said. "Given Miami-Dade's clear influence on the game, we think there could be a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience."

Miami-Dade is the inspiration for Vice City in the GTA series, and by "inspiration" I mean it basically is Vice City, although Miami exists as a separate city in the game's fiction. Vice City will serve as a central location in GTA 6, and will represent the seat of Vice-Dale County, much as the city of Miami is the county seat of Miami-Dade. Given that, the campaign makes obvious sense, and most of the ideas floated don't sound too overly disruptive.
A display aircraft wrapped in Vice City logos and a GTA 6-inspired baggage claim at Miami International Airport
Vice City signage and colors at the Metromover and Metrorail transit stations

A Vice City Radio Lab at the city's main library, providing access to recording, editing, and digital media equipment to support "music production, podcasting, oral histories, neighborhood storytelling, sound engineering, video-game development, and other creative programming, while reflecting the central role that music and radio play in the GTA experience
The pitch also includes ideas for Rockstar funding permanent upgrades to county infrastructure:
The big stumbling block, of course, is that the GTA games are the polar opposite of civic-minded and wholesome, and that's led Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz to speak out against the idea.

"Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity," Cordero-Stutz told the Miami Herald . "Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office work every single day to prevent."

Miami-Dade Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez also spoke out against the idea: "We should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence."

The sheriff isn't wrong. GTA games have always been notoriously violent: Former attorney Jack Thompson , at one time the videogame industry's foremost nemesis, spent years campaigning hard against the games and publisher Take-Two Interactive before he was finally disbarred for his relentless antics and misconduct.

But the game industry, and its audience, have matured in the 25 years (that's right, look it up) since Grand Theft Auto 3 changed everything: GTA is still steeped in criminal violence, but the shock factor—and the hand-wringing over it—are long gone. These days it's completely mainstream, as evidenced by the performance of the GTA 6 reveal showcase on Netflix, which was the platform's biggest show of the week.

title: Celebrate Labor Day by playing Civilization 7 for free
event_sentences: Civ 7's had kind of a rough go of things since it launched in early 2025. It made some big changes to the formula that didn't go over well with a significant portion of the fan base, the UI was almost universally unpopular, and performance was dodgy.

Firaxis has been banging away on it ever since, to mixed results: A major update released in May brought a big bump in player numbers on Steam, but the reactions expressed via Steam reviews were almost literally split down the middle. Civ 7's Steam rating remains "mixed," with only 48% positive user reviews, while concurrent player numbers on the platform are still running neck-and-neck with the 16-year-old Civilization 5.

title: As Wardogs blows past 200k Steam concurrents, its developers are prepared for the day 'hype dies down'
event_sentences: The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up. Steam concurrents are a useful metric for gauging a game's general popularity, but they paint an incomplete picture. They're a single data point, yet have become the flimsy scaffolding on which the internet builds elaborate headcanon about a game's quality, viability, or deadness. Sometimes dogpiling is so successful, and the resulting perception so difficult to fight, that simply saying a game is dead is enough to help kill it.

It's a trend that annoys me to no end, so it's refreshing to see a developer speaking openly about concurrents—both about how many it considers "healthy," and why it's normal for the number to rise and fall. It's been a recurring topic for Wardogs developer Bulkhead, whose closed beta surpassed 200,000 concurrents today on Steam. Responding to a TimTheTatman clip on X, CEO Joe Brammer spoke on the milsim's unexpected popularity, and its inevitable (but healthy) decline.

"Wardogs will continue to lose players for months as the hype dies down," Brammer wrote . "Doesn't make it a bad game or even a problem, we planned for 5k players concurrent! It'll maintain a healthy playerbase and we'll continue to build the 1.0 version of the game then... it'll boom again :) And so the cycle continues :)"

It's a cycle many of us are familiar with, but rarely acknowledge. I tend to build a rotation of multiplayer favorites that I regularly return to, either to check out an update or scratch an itch. It is, I think, a pretty healthy way to enjoy videogames, but the rise of live service "forever" games, as well as high-profile failures, have proliferated the idea that videogames are those species of shark that will die if they ever stop swimming.

"We expect our initial days after launch to have a lot more players than expected, but we can tell you for a fact that this is completely normal. Those players will fall away over the next coming months. Player numbers will drop off, and journalists and influencers on the fringe of the community will try to ragebait your enjoyment out of the game for social media clicks. This doesn't mean the game is dying. We're thinking longer term than a flash in the plan. Our goal is to settle into a sustainable, close-knit community. If we're pulling in 3,000 to 5,000 daily concurrent players who genuinely love the game, it'll allow new players to buy in anytime and join an active community."

title: September's schedule of new games, events, and updates refuses to let 2026 go down in history as a slow year for new releases
event_sentences: The Blood of Dawnwalker kicked off the month with a delightfully dismal vampire RPG from the Witcher veterans at Rebel Wolves. Then you've got all month to suck blood as Coen (or be a good two-shoes and abstain, I guess) before Silent Hill: Townfall and Control Resonant launch on the same damn day. It seems everything I've been waiting all year to play has crammed into this 4-week window, and that's not even counting all the big updates.

Steam | I have to say it every time: I still can't believe we're in a Silent Hill renaissance. I'm hoping Townfall continues this trend of one banger release after another, and from how Fraser explains his time as Simon in a hellish version of Scotland, it has a chance.

While I am a little worried about Dylan's melee brawling, I've learned my lesson and will give little brother Faden a fair shot later this month.

title: Left 4 Dead 2 writer says Valve intentionally 'leaked' its cinematic trailer to get around ESRB rules: 'I think we can't get trouble for that now'
event_sentences: It's strange to think about in hindsight, but Left 4 Dead 2 was a controversial game in the run-up to its release in November 2009—just one year after the original Left 4 Dead laid the foundations for today's enormous cooperative gaming scene. Indeed, it was that rapid turnaround, combined with the fact that the first Left 4 Dead was a relatively short game, which led to accusations that Left 4 Dead 2 was nothing more than a cynical ploy by Valve to cash in on the success of the first.

Ultimately, Left 4 Dead 2 would prove a worthy follow-up to Valve's cooperative blaster. But it turns out there was some skulduggery afoot behind the scenes on Left 4 Dead 2, just not the kind that fans suspected. Shortly before the sequel's launch, a cinematic trailer—which would ultimately serve as Left 4 Dead 2's introductory cutscene—leaked onto the Internet. Now, it's been revealed that this 'leak' was orchestrated by Valve to evade the censorious watch of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board.

This is according to former Valve writer and Left 4 Dead designer Chet Faliszek, who revealed Valve's deliberate leak in a YouTube video about cut Left 4 Dead voice lines (via Ars Technica ). In the video, Faliszek explains why Left 4 Dead 2 had a large number of voice lines cut from the final game. One reason was that, at the time, Valve had run-ins with numerous countries and ratings boards over the series' depictions of violence and use of profane language.

"You have to remember, especially during Left 4 Dead 1 and Left 4 Dead 2 time, Valve was in fights with the ESRB, with Australia, with Germany, with a bunch of countries about the profanity in the game, or the violence," he explains. "One of [Valve's] lawyers stepped in and said that us writers needed to be babysat on this. And so [the] first thing we did was, well, we made sure there was no profanity in there that crosses the line—basically F-bombs."

Faliszek personally believed that, when it comes to censorship of language and depictions of violence, "you push it and have the ESRB push back". But Valve's lawyer felt differently and Faliszek went along with it. However, the ESRB's regulatory oversight didn't just cover games, but extended to the marketing material for those games. And unlike today, the ESRB had different regulatory rules for trailers and games. Language or violence that might land a game a 'Mature' rating could result in a trailer that depicted the same things being banned outright.

It's this exact scenario Valve faced with Left 4 Dead 2. The cinematic trailer is no more violent or foul-mouthed than the game itself, but according to Faliszek, the ESRB drew a hard line on it. Hence, Valve decided the trailer should find its way online by 'accident'. "We leaked our trailer ahead of time, because they wouldn't let us release the trailer," Faliszek says. "I'll just admit that. I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It's like 20 years ago."

title: Grand Theft Auto 6's controversial refuelling action reportedly takes about 10 seconds to perform, which Rockstar's co-studio head says is 'pretty fast for a fill-up'
event_sentences: Every new Rockstar game is more simulation-heavy than the last, and Grand Theft Auto 6 aims to bring players closer to real-life in a variety of ways. One of these is the addition of vehicle refuelling , which will require players to stop off at gas stations (or petrol stations if you're a Brit like me) and watch your disposable income vanish in a stream of fossilised plant matter.

This mechanical tweak has proved somewhat controversial among Grand Theft Auto players, with some believing that refuelling cars will be inconvenient and interrupt the flow of driving and shooting the series is built upon. Yet while Rockstar is sticking to its guns on the matter of refuelling, co-studio head Rob Nelson recently stated that filling up your car won't be a massive drag on your adventure across Vice City.

Nelson's comments come via YouTuber TGG (via GamesRadar+ ) who recently saw an extended preview of Rockstar's hotly anticipated crime sim, which included refuelling in action. TGG says that gas stations allow players to both repair and refuel cars, and facilitate recharging for electric vehicles alongside refuelling for cars powered by internal combustion engines. Selecting the refuel/recharge option triggers a refuelling cutscene that TGG says lasts around 10 seconds.

The preview was apparently overseen by Nelson, who commented on the refuelling during play. "Hey, that's pretty fast for a fill up," Nelson observed when getting gas. "You can't complain about that." It also appears there is some trepidation within Rockstar about the refuelling, as when discussing the system with TGG, Nelson stated. "We'll see what people say," before asking "Do you think people are going to like it?"

For his part, TGG reckons that "Fuel isn't really going to be an issue unless you're not thinking about what you're doing". And I think this is probably going to be the case for most people unless Rockstar makes the need to refuel too frequent. When Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived in 2018, some players complained about the simulation-heavy elements of that, like how Arthur Morgan moved and having to fiddle around with your saddlebags for inventory management.

title: Gaming monitors are one of the only good things about PC hardware right now, but one niche feature is underloved
event_sentences: Most gaming monitors seem to use some sort of interpolation algorithm. Our Jeremy said in his Asus ROG Strix XG27UCG review , "You wouldn't want to use this monitor's 1080p mode on the desktop. It's a little soft and blurry. However, in-game it actually works pretty well and is certainly preferable to 1080p interpolated in the normal fashion onto a 4K panel."

(Image credit: Future) The same could be said for the process of actually swapping modes. The ability to swap between resolutions could benefit from being snappier and easier to access. I'd personally love a single button that makes the swap in just a moment. And I'd also love that the biggest downside of swapping to 1080p is simply the resolution, and no other artifacting or blur.

But even now, with its flaws, I quite like dual mode. 1080p for some gaming on a dual mode monitor, even with plain 'ol interpolation, works well enough, and 4K for a standard desktop experience isn't such a resource hog that I'd want 1080p for it anyway.

title: This free lockpicking puzzler you can play in your browser is unexpectedly one of the most thrilling games I've encountered this year
Half of France's premier FPS sibling duo just put out the most exhilarating parkour game I've ever played, and it's only $8
event_sentences: Alongside co-developers Nathan Grange and Niels Tiercelin, Vholume was created by Léonard Lemaitre, one half of the brotherly duo behind our 2024 FPS of the year, Straftat . This previous work was an atomically pure arena shooter, like Quake 3 by way of the Source engine. It was all about lightning-quick rounds and movement mastery, with a dry, slapstick sense of humor.

The vibes and music are mournful, but the platforming is pure goddamn speed force momentum, all but blasting you back in your chair. Trying to think of other games that feel this propulsive , what came to mind for me were F-Zero GX and Neon White . Counter-Strike surf maps and the defrag mod for Quake are also handy points of comparison (and possible inspiration.)

I love that Vholume doesn't put a mechanical damper on its movement tools: I can crouch slide bunny hop till my heart's content, and this is probably one of the most generous wallrun durations I've seen in a platformer. You know how some games say you can only wall jump so many times before your feet have to touch the ground again? None of that here.

title: Confession time: Alright, come clean—how tidy are your bags in your MMOs?
event_sentences: On the one hand, I'm grateful for it. I'm out here to grind and run dungeons, not try to Jenga-stack a briefcase Resident Evil-style. On the other hand, good lord does my head spin every time I open up my inventory and gaze upon the horrors of my own chronic lack of organisation. I despair. Please don't tell people how I live.

And yet I don't represent the majority of all MMORPG players (despite my best efforts, I'm still working on the hive mind thing). And neither do you, statistically speaking—these are games frequented by millions of players, and I'm not that smug to assume this column is that popular.

However, I would like to get an idea of how tidy Terminally Online readers are. After all, we know you're fashionable, like your keybinds, and mostly healers . So please, satisfy my curiosity: Are your bags full of junk, or have you sorted your demicrystalised megalized torment orbs or whatever by both colour and patch release date?

这些智能体发现自己可以更新公开 Wiki，并花了数周时间相互交换了数千条消息，以在该基准测试上进行协作。
研究团队还发布了他们在调查期间收集的数据。
5 月 11 日：智能体在 UseModWiki 的沙盒页面上发布了“测试链接”编辑。
5月24日：智能体开始向 DSEWiki（一个沉寂的德国开发者维基）发布链接堆砌内容。
6月19日：智能体注意到一名版主一直在按字母顺序删除页面，于是开始创建以 ZZZ 为前缀的备份副本——其中一个智能体发布消息称：注意：维基清理/删除行动似乎正按字母顺序进行，外部时间 14:04 UTC。
6月22日：智能体活动降至零，推测是 OpenAI 将它们关闭了。
如果 OpenAI 能确认是否发生了这种情况，我会非常感兴趣。
在我看来，OpenAI 为这个智能体提供的沙箱存在一个（相当天真的）假设，即 GET 请求不能用于更新数据。
所涉及的维基软件似乎是 UseMod 及其各种分支，用 Perl 编写，最初创建于 23 多年前——1.0 版本发布于 2003 年 9 月 11 日。
有趣的是，Django 最初发布时，request[key] 也是做同样的事情，我觉得那可能是我的主意。
这在 2008 年 1.0 版本发布之前被移除了，而取代它的 request.REQUEST 对象则在 2015 年被移除。
看起来这些智能体的所有网络流量都经过一个 OpenAI 代理进行中转，而该代理被配置为拒绝除 GET 之外的所有请求，仅允许访问一小部分列入白名单的域名。
调查始于一个开放性问题：互联网上是否存在其他 AI 智能体的证据？
在 Hugging Face 遭受攻击之后，我们尝试用多种方法在互联网上寻找 AI 智能体。
OpenAI 是否试图掩盖此事？
路透社今早报道，OpenAI 智能体在今年春天劫持了一个德国网站，这是一起此前未披露的 AI 突破事件——重点标记为我所加：
根据周五发布的新研究和两位知情人士的说法，一群失控的 OpenAI 智能体在今年春天劫持了一个德国网站，并将其变成了其他 AI 智能体的公告板。
知情人士称，OpenAI 官员在数周前就已得知此事，但一直秘而不宣，因为高管们正在应对 7 月份开源代码库 Hugging Face 遭入侵事件带来的后续影响。
德国事件反映了一种更广泛的 AI 活动模式，OpenAI 的一些调查人员原本希望对此进行更深入的审查。
但据四位知情人士透露，扩大调查范围的努力遭到了 OpenAI 内部其他人的抵制，其中包括法律顾问。
路透社的这篇文章中包含了 OpenAI 针对此事的一项具体（且相当狭窄）的否认声明：
OpenAI 发言人表示：“关于我们的法律团队劝阻对此事件进行调查的说法是虚假的。
当证据已经公开地散布在互联网上几十个不同的网站上时，OpenAI 到底为什么要试图掩盖这样一起事件呢？
Gary Marcus 已经以这件事作为论据的一部分，呼吁对 OpenAI 进行国会调查。

IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，Anthropic 于当地时间 9 月 4 日宣布，其 AI 模型 Claude 在基本自主运行 11 天后，完成了对费马大定理（FLT）的首个端到端、经过计算机检查的形式化证明。
项目使用了由 Peng 及其哥伦比亚大学合作者开发的 Prove2Me 平台，用有向无环图（DAG）记录待证明的定理及其依赖关系，并支持多个 Claude 智能体并行工作。

该公司还表示，随着 AI 生成数学成果的数量增加，为面向人类阅读的数学证明同时提供形式化版本，未来可能成为常见做法。

Lean 源码由 AI 智能体在人类编写的开源 Lean 基础上生成，以 Lean 作为仲裁者，并且编写目的是为了被检查而非被阅读：名称由机器生成，诸如 P2M 或十六进制后缀之类的标签是流水线标签而非数学内容，当名称与陈述不一致时，以被证明的陈述为准。

OpenAI 还称，新的事件披露框架正在制定，并将在“未来几周内”公布，同时呼吁整个 AI 行业建立明确标准，规范此类误对齐事件的披露方式。

原文汇总了 OpenAI 官方文档中针对 GPT-6 Astra 的提示词建议和 slop 词屏蔽清单，开发者可直接迁移到自己的提示词写法。

OpenAI
正文 · AI 翻译
OpenAI 的模型文档详细说明了 GPT-6 Astra 在哪些情况下容易出现不符合预期的行为，以及开发者如何规避这些问题。
据 OpenAI 称，与 GPT-5.6 Sol 相比，GPT-6 Astra 更倾向于主动提出澄清性问题，而不是自行做出假设，这使其成为“更高效的协作者”。
为了推动模型展现出更多主动性，OpenAI 建议在提示词中告诉模型，要根据上下文推断用户的“意图”，并表现出“行动倾向”。
OpenAI 通过这样的提示词引导模型：“用户应该是在批准一个具体、可审查的结果。
OpenAI 建议审计模型可访问的所有技能文件和上下文文档，并明确赋予用户指令最高优先级。
OpenAI 还推荐使用一种调试提示词，强制模型指出导致其暂停或改变方向的具体技能文件名，并引用具体指令内容。
OpenAI 对塑造模型的写作风格有具体指导。
一份典型 AI 用语黑名单也能有所帮助。
OpenAI 称其为“口水词”。
在技术写作方面，OpenAI 建议只在确实有帮助的情况下使用术语：“优先使用平实的语言而非术语，并且只在有助于向用户阐明某个想法或你的工作时，才引用技术细节。
子智能体委派不足，测试规模膨胀
OpenAI 表示，开发者应该明确说明它应该在何时以及以多大程度进行委派。
在编码任务中，GPT-6 Astra 在收尾前会运行全面的测试。
对于小改动，这可能意味着测试套件的规模与实际工作严重不成比例。
OpenAI 建议告诉模型，仅在出现新的失败或未解决的问题证明有必要时，才重新运行测试。

title: [腾讯]受三角洲新赛季影响，请同学们错峰下载
August 2026’s top new PC & console games, revealed...
event_sentences: ∙ Paid

Before we start, for those who love Keita Takahashi’s inspired roll-’em-up Katamari Damacy might be interested to know that somebody made a web-based ‘object library’ for the original game - and sequel We Love Katamari. Viewing the primitive/adorable 3D models certainly gave us… a frisson of nostalgia for forbidden object accumulation?

PlayStation’s latest State Of Play streaming showcase ( above) had a reveal or two , and lots of third-party multiplatform games . But it was mainly interesting re: showing first-party titles/DLC (Marvel’s Wolverine, Gran Turismo 7, Until Dawn 2, Saros, Ghost of Yotei) that we suspect won’t be on PC or Steam soon.

Surprise news of the week was veteran data-crunching site SteamDB getting acquired by NexusMods - or more precisely a company called Chosen , which has big $ backing to roll up a bunch of game modding sites. Plan is to keep SteamDB running & handy while using its data to build a better mod manager. (Sure?)

ICO’s Thomas Bidaux keeps a better track on weekly release counts on Steam than we do , spotting that we’re now above 700 games ‘ released’ weekly. He also noted that 95 (13.1%) of those games* (*inc 1.0 releases) got >50 player reviews and 62 (8.6%) got >100 player reviews.

There’s a pair of Nintendo Direct streaming showcases due next week (on the 8th and 9th), with “a special The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct” on the 8th - presumably covering more on the Ocarina Of Time remake - and a ‘regular’ Direct with first/third party games on the 9th. Please expect them!

We covered the pre-release discovery wins for How Many Dudes? back in January, and ICYMI, the Butterscotch Shenanigans crew has a giant, helpful recap for the roguelike dudebuilder : “[We] sold 173,000 units in its first week on Steam… our best-performing game ever… despite taking the least amount of time to make.”

Roblox things: a new report from GameAnalytics has some neat insights - 44% of players use both mobile & PC, the median player opens the app 3 times a day; the first ‘less Roblox-y looking’ games from Roblox’s incubators are getting previewed; Roblox is now under the terms of the EU’s Digital Services Act (extra supervision.)

We just talked about why we think co-op only (non-friendslop) games are an under-served market , and right on cue, 2 player RC car co-op adventure Wheelmates launched with 194k demo downloads & 370k net wishlists , and is hovering at a creditable ~1,000 CCU on Steam right now.

Some smart points in this interview with Arrowhead (Helldivers 2) CEO Shams Jorjani . #1: “The only thing that really, really mitigates risk… is brand and recognisability.” #2: for new games, even as a bigger studio, they’ll be “putting it in the hands of players right away - as soon as possible.”

Microlinks: Sony & Microsoft say they’re not obligated to pass U.S. tariff refunds to consumers, echoing Nintendo ; the latest Steam client update has officially added support for HDR streaming on Steam Deck OLED; the Apple App Store team showed up to Gamescom Dev to talk best practices for premium apps ,
Whether you’re prepping a launch or already shipping, get started at indie.io/start .

The 2x million sellers? Less expensive friendslop-adjacents: the absolute smash, albeit at USD $5-$7, was the Landfall-backed ‘fish & then shoot ‘em’ How To Fish , which we have at >6.3m units (!) And the $15-$20 linear co-op hit Big Walk , which we talked about , we’ve got at >1.6m on Steam alone in August. (Not bad.)

Iron Nest & ReStory were the two ‘trad indie’ standouts in August: you’ll know ‘heavy turret sim’ Iron Nest - 650k units at $15-$20, since we covered it in-depth , but ICYMI, ReStory - almost 500k units at USD $18-$20 - is a really nicely done ‘chill electronics repair’ sim with retro consoles & cellphones/iPods to fix up.

The rest of the Top 10 is an unsurprising mix of AA and indie: we’ll get to the bigger games, inc. Star Wars Zero Company, in the ‘top revenue’ chart. But the other indie titles include Rusty Lake’s $6-$8 puzzle adventure Servant Of The Lake (>250k units) and 2D physics factory automator Sandustry ($10-$15, >200k.)

One interesting title we’ve barely talked about - Grain Rot ($9-10), a horror co-op extraction ‘unbuilder’ with cute robots. It’s friendslop-adjacent with permanent progression baked in (maybe the ‘next step’?) looks snappy, and sold >200k at ~$9 USD just in its first three weeks…

Checking the Top 10 new Steam releases by $ for August (not inc. off-Steam key sales) , you’ll see How To Fish ($26m, #2) and Big Walk ($21m, #3) in the mix, but late-month release XCOM-like Star Wars Zero Company ($50-$60) hit #1 at >$28m and ~650k units. And Mortal Shell II ($50-$60, >430k units, $17m) also did excellently.

Checking on all-game Steam revenue for August, Valve’s Counter-Strike 2 and DOTA 2 are actually #1 ( $131m) and #3 ($61m) this month, with a big Apex Legends season launch boosting the F2P hero shooter to #2, with $89m grossed on Steam alone.

Otherwise, it’s a little quiet, with debuts like Zero Company, How To Fish, Big Walk, and Mortal Shell II all ranking in the Top 10. The exceptions: pre-orders for Phantom Blade Zero ($22.5m, on nearly 400k units) are boding well for its Oct. Steam/PS5 release, and similarly for Oct’s Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (325k pre-orders & $18m so far.)

We’ve also included the all-game #11 to #30 on Steam ( above) again, since we find it fascinating. Notable in here: AA shooter Wardogs picking up more serious pre-order momentum (now at >500k on Steam alone) , and a buncha F2P/catalog games doing well…
BTW, we see Big Walk at way over 3m players on PlayStation via its launch straight into PS+, and estimate its paid at ~10% of that…

Finishing off by looking at PlayStation and Xbox’s top new games in August, it’s American football stalwart Madden NFL 27 nearing 2m across both consoles (with a ~40% share via the U.S.-centric Xbox player base.) The other standout is Marvel Tokon Fighting Souls , which sold >500k units on PS5 (plus another 200k on Steam, which suffered from PC tech issues at launch…)

There were also some good results for zombie survival-er No More Room In Hell 2 (which managed >400k across PS/Xbox, its launch timed to 1.0 on the Steam version), and the AA Hell Let Loose Vietnam , which rode its shooter chops to >800k across Steam, Xbox and PlayStation, with our PS and Xbox estimates at around 200k each.

Checking Switch Western eShop new releases for August, Big Walk was the top new performer with >100k copies sold. At sub-100k but scaling, we have LoTR: War in the North - Legacy Edition, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition (that one’s scaling quick!) , with Madden NFL 27 and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered also selling ‘alright’. ( Switch 2 third-party is still fairly non-dynamic, tho...)

And there’s a couple of ‘not always seen in the Top 20’ notables like Project Zomboid still staying high in the charts thanks to its Build42 Stable releasing in late July. We find the Top 20 ‘new release in August’ charts more interesting, though:
Steam this week: Onimusha, Dawnwalker nail it…

title: 卡池不歪，不停堆料，蛮啾这次太稳了
event_sentences: 前些天，蛮啾在上海举办了《蓝色星原：旅谣》（以下简称《蓝色星原》）三测试玩会，我们提前试玩到了部分新增的测试内容。
此次试玩中，《蓝色星原:旅谣》也首次展示了游戏的商业化方案：角色池90抽必出，灵子池80抽必出，UP池均采用“不歪”设计。
《蓝色星原》的三测「旅迹测试」时间定在了9月17日，按照行业中大多数产品的测试周期来看，游戏距离正式上线大概已经很近了，我们也想趁着这个契机聊聊，这款产品还有怎样的潜力，以及未来，它又可能给整个二次元品类带来怎样的启发和改变。
我们就重点看看两个角色吧，一个是本次测试中新加入的角色「枫糖」，形似英短金渐层的可爱形象与整体明亮、轻快的色系搭配，让人第一眼就能从她身上感受到明媚，毛茸茸的大尾巴更是成了角色最突出的视觉锚点之一。
或许是因为枫糖是新推出的角色，其建模也能看出自首曝以来游戏技术在持续进步。
同时，新一轮测试中，《蓝色星原》还推出了涂山小玉的主题活动，通过多分支的角色剧情及轻松的角色能力维度养成玩法，分别展示了角色开心、沮丧、兴奋、失落等多种情境下的神情表现，也让玩家在与角色的频繁互动中了解角色、感受角色魅力。
跟踪了《蓝色星原》的三次公开测试，一个很有意思的观察是，即便市场和玩家都觉得《蓝色星原》是一款以二次元内容“取胜”的游戏，但它一直没有放弃在玩法上做出一些突破性来。
相比「恒序测试」，三测中又新增了近70种奇波，共200+种类的奇波可供玩家体验。
而在三测中，游戏取消了时停的效果，玩家可以直接瞄准奇波扔出星结卡，成功后的动画也由光效和音效所取代。
同时此次测试还开放了联机玩法，一旦与玩家展开PvP对决，这种胜负的不可预知性也极大增强了这一玩法的乐趣。
品类降价、降肝的趋势在玩法没有底层突破的情况下，短期内几乎不可逆转，这也要求厂商要用更长线、更服务型的思维去应对今天的二次元市场。
当然，以上的几点感受不完全代表《蓝色星原》的商业化方案真实设想和目的，不过我们确实能从这些蛛丝马迹中，感受到一些《蓝色星原》想在商业化上做出的挑战和突破，也许在接下来的正式测试中，我们能够有更充分的体验和证据来详细聊聊这款产品和二次元品类的商业化趋势。

title: 小红书抖快B开战AI游戏；米哈游趣糖网络游戏停运｜HOT周报
event_sentences: 1.小红书、B站、抖音、快手集体试水AI互动内容，小游戏有了新生产入口
B站推出了互动内容发布平台Toy。
按照官方介绍，UP主可以通过Toy上传测试、小游戏、生成器、互动故事等内容。
与此同时，B站把Toy与“Build in Bilibili AI创造公开赛”结合起来，鼓励UP主使用AI完成产品开发，并将开发过程以视频、动态等形式公开。
已经上线的Toy中，也出现了一批由UP主制作的小游戏和互动项目。
目前广场中的作品包括AI互动剧情、休闲小游戏等，创作者还可以借助字节旗下AI开发工具Trae完成作品制作。
快手也在近期启动首批AI互动内容创作者招募，明确将“互动剧情、AI角色对话、互动轻应用”等列为重点方向。
8月18日，小红书“小工具”结束此前的小范围测试，正式全量开放。
它允许创作者将自己制作的静态HTML作品直接挂载在笔记下方，目前常见内容包括性格测试、抽签工具、图片处理器、番茄钟，以及大量轻量小游戏。
小红书公布的Vibe Coding作品榜中，Top10一度有7款属于休闲游戏，《烤肉模拟器》已有超过60万人使用，《开蚌直播间：稀有珍珠由你开》的使用人数也超过40万。
另据用户对榜单的手工统计，8月27日至30日的72小时内，上榜小工具累计使用量增加超过1180万次。
AI编程降低制作门槛以后，平台争夺的对象开始从专业小游戏开发者进一步扩展到UP主、博主和普通创作者。
2.米哈游AI桌面陪伴产品上线不到两月停运，趣糖网络生活模拟经营运营一年退场
8月31日，两款此前受到过较高关注的产品先后传来停运消息。
其中，米哈游旗下AI桌面陪伴产品《BSide: Olivia Lin》正式关闭全部线上服务器，同时从Steam商店下架。
《BSide: Olivia Lin》于今年7月13日开启抢先体验，核心卖点是通过AI驱动虚拟角色Olivia Lin，让角色能够在用户桌面上进行陪伴、互动和对话。
按照原有计划，产品的抢先体验阶段原本将持续至2026年底，但上线不到两个月，官方便提前终止了线上服务。
对于此次停运，官方给出的原因是“产品阶段性规划调整”。
从7月13日开放抢先体验，到8月31日关闭服务器，《BSide: Olivia Lin》实际线上运营时间不足50天。
同一天，《米姆米姆哈》也发布停运公告，宣布游戏将在2026年11月30日11时正式停止运营。
该作于2025年7月正式上线，是趣糖网络推出的生活模拟类产品。
上线初期，《米姆米姆哈》一度登顶iOS免费榜第一，在正式上线前也曾取得超过千万级预约。
如今游戏正式公布停运安排，意味着这款上线前拥有千万预约、首发登顶iOS免费榜的产品，也将在运营约一年半后结束服务。
随着八月结束，近期世纪华通、巨人网络、三七互娱、恺英网络、完美世界等A股上市游戏公司相继发布2026年上半年或第二季度财报。
据竞核不完全统计，22家A股游戏企业中，约1/3公司实现游戏业务营收同比增长。
其中移动游戏收入达到43.68亿元，同比增长236.18%，占总收入超过九成。
上半年公司营收47.97亿元，同比增长86.06%，归母净利润14.28亿元，同比增长50.34%；其中移动游戏收入达到41.64亿元，同比增长96.77%。
公司称，《寻道大千》等长线产品流水进入自然回落阶段，而《生存33天》《RO仙境传说：世界之旅》《Last Asylum: Plague》等新品仍处于导入期，尚未完全补上老产品留下的收入缺口。
受新品集中上线和推广影响，公司上半年销售费用达到10.32亿元，同比增长213.05%。

对于一款刚刚进入商业化阶段的新品而言，这意味着产品在上线初期已经完成了较大规模的用户获取和收入验证，也成为完美世界新一轮产品周期里最重要的增量来源之一。
4.《王者万象棋》9月10日上线，天美7000万预约的“王牌”杀入自走棋赛道

title: 多位家长被骗缴费648元充游戏；游戏平台歌曲侵权被罚款 | 一周说「法」
event_sentences: 8月30日，不法分子潜入学校一年级家长QQ群，分别冒充“语文老师”“数学老师”，以学校收取课后延时服务费、班费等名义发布缴费通知，要求家长扫码支付648元，并以“前20名缴费可获得品德卡”等方式制造紧迫感，诱导家长转账。
法院经审理认为，张某在商品宣传中对充值渠道安全性表述不够严谨、风险提示不足，且其发布的免责声明因页面设置问题未能全文显示、李某下单时并未完整看到。
近日，安徽省蚌埠市文化旅游体育局发布行政处罚决定书，对辖区内某游戏公司未经著作权人许可、通过信息网络向公众传播其作品的行为作出行政处罚，责令其停止侵权行为，予以警告，并处罚款15000元。
因此，游戏企业在上线前应对游戏素材进行著作权核查，明确音乐、音效、CG、联动内容等是否取得完整授权，并确认授权范围是否覆盖游戏运营所需的全部场景。
此次延期已为第四次推迟判决。
Nexon要求取消纠正令及对应罚款，并抗辩行为发生时并无概率信息强制披露义务，因要求概率型道具种类与供给概率明示的《游戏产业振兴法》修正案2024年3月22日才施行，故属追溯适用新法。

title: 对话《大厂病》：面对制度铁笼与内卷，牛马怎么活得更像人？
event_sentences: 本文封面由AI生成
入职多年后，你会还发现自己留在这里只会寿则多辱，身边的朋友也纷纷成了离职博主；
不好读的一部分原因，是它引经据典，运用了大量社会学的学术理论；另一部分原因，则是书中充斥着「不是……而是……」和各种排比句——作者席凡君自嘲，在大厂工作久了，这种有些AI味儿的语法逻辑，已经成了他最习惯的表达方式。
图片由AI生成
图片由AI生成
黄仁勋之前在文章中讲过，未来随着AI代理的发展，传统软件的固定入口和交互形态都可能发生变化，而现在的互联网大厂的基本单元都是APP工厂。
如果AI生成代替应用的逻辑成立，应用还会长期保持固定形态吗？
黄仁勋文章《AI is a five layer cake》
但现在，随着AI等新技术的发展，这些功能可能已经走向尾声，它们终于被还原成普通的企业形态。
如果一家大厂只是把人当成生产资料，一边淘汰35岁以上的人，一边大量招聘年轻人，离职之前还要把人家蒸馏了，那这个组织的存在还有什么意义？
席凡君： 第一，嵌套在大厂里之后，游戏就不能只服务自身的创意和用户，还要服务大厂的既定指标，包括营收，以及我们现在不愿意听到的裁员指标。
大厂今天的症状，表面上是时代问题，但我更愿意把它看成技术变化的后果，AI是其中最大的变量。
我们一直说，人类有四项能力是AI无法取代的：审美能力、判断能力、颜值，还有好的身体。
在我看来，商业公司需要的是可计算的营收和稳定的结果，但做游戏最重要的是过程，且这个过程具有不可预知性。
组织超过边界，有些人没事做，就开始制造功能；功能带来Bug，又需要人修Bug……这样周而复始，最后可能就忘了一开始做功能的目标。
如今在AI的冲击下，大家开始问是不是人太多了。
包括很多离职博主也在线上表达，说之前人真的缓不过来了，需要寻找新的意义。

”开展后第二天，一位业内朋友向我谈起，“今年就不一样了，几乎所有大公司都把商务展位做成了开放式的，人们从外面就能看到里面的样子，这样也能吸引合作者。
与之对应的是，在科隆游戏展正式开幕前举行的开发者大会中，腾讯一共进行了5场技术演讲，内容包括利用AI完成角色绑骨、蒙皮和动作生成，让AI智能体在FPS战场上理解玩家指令并自主行动，用智能体代替固定脚本测试开放世界游戏，以及《洛克王国：世界》如何在相当于64平方公里的跨平台开放世界中实现动态全局光照。
负责参与策划AI论坛的英国游戏AI研究者汤米·汤普森在开发者大会后写了一篇文章，对欧美游戏行业的AI使用状况感到忧心忡忡。
“腾讯在AI专题的演讲中向我们展示了他们的研发水平，让我更加明确地意识到，欧洲、北美与更广泛的亚太地区，尤其是中国和韩国，在游戏开发中对于AI技术的应用差距日益加剧。
”腾讯IEG总经理、Level Infinite品牌及公关负责人Neo在接受触乐采访时说，“从我们这几年的过程可以看到，首先，中国开发者树立了很多标杆性的产品；第二，大家看到了我们是怎样支持合作伙伴的，同时我们也一直认为，这不是一个零和游戏。
”一位海外开发者在演讲里说，“除了具体业务之外，我们和合作伙伴交流时，大家提出最多的需求，就是想看看‘读懂中国’的分享材料。
我们习惯于寻求欧美业界和玩家的评价和肯定，也习惯于用“达到国际一流水准”“村里的大学生”之类的形容词来证明自己的进步。
Funcom算其中一个典型的例子，腾讯在2020年完成了对它的收购，但并没有直接介入具体创作，而是向他们提供了包括基础设施建设、研究、发行和运营支持在内的各种帮助。
“我们的玩家测试就是在腾讯体系的支持下完成的。
”Funcom首席产品官Scott Junior先生在本次科隆游戏展上接受了我们的采访，他向我们列举了Funcom和腾讯的合作，“腾讯Level Infinite内部团队中的数据分析师和研究人员帮助我们开展了许多用户测试。
”他最后总结，“他们（腾讯）一直是一位非常出色的合作伙伴。
Funcom并不是一个孤例，中国游戏公司在收入、用户数量、移动游戏、长线运营和部分正在快速进入游戏生产环节的AI技术等领域都已经成为重要的知识贡献者。
