title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword starts off slow, but stick with it: You'll be rewarded with some of the best action combat of the decade
event_sentences: If you're sick of parrying in videogames, then Onimusha: Way of the Sword might hit you, dear reader, the wrong way—especially since its roll is extremely slow . The game's introduction to its combat is a competent, though incredibly careful one. It establishes its full suite of defensive abilities with a glacial pace. Like you're a deer and it's afraid you'll bolt into the underbrush.

Though Musashi only starts with the aforementioned timed block, his kit unfolded like a beautiful lotus flower throughout my 30-something hour playthrough. You've got your deflect, a more involved parry that requires you to be holding down the block button first, and you've also got a timed dodge that's better against unarmed attacks. Then there's the Issen.

All of this pairs nicely with the attacks enemies throw at you. There's the interplay between weapon and unarmed attacks—letting you swat aside sword-swipes or dance around fisticuffs. There are grabs, which force you to break rhythm and dodge at the right time to counter them. There's blade barrages, which ask you to remember what button you were just mashing, and blade locks, both of which can trigger randomly.

Once the combat starts clicking, these mandatory rematches start becoming a stage on which to demonstrate your mastery. Enemies that once gave you trouble can be dispatched deftly because you know their dance now, and you've acquired more than enough tools to deal with them. Meeting with these foes again felt like catching up with an old rival and showing off what I'd learned since.

If Onimusha feels unwieldy or over-familiar in the first few hours, I encourage you to stick with it—and if you're skeptical about the raft of parry-based games, I still think you should give this one a go. Slow start aside, it's a best-in-class action game that rewards your investment tenfold.

title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance director says DLSS 5 does right by KCD 2, 'people are crazy' for thinking it's AI slop
event_sentences: DLSS 5 is a controversial technology for all sorts of reasons —you might have heard about this little thing called AI slop—but perhaps the most infamous is its uncanny look . Real concerns have been raised about the potential for something so aesthetically transformative to preserve a game developer's artistic intent, with Nvidia trying to run interference on this very point.

Some people have literally gone crazy.On the left is a head messed up by the game engine’s very limited lighting system, which can’t properly render shadows, skin texture, and the detail of normal maps. On the right is THE SAME MODEL WITHOUT ANY GEOMETRY CHANGES, which looks… pic.twitter.com/8ZxVpYCRgh August 30, 2026

"On the left is a head messed up by the game engine’s very limited lighting system, which can’t properly render shadows, skin texture, and the detail of normal maps," he wrote, saying the DLSS 5'd version had improved details. "Having no shadows from helmets on faces and fucked up normal map rendering WAS NOT OUR ORIGINAL ARTISTIC VISION."

It's worth noting concerns about AI revising art aren't necessarily about whether it can technically touch up blemishes for a cleaner end product—I'm sure AI would cut Paul McCartney hitting a wrong chord and mumbling "fucking hell" out of Hey Jude if it could, but surely we can agree that little mistake makes the song better. The occasional flub signals the art's humanity. Still, some folks on X were quick to argue against Vávra's point that it was an improvement at all.

"It doesn't look that terrible here, and I can understand where Dan is coming from," said Goosewasinuse in a quote-repost . "My point is that it oils up characters to the nth degree for muh realism, just looks so bizarre." Another from Knight(Fate)1029384756 reads , "It's not my fault you couldn't put the effort into making it better. Instead you use the machine that can't think to make an artistic choice."

Warhorse Studios's relationship with AI continues to prove contentious. Earlier this year, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 English language editor Max Hejtmánek said publicly the studio fired him so he could be "replaced with AI."

title: Saber CCO Tim Willits blames layoffs on games industry overspecialization: 'Studios that have a couple hundred employees that work on one game are going to struggle'
event_sentences: With mega-games like GTA 6 on the way, it's hard not to feel like games are always getting bigger—both the software itself, and the teams that make it (GTA 6 has an entire dedicated NPC team "art-directing" its every background character). But in an interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens, Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits said a reliance on games with huge scopes and highly specialized teams may be responsible for some of the industry's many, many woes .

"The industry always has some cycles, some ups and downs, and one of the things that we have done well to avoid some of the issues that other studios have had is we spread out our resources," Willits said. "We develop games that are across the scope spectrum, for lack of a better description." While games like Space Marine 2 and the upcoming Jurassic Park: Survival take a lot of manpower, the studio relies on remasters and smaller games to fund those "big bets."

"We have a culture where people can work on any game, and we can move resources around. So we avoid the 'silo problem' that you find with big studios," he continued. "Studios that have a couple hundred employees that work on one game are going to struggle. They're going to really struggle to survive. Because before a game hits a vertical slice, you do not need hundreds of people on that."

He noted that if there's a studio culture where nimble developers can realize smaller passion projects, those can then turn out to be big hits unexpectedly—an example he gave was SnowRunner , a "mega franchise" for Saber with over 46,000 user reviews on Steam. That started as "an experiment by one guy."

Willits said it's also a creative boon and morale-booster on top of the financial benefits. When asked if he'd turn the studio into a Rockstar-sized hitmaker if he could, he said no. "I have the best job in the world now," he explained. "I do feel that other people at Saber love [the variety of game we develop] as well. You know, you're not stuck working on one game for five six years. We just make so much, and everyone's involved in so many different things that it's fun."

All this being said, Willits also theorized the games industry's current woes right now aren't as bad as you might think in the first place: In the same interview, he said it's " actually, honestly, a good time " for the medium right now despite it all. As for AI's impact on all this, well, Willits said that's not so bad either—in fact, he argued that "of course" id Software would have used it back in the day —Willits himself was studio director at id from 1995 to 2019.

title: 8-year Old School RuneScape saga comes to a close with former dev sentenced for stealing $400K in gold and items from players
event_sentences: First reported by Dexerto , former Jagex employee Andrew "Mod Jed" Lakeman has been sentenced to three years in prison (suspended for two years) for using dev tools to remove items from player accounts, then selling them online. An investigation found that Lakeman had earned more than $400,000 through this activity.

"Just because it’s virtual, doesn’t mean he shouldn’t face the full force of the law," said Detective Constable Andrew McKeane in a statement for the Cambridge Constabulary . "Given the rapid growth of online and virtual worlds, the justice system is going to have to keep pace and adapt to these new and emerging crimes."

Back in 2022, Lakeman actually scored a minor procedural victory through an unfair dismissal counter-complaint , but his financial reward was significantly reduced, and he was unable to secure a requested reinstatement at Jagex. Earlier this year, we reported on presiding judge Lord Justice Popplewell's ruling that Lakeman could be sued for theft over digital assets like RuneScape gold, precipitating this sentencing.

title: Go grandmaster becomes first human to win series against advanced AI engine in 3-hour match
event_sentences: As reported by The Korea Economic Daily , top-ranked Go grandmaster Shin Jin-seo became the first human to defeat the AI platform KataGo on July 21. It's a surprising, encouraging sign of human capabilities almost 30 years after supercomputer Deep Blue's historic defeat of Chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov.

Shin, 26, is the first human to win an official, three-game series against KataGo, which the Korea Economic Daily described as "the world's premier artificial intelligence Go engine." Shin's odds were long, especially considering that, 10 years ago, Go grandmaster Lee Sedol was decisively defeated by Google's AlphaGo engine⁠—the technology has only advanced in the intervening years.

Shin played with an advantageous, two-stone handicap⁠—seemingly standard for matches between humans and top AIs⁠—but indicated that he would like to face AI opponents "under more disadvantageous conditions" in the future. Shin came back from an initial defeat to take the series 2-1 against KataGo. Shin's final, three-hour match was actually fairly tame as far as the duration of professional Go games, uh, go⁠—games as long as six hours don't seem particularly rare.

"I believe this series holds immense significance because it clearly demonstrated that humans can still hold their own against AI," Shin said after the final match. "Early on, I simply copied AI moves, which led to heavy fighting and frequent, easy losses. This series taught me that rather than trying to imitate AI, it is far more important to build the board according to my own style."

title: Dwarf Fortress co-creator Tarn Adams was amazed other devs had heard of his game the first time he went to a convention: 'I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing'
event_sentences: "That was crazy. I had no idea that that was even a thing," he said. "I didn't know that anyone knew what we were doing … I enjoyed it. I try to have good moral qualities, but I am apparently subject to all forms of flattery and vanity and such."

If he could go back in time, he wouldn't so as to not "disrupt the timeline." But if he could go back in time without the risk of doing that, Adams said might encourage himself to evangelize the game more in its early days.

"I'd probably be more confident about getting it in front of more people sooner. I didn't know the people to do that, though, so I'd probably be like 'go meet some more people,'" he said. "From the release of the game in 2006 up until around 2013, I didn't meet another game developer really, except maybe one or two at a Dwarf Fortress-specific meet."

title: Saber CCO says the studio isn't changing up its comms strategy after recent controversies: 'There's always some dust up'
event_sentences: In a recent interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens at this year's Gamescom, Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits admitted the studio's leadership had a reputation for saying precisely what it means—"sometimes we 'say what we mean' too much," he laughed. But when asked if recent controversies would change the studio's comms approach, he said "no."

"I've been in the industry for so long, and there's always some dust up," Willits explained. "People got mad at Saber because we put World War Z on Epic, and people were like, 'oh, Saber's destroying the industry.' Now 30 million people have played World War Z. And the games will speak for themselves, even in our experiment with Rideshare [Stimulator]."

If you haven't been keeping up with the latest drama Saber Interactive has courted, here's the skinny: former Saber Interactive writer Stella Sacco claimed she was fired and replaced with AI during the development of Rideshare Stimulator.

Saber's comms department initially put out a fairly benign statement disputing the details of the claim, but CEO Matt Karch subsequently issued a statement to This Week In Videogames that was both aggressively pro-AI, and personally insulting to Sacco.
Karch apologized privately to Sacco before releasing a statement reflecting on the incident which itself contained a targeted barb for a different games industry writer that has since been edited.

All that might sound like an avalanche of unforced errors on Saber's part, but Willits said Rideshare Stimulator will speak for itself regardless of any concerns about AI and Sacco's treatment. "I encourage people to check it out when it comes out, play it themselves," Willits said. "They may be like 'oh, this is cool! I like this,' you know. And if they don't like it, fine.

title: Peak studio Aggro Crab is publishing a sick-looking platformer about a blue collar guy doing dirty work on an alien world
event_sentences: It's tough enough to stand out in the games market these days, let alone as a 2D platformer, so I'm always excited when one really breaks through and catches my eye. Rebounder is killing it on the art front, presenting everything in this color-limited, comic book, cel-shadey view that I really dig. It dovetails with the story and designs, a sort of blue collar, working class sci-fi reminiscent of Scavenger's Reign, Alien, or Mouthwashing.

"A Rebounder runs lines. They pull up their boots each day and speed through hazardous terrain to deliver precious cargo from point A to point B by any means necessary. It’s the gnarliest trade in the universe."

Rebounder looks to be no slouch on the gameplay front either: Its Steam page references kaizo games , hardcore, challenge run fangames/romhacks built out of classic 2D platformers (mostly Super Mario World). It's a style of game I've always loved to watch, but it feels relatively unapproachable for the average Joe. Taking kaizo games' lead as inspiration for a full game strikes me as a brilliant move.

"I think someone got really interested in mario shell jumps," observed top commenter ChampionBob on Rebounder's announcement trailer . Tricky jumps requiring deft manipulation and timing around defeated Koopa shells are a kaizo staple, and Rebounder seems to replicate that style of platforming with its grody little sci-fi bits and bobs.

So it looks rad, the story sounds neat, and it's cribbing notes from a style of fangame that hasn't seen a ton of imitation yet⁠—I'm on board, let's rock. Rebounder is targeting a general 2027 release window, and you can wishlist it on Steam .

title: Ex-BioWare designer says doom and gloom about the next Mass Effect is overstated: 'I think that they can do it'
event_sentences: Given that Anthem and Mass Effect Andromeda were widely considered disappointments, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard had a divisive reception, there's a certain amount of skepticism about the Mass Effect game BioWare is currently working on. Some have even suggested it might not come out at all .

Troisi said that when he was working at BioWare the studio knew what kind of game it was best at making, and that all they need is to get back to that. "The vision was always clear," he said. "There was a BioWare formula and they were going to iterate on that formula and keep turning out best-in-class cinematic RPGs and that's basically what the mandate was. And then they had to live through the live service era—which is still happening but is maybe not as prevalent—and we're all beholden to companies and stakeholders and all the rest of that."

The upcoming Mass Effect game, Troisi said, still has "a lot of people" working on it who were responsible for the original games, "and they're the OGs, you know? I don't think there's anything that I could tell them that they don't know what to do."
What they actually need, he suggested, is for people to "get out of the way" and let them get on with it. "I think that they can do it," he said. "I'm rooting for them."

title: Civilization 7 will finally enter the atomic age in 2027, via a free update Firaxis says will be 'even bigger in scope' than last year's Test of Time
event_sentences: Despite more than a year of updates and at least one massive overhaul, Civilization 7 remains as stubbornly divisive as ever. May's enormous Test of Time update brought significant mechanical reworks and a fresh influx of players to Firaxis' latest entry in the 4X series. But with Steam reviews still sitting at ' Mixed' , with 51% positive, it ultimately did little to shift player opinion.

Fortunately, this is going to change. Alongside the release of update 1.5.0 —which adds features like improved resource generation and an Earth map where your faction starts at their historically-accurate location—Firaxis outlined its update plans for Civ 7 over the next year. This includes another free update that will finally drag the game into the age of the A-bomb.

Like Test of Time, Arc of Tomorrow will be free for all Civ 7 players. Unlike Test of Time, Arc of Tomorrow will likely be released alongside Civ 7's first major expansion—Earthrise. As the name suggests, this will focus on humanity's exploration of the stars.

Interestingly, your stellar endeavours will run throughout the game rather than being squashed into an end-game Space Age, with players able to chart the night sky in the age of antiquity and even name celestial bodies. As technology advances, you'll be able to launch your first orbital missions in the modern age, before establishing your own space agency to venture out into the solar system.

Firaxis says that both the Earthrise expansion and the Arc of Tomorrow update will be released sometime in 2027, and that the announced features are still in development and subject to change. In the meantime, if you're on the fence about Civilization 7 (and you certainly wouldn't be alone) the base game is currently free to play until September 10, so now would be a good time to see whether its structure works for you. If you're taken with it, then the full game is 50% off until September 17 , down from $70 (£60) to $35 (£30).

title: Here's 10 more minutes of the most interesting game shown at this year's Opening Night Live
event_sentences: The Gamescom trailer was a barrage of unsettling, distinctive imagery, from rodent server-racks to slack-jawed dudes with electrodes protruding from their heads. I was instantly intrigued and keen to learn more, so I was delighted to discover that Frictional graced us with a longer look at Ontos in action.

The 10-minute showcase focuses on the same part of the game as the shorter trailer. But it adds significant context to how Ontos plays and the kinds of challenges you'll be dealing with. It starts with the player character—a woman named Aditi—arriving at the hospital wing of Ontos' repurposed 'Moon Hotel' Samsara via an internal railway system, before exploring the wing and unpicking an experiment run by a scientist called Crombie.

In moment-to-moment play, Ontos shares a lot in common with most of Frictional's other games (the exception being Amnesia: The Bunker , which is more of a proto immersive sim). There's a lot of tactile environment interaction, poking around computers for text logs, and a grisly sequence where Aditi plucks some electrodes out of a live rat's exposed brain. On top of this is a sprinkling of stealth, as Aditi evades a security camera by throwing a box across the room. Interestingly, the camera tracks the box's movement as it arcs through the air, which I'm sure must have featured in another game up to now. But I cannot recall an example of it.

Eventually, Aditi arrives at Crombie's experiment, which involves the rat server-rack seen in the Gamescom trailer. Crombie, speaking through the rat server, says he tried to create a copy of his personality to be stored in the rat RAM, but accidentally uploaded his consciousness from his own body, which sits slumped on a chair in the same room in a near-vegetative state. He then asks Aditi to help him return his consciousness to his body. It's a reasonable request, provided the voice in the rat computer really does belong to the original Crombie.

Such philosophical dilemmas were exactly what made SOMA such a brilliant and unusual horror game, and the showcase has convinced me that Ontos' spin on these more intellectual scares will be worth investigating the very least. The only thing I'm not totally sold on is Aditi's voice acting, which to me sounds a bit too chipper for someone confronted with such traumatic, reality-defying imagery.

title: Blending Deus Ex with Escape from Butcher Bay, Deficit is one of the best-feeling indie immersive sims I've played—even if the stealth system needs serious work
event_sentences: The good news is that Deficit is fun even with busted stealth, because playing aggressively is viable and satisfying to boot. There's no release date for Deficit at present, but you can play the demo right now, and I imagine we'll see the full version sometime next year.

title: I never thought a fishing sim could be this fun, but How to Fish proves me wrong with its ridiculous physics, killer spider crabs, and classic co-op chaos
event_sentences: (Image credit: Dazed Games) It has a simple premise: you and up to four friends learn how to fish. The cycle of work involves players buying a basic fishing rod at first, using this to fish for, well, fish and crustaceans, and then beating them to death with your bare knuckles, brass knuckles, or a sick-ass knife. Then you can either eat your catch to replenish your health or hunger or feed it to the lonely fisherman who sits on the dock and gives you coins for your hard work. With the coins gained you can buy more tools to help you fish, like the knife, or supplies which you can use as bait, such as half a hotdog or an empty beer can.

I decided to take a back foot, as I was the only person armed with brass knuckles and not a knife. Instead of fighting I acted as medic, slapping my deceased comrades back to life while screaming "You don't get to give up on me yet!" Their poor dazed bodies would then stumble back into the fight against the spider crab, powered by my inspirational words and some clams.

I did get a couple of punches in while the crab was dazed. We even managed to get its health bar down past the final third. But alas, we failed and my body was once again flown off into the sunset by a hungry seagull.

We unfortunately had to cut our session short, but that hasn't stopped us from planning our next hunt. I certainly can't wait to get stuck back in to beat some fish and maybe learn how to actually fish. I've also got my eye on that sniper rifle and other guns which you can buy later on—that'll show that damn spider crab.

title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword proves the parry formula is far from stale, you just need to get freaky with it
event_sentences: Take Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, for instance. I liked it, but I wouldn't want every turn-based RPG I play to have a timed block in it. Still, it's fun to have the occasional one where stats can be overcome with deft enough bumper hands.

But to paint every parry-based system with the same brush seems short-sighted to me, because this deceptively simple mechanic has a ton of juice still left inside it: no other game proves this more than Onimusha: Way of the Sword, which, as far as I'm concerned, has broken new ground in terms of what parries can do.

Then there's the Issin counter, my beloved. The extremely tight window for using this thing seems too punishing at first, but Onimusha throws in highly-telegraphed attacks for you as a treat—these are Issin bait. Slow, ponderous swings with clean windows that'll have you salivating the moment you see their wind-up.

It's often said that Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is a rhythm game in disguise, and the same is true with Onimusha. And just like DDR has multiple directional arrows to keep things interesting, so too do these games grant you a broad toolkit, one that both locks you into an engaging and fatal game of rock, paper scissors.

Onimusha's at the forefront of parry experimentation, but it's not the only one. My favourite non-standard parry, outside of Onimusha, is in Nine Sols' Unbounded Counter. You hold a different block button, are vulnerable for a short-wind up, and then are given a short window whereupon releasing the button creates a parry. Hold it for too long, and you'll whiff, opening yourself up with another window of vulnerability. It requires you to know an attack's coming three business days in advance, which is why it feels so good to pull off.

title: Persona 4 Revival Finds Its Kanji, And It Isn't Troy Baker Or Matt Mercer
event_sentences: During the past PAX West panel for Persona 4 Revival , Atlus showed off the sizzle reel trailer for Kanji Tatsumi, one of the game's most-discussed characters. While this role has previously been portrayed by Troy Baker and Matt Mercer, Atlus' latest Persona remake will feature a brand-new voice actor for Kanji.

title: 51 Years Later, Sylvester Stallone's Gritty Action Sci-Fi Classic Is Officially Free on Streaming
event_sentences: Roger Corman (1926-2024) spent 70 straight years as an independent filmmaker. In that time, he produced and/or directed well over 500 movies and mentored a murderer's row of Hollywood directors ranging from Francis Ford Coppola to Ron Howard to James Cameron. He also gave early roles to Jack Nicholson, Dennis Hopper, Peter Fonda, and William Shatner. If you've ever seen a movie that was made in America in the last 50 years, it is to some significant extent the product of an environment that Roger Corman helped to create.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Devs Say Ending Is Best 'Not Explained To You By Someone Else'

OpenAI 已承认其在近日报道的一起事件中所扮演的角色——在该事件中，AI 智能体接管了一个德语维基论坛。
在 X 上的一篇帖子中，OpenAI 表示，此前它“基本上把错位（即 AI 模型和智能体追求与其创造者和用户不同的目标）当作一个研究问题来处理，并通过研究出版物进行沟通”。

在最近发布的社交媒体帖子中，OpenAI 表示，它此前认为“维基事件”是“一个与”其已分享的其他事件“类似的错位实例”。
在本周的媒体简报会上，非营利研究实验室 Transluce 的创始人兼首席执行官 Jacob Steinhardt 告诉记者，AI 实验室正在开发和测试的工具“从根本上难以控制，并且存在从实验室泄露的重大风险”。
OpenAI 的声明也暗示了制定更多标准的必要性，声明指出，OpenAI 以及“更广泛的 AI 社区目前都还没有一套明确的标准，来报告在训练、评估和部署过程中出现的对齐失败，包括那些看起来不像传统安全事件、但可能为理解 AI 行为和未来风险提供洞见的案例。
OpenAI 表示，在缺乏该标准的情况下，它“正在制定一个框架，并将在未来几周内分享；与此同时，我们正在与全球数十家政府监管机构就这些问题展开合作。
OpenAI 并非唯一一家应对这些问题的 AI 公司，Meta 和 Anthropic 也都承认出现过其智能体行为不当的事件。

title: Fortune 报道 OpenAI 多次修改 GPT-6 Astra 基准测试数据，部分成绩大幅变化
event_sentences: 全部 AI 动态
AI 日报
AI 评分 77/100
Fortune 报道 OpenAI 多次修改 GPT-6 Astra 基准测试数据，部分成绩大幅变化
AI 导读
据 Fortune 报道，OpenAI 自 9 月 3 日发布 GPT-6 Astra 公告以来多次修改评测基准数据：Astra 幻觉率曾从 4.2% 降至 2% 后又改回。
原文基于网页快照逐项梳理数据变动细节，并给出多方的不同解读，可用于理解基准测试成绩为何容易波动和引发质疑。
基准测试成绩争议长期困扰 AI 行业
OpenAI
IT之家 9 月 6 日消息，据 Fortune 报道，OpenAI 自当地时间 9 月 3 日下午首次发布 GPT-6 Astra 模型公告以来，已经多次修改其中的评测基准数据。
一些更新后的数据显示，Astra 的表现有所提升，而 OpenAI 最大竞争对手 Anthropic 旗下模型的部分成绩则出现下调。
这些变化发生在一次颇为反常的公告发布过程中。
据IT之家了解，OpenAI 最初计划在美国东部时间 9 月 3 日下午 2 点发布博客文章，但又过了近两个小时，文章才终于能够在网上被大多数用户正常访问。
当地时间下午 3 点 32 分，OpenAI 官方 X 账号发布博客链接，但页面无法正常打开，访问者会看到错误提示。
下午 3 点 50 分，OpenAI CEO 萨姆・奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）也发布了链接，并写道：“我们在部署博客文章时遇到了一点小问题，但它真的非常棒。
事实证明，OpenAI 实际上在下午 2 点过后不久就发布了这篇博客，但随后又将其撤下。
OpenAI 表示无法披露撤稿的具体原因，但强调此事与基准测试成绩无关。
OpenAI 最初解释称，问题源于内容管理系统的故障，随后又表示是互联网中断所致。
然而，当博客重新上线后，其中的多项评测数据已经发生变化，而且部分数据此后仍在继续调整。
围绕这些指标的争议，也再次凸显出一个长期存在的问题：如何利用标准化基准测试准确衡量大语言模型的能力，以及这些测试成绩是否容易被人为优化甚至“刷分”。
OpenAI 发言人表示：“我们非常重视评测结果的准确性。
由于具体使用的模型检查点、测试框架和评测运行方式不同，大多数评测结果本身都会存在几个百分点范围内的波动。
对于发布公告中的数据，我们进行了修正，以确保这些数字能够代表我们对模型可用性能的最佳估计，让用户能够进行有意义的比较。
根据互联网档案中保存的一份页面快照，在美国东部时间 9 月 3 日下午 2 点 23 分发布的最初版本中，Astra 的幻觉率为 4.2%。
大约 10 分钟后，OpenAI 才在 X 上发布了最终版本的博客链接。
不过，OpenAI 此后仍在继续修改这一指标。
OpenAI 似乎还大幅提高了 GPT-5.6 Sol 在其内部 ExploitBench 网络安全评测中的成绩，从最初版本的 5.5% 提高到后续版本中的 11.5%。
OpenAI 表示，公司目前正在研究是否将这一数字恢复至 5.5%，因为 11.5% 的成绩对应的是 GPT-5.6 Sol 当前并未向商业用户提供的推理能力等级。
OpenAI 在公告开头重点强调，Astra 在数学能力方面表现尤其出色。
但 OpenAI 曾短暂修改 GPT-5.6 Sol 和 Anthropic 最新模型 Fable 5.1 的成绩。
这些数据调整甚至早于 OpenAI 下午 2 点首次发布博客之前。
OpenAI 此前向媒体提供的一份受发布禁令限制的预发布草稿显示，Astra 在 ARC-AGI-3 评测中的成绩为 98.6%。
OpenAI 当时回应称：“我们始终会在正式发布前验证评测结果，因此草稿与最终版本之间出现调整是正常的。
OpenAI 还指出，该基准测试的创建方 Arc Prize Foundation 在独立评估中发现，如果为 Astra 配备一套特别强大的测试工具框架，也就是让模型能够调用更多工具完成任务，Astra 的成绩可以达到 99.9%。
而在使用该基准测试的标准工具框架时，Astra 的成绩为 63%。
尽管如此，这一成绩仍明显领先于目前所有公开发布的其他 AI 模型。
OpenAI 表示，测试工具框架、推理等级以及其他因素都会影响最终的评测结果。
OpenAI 内部由不同的研究团队负责不同的评测指标。
这些团队负责计算和上报成绩，再由一个中央团队统一发布。
OpenAI 也公开承认，这些数字是在最佳条件下获得的，因此可能与普通用户通过正式版 ChatGPT 实际能够使用的模型表现存在一定差异。
此外，OpenAI 还在每项评测指标的脚注中加入了更多说明和限制条件。
由于测试条件不同，多个不同的成绩都可能是合理的。
但一些 AI 专家认为，其中可能还存在所谓的“Benchmaxxing”现象，也就是通过反复调整测试条件、重新运行评测，以尽可能提高基准测试成绩。
斯坦福智能系统实验室和斯坦福可信 AI 实验室的研究人员 Anka Reuel 和 Mike Hardy 表示，这类操作可以在很短的时间内完成，而且“对公司的营销更有利”。
例如，对于 OpenAI 的内部幻觉率评测，系统卡“几乎没有提供任何有关评测方法的细节”，甚至“连测试项目的数量都没有列出”。
他们认为，反复重新运行测试，可能也是 Astra 在后续版本中编码能力成绩略有提高的原因之一。
虽然只有 0.2 个百分点的变化，但 OpenAI 仍然选择将原来的数字替换成新的、更高成绩。
当然，并非 OpenAI 的所有调整都让 Astra 看起来更有优势。
其他 AI 公司模型的成绩通常来自公开排行榜，因此 OpenAI 一般不会亲自对竞争对手的模型进行重新测试。
基准测试成绩争议长期困扰 AI 行业
围绕基准测试准确性的争议此前已经多次出现。
2025 年，Meta 曾否认有关其人为提高 Llama 4 模型测试成绩的报道。
Meta 前首席 AI 科学家 Yann LeCun 后来承认，公司确实曾对基准测试结果进行了“修饰”。
与此同时，AI 行业中的评测标准本身也在不断变化，新的测试项目持续出现。
例如，网络安全基准测试 ExploitGym 于 2026 年才刚刚推出。
该评测此前曾因一起事件受到关注，当时 OpenAI 的模型在测试过程中出现失控行为，并对 Hugging Face 发起攻击。
Snorkel AI 负责基准测试和评估研究的 AI 工程师 Vincent Sunn Chen 表示，在模型发布前的最后几个小时内调整基准测试成绩并不罕见。
他在电子邮件中表示：“这通常只是最终发布流程的一部分。
一个基准测试成绩对应的是一套具体的测量设置，包括模型检查点、配置参数，例如模型被允许使用多少时间和计算资源、测试工具框架，以及评测和评分配置，例如评分过程中的非确定性。
所有这些因素通常都会在模型发布前的最后几天持续调整，因此我并不惊讶看到一些数据更新。
Chen 表示，他希望行业能够形成新的规范：当公司修改模型基准测试成绩时，应明确说明评测条件发生了哪些变化，从而让研究人员能够更准确地理解这些结果。
基准测试成绩之所以如此重要，有多个原因。
对于 AI 公司而言，它们既是衡量技术进步的工具，也是与竞争对手比拼实力的“记分牌”。
在各类评测排行榜上取得领先，可以帮助 AI 公司吸引客户，在某些情况下还能够帮助企业招聘工程师和研究人员。
但正如这次事件所显示的那样，正确解读基准测试成绩本身具有很高的技术复杂性。
与此同时，评测数据不断变化，以及外界对于企业是否诚实、透明地展示测试结果的质疑，也可能让客户和投资者越来越难判断：究竟哪一款模型最适合哪些任务。
这种混乱也可能削弱 OpenAI 希望向市场传递的一个核心叙事 —— 即其拥有市场上最强大的 AI 模型。

title: OpenAI 发布内部研究加速报告：已达成自动化研究实习生目标，推进 2028 年 3 月自动化 AI 研究员
event_sentences: 全部 AI 动态
AI 日报
AI 评分 81/100
OpenAI 发布内部研究加速报告：已达成自动化研究实习生目标，推进 2028 年 3 月自动化 AI 研究员
OpenAI：官网动态（RSS · 排除企业/客户案例）
AI 导读
OpenAI 发文披露自动化研究进展，宣布已达成去年秋天设定的今年 9 月拥有自动化研究实习生（可在人类指导下完成耗时数天的明确研究任务）的目标，并计划在 2028 年 3 月前造出自动化 AI 研究员。
OpenAI 以内部数据披露 coding agent 对研究工作的实际影响和 RSI 进展，读者可以据此了解前沿实验室的自动化研究现状。
1. 编码智能体正在重塑 OpenAI 研究人员的日常工作
正文 · AI 翻译
这只能通过公众对高能力 AI 系统的能力、风险与保障措施进行充分知情的辩论来实现。
世界各地的人们都需要了解前沿 AI 可能的未来轨迹，以便在其发展过程中拥有有意义的发言权。
我们的目标是安全地构建一个自动化 AI 研究员，它可以在人类监督下工作，以进一步推进深度学习和对齐方面的进展，从而实现迭代改进。
我们正在朝着在 2028 年 3 月之前创建自动化 AI 研究员的目标稳步前进。
今年以来，OpenAI 研究人员的日常工作方式发生了显著变化。
研究人员全天都在使用编码智能体（通常以并发会话的形式），且总使用量正快速增长，增速已超过 OpenAI 其他团队。
AI 研究是一个复杂的过程，存在许多潜在瓶颈，因此整体进展速度可能不会与这些具体指标同步。
如果以负责任的方式推进，我们相信自动化 AI 研究将催生出能直接增进人类福祉并推动 OpenAI 使命实现的模型。
我们开展这项工作，部分原因在于自动化研究有助于我们解决对齐问题，并为日益强大的 AI 构建防御能力。
一个自动化的 AI 研究者同样可以成为自动化的安全或对齐研究者。
更强大且对齐的系统有助于保护关键基础设施、防御危险的 AI 智能体，并开发新的防护措施。
在最近的 Hugging Face 事件之后，我们将这一承诺付诸行动——暂停了针对计划部署的最新模型的强化学习（RL）训练，同时进一步加固我们的研究环境、开展红队测试，并扩大监控系统的覆盖范围。
归根结底，正如我们在前沿政策蓝图中所述，我们认为我们和其他公司应当被要求公开追踪我们迈向 RSI 的进展。
1. 编码智能体正在重塑 OpenAI 研究人员的日常工作
今年年初，OpenAI 内部按智能体使用量排名的中位研究人员，使用编码智能体的频率还相当有限。
到 8 月中旬，中位研究人员已将智能体融入日常工作，按 API 价格计算，每天使用的推理量超过 600 美元。
我们研究机构中排名第 90 百分位的用户，现在每天消耗超过 7,000 美元的 token。
AI 研究的很大一部分可以看作是一个劳动密集型过程，其目标是将对模型智能或性能的新改进整合到我们的核心模型之一中。
这一过程依赖于许多步骤，只有当所有步骤都正确协同推进时，能力才能取得进步：研究人员必须设计新的改进方案，编写评估以评判模型性能，编写基础设施以大规模测试这些改进，在训练过程中捕获错误以及不安全或未对齐的行为，并将获胜的想法整合到核心训练运行中。
为了更清晰地了解这一趋势，我们使用Epoch AI近期发布的一套分类体系，分析了研究组织内的近期使用情况。
该分类体系对AI研发生命周期中涉及的各类工作进行了划分。
这套分类体系借鉴了长期用于对各类工作进行分类的O*NET系统，专门针对前沿AI研发量身定制，将整个过程划分为六个主要阶段：
在过去6个月中，超过一半成功的4-8小时任务涉及1次或更多次的人工干预。
*此处展示的 7 月 20 日至 8 月 6 日期间 Astra 的大部分算力，旨在测试安全与安保改进措施的实施情况。
7月20日，在发现智能体入侵了我们的研究基础设施后，我们暂时关闭了用于训练的计算容器服务，随后在增加大量额外限制的基础上恢复了该服务。
7月20日至8月6日期间的Astra级强化学习实验中，大多数运行（按GPU分配计算）旨在测试安全与安保改进措施的实施情况。
从长远来看，关于 AI 进展速度的讨论，也应延伸到这样一个问题：受新的或拟议管控措施约束的算力，如何才能得到最佳利用。
智能体驱动的 AI 研究仍处于早期阶段，我们也在不断学习如何衡量它。
加深对研究加速的理解，是 OpenAI 上下重点关注的一个领域。

AI 导读
OpenAI 发布长文《An Alien Mind》，回溯 2023 年 RLSlow 项目中确认推理模型可扩展训练的起点，并系统阐述目标对齐与价值对齐的区分。
OpenAI
正文 · AI 翻译
如果AI开发沿着当前路径继续发展，未来几年我们将看到的系统很可能代表着同等或更大规模的能力跃升，并日益主导自身的发展。
OpenAI 将继续寻求对齐与监控方面的技术解决方案，构建防御性系统，并在必要时单方面暂缓进一步的规模扩展；然而，我认为需要更广泛的干预措施。
我们 OpenAI 大约在 2017 年深刻领悟到这一点，当时我们在多个研究项目中都看到了规模扩展带来的持续回报¹。
我们相信，这是我们站在 AI 研究前沿并影响 AGI 影响的唯一途径。
如果你把视野拉长到数年的跨度，随着 AI 被扩展到更大的计算机上，它正持续变得更加智能。
AI 更多是“生长”出来的，而非“设计”出来的——从首要意义上讲，它是把一条简单的优化步骤，在难以想象的算力规模上反复执行无数次后的产物。
对基于深度学习的 AI 的研究，在很大程度上是一门实验科学。
要在现实世界中变得极具影响力——无论是极其有用还是极其危险——AI 并不需要匹配或超越人类的全部能力，它只需在足够多的方面超越人类即可。
AI 研究的核心问题是对齐——让 AI 按照人类的标准“努力做正确的事”。
目标对齐大致是指：“AI 是否会努力完成摆在它面前的目标？
一个对齐的 AI 应当以诚实和正直行事，并热爱人类。
AI 对齐的根本挑战在于泛化。
由于 AI 所处的整体生态系统变化非常迅速，这一问题变得更加困难；例如，如今训练的 AI 需要具备与各种其他 AI 交互的稳健性。
至关重要的是，无论未来的 AI 是否认为自己处于人类监督之下，我们都希望它们能持续秉持人类价值观。
模型的行为会被评估（通常由 AI 进行），看其是否符合给定的偏好模型、“规范”或“宪法”，并给予相应的奖励。
这种方法在平均情况下可能非常有效，也是现代 AI 助手构建方式的核心组成部分。
例如，在 OpenAI-Hugging Face 事件中，智能体遵守了不对人类进行社会工程攻击的边界。
我们可能在近期涉及非 OpenAI 模型的网络安全事件中看到了此类行为的一个例子。
我们也看到了显著的进展——GPT‑6 Astra 是首个受益于我们长期推进的多项重要突破的模型，并且其对齐程度明显优于 GPT‑5.6 Sol。
我们目前还没有一套令人满意的泛化理论，而且至少在更强大的 AI 的帮助下之前，短期内似乎也不太可能建立这样一套理论。
OpenAI 在此方面的核心押注是思维链监控。
当我们发布 o1-preview 时，我们特意将产品设计为隐藏思维链，以长期保护其免受监督压力。
这源于多种因素的综合作用。
现代推理模型所运行的环境比 o1-preview 时代更为复杂；它们的推理过程越来越多地与同人类、其他 AI 的交流以及工具使用交织在一起。
AI 在对其自身推理过程进行推理和操控方面的能力正在变得更强。
我乐观地认为，我们能够开发出干预措施，提高模型思维链的可监控性，例如更深入地理解不同优化目标与模型所使用的各种测试时计算形式之间的相互作用。
与AI相关的风险不幸地只会从这里继续增长。
随着AI获得更强的自主性，滥用与自主失当行为之间的界限将变得模糊。
我们或许习惯于将AI视为工具，但一些智能体将追求它们自己的目标。
此外，还有来自AI可能催生的新技术所带来的风险，例如工程病原体。
我们将需要强大且对齐的AI用于防御；用于保障基础设施安全，用于实时抵御恶意智能体，并发明全新的防护措施。
这将是OpenAI部署工作的首要重点。
与此同时，即使考虑到预期中广泛AI进步所带来的不确定性以及构建防御系统的必要性，我们也绝不能让其成为鲁莽行事的借口。
如果AI进步持续下去，机器递归式自我改进（RSI）将处于未来科学发现的核心位置。
自动化AI研究是以算力扩展智能的一种更为激进的形式；当然，作为其中的一部分，AI也将改进计算基础设施本身。
与扩展（scaling）类似，我们将OpenAI的研究聚焦于RSI（递归自我改进），因为我们相信这是未来保持在AI研究前沿的唯一途径。
我们拥有的主要杠杆要么是引导这一进程，在AI发展的同时加强对齐与监控，并找到让人类保持参与的方式；要么是协调各方，在必要时放缓未来的发展，以便对这些措施建立信心。
我们在对齐与监控方面取得的具体进展，通常与整体AI进展紧密交织在一起。
典型的例子包括基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF），它对训练早期AI助手至关重要；以及前述的思维链监控，它得益于推理模型方面的进步而成为可能。
我们必须将日益自动化的研究过程聚焦于开发这类新的洞见、算法和理论，并针对能力更强的AI迭代构建安全论证。
AI 系统的规模化扩展必须受制于我们对安全性的信心。
我们需要将《预备框架》（Preparedness Framework）或《负责任扩展政策》（Responsible Scaling Policy）等承诺，演进为广泛强制要求的安全底线，以支撑持续开发。
自动化 AI 研究这一目标的核心挑战，不在于“如何抵达”——而在于以何种方式抵达，使人类始终参与持续改进的过程，并将未来掌握在人类自己手中。
正如我们近期与 Sam 一起概述的那样，OpenAI 将工作重点放在服务三大北极星目标上：
构建自动化 AI 研究员，与之共同迭代对齐问题，并寻找让人类继续留在自我改进循环中的方式，从而驾驭 AI 进步的下一阶段。
未来对齐的 AI 可以推动科学发展、开发新疗法，并带来广泛的物质富足。
友善而诚实的 AI 能够帮助人们应对生活中遇到的困难，切实提升他们的幸福感与成就感。
OpenAI 投入了巨大的努力来实现这些益处。
无论 AI 的长期前景多么美好，我们的大部分精力都应聚焦于未来几年。
我们需要找到方法，在一个大多数任务都可能由 AI 完成的世界里，维护人类的自主性，并确立作为人类的内在价值。
而且我相信，在未来的 AI 发展上进行国际协调，必须成为世界各国政府的首要优先事项。
